column3: Parents, father and mother together: 父 ("father") plus 母 ("mother"). It is a general, slightly formal word for both parents, used in sentences like 我的父母住在上海. In speech people often say 爸爸妈妈 instead.
column6: Wǒ de fùmǔ zhù zài Shànghǎi.
column7: My parents live in Shanghai.

column3: Father, the formal or written word. In speech you say 爸爸 and call him 爸 directly; 父亲 is what you use when writing about or describing someone's father: 我的父亲是医生. Its pair is 母亲.
column6: Wǒ de fùqin shì yīshēng.
column7: My father is a doctor.

column3: Mother, the formal and written counterpart of 妈妈. It suits writing, speeches and set phrases such as 母亲节 "Mother's Day". In speech you call her 妈 or 妈妈, and use 母亲 when describing or writing about someone's mother.
column6: Mǔqin měitiān dōu hěn zǎo qǐchuáng.
column7: My mother gets up very early every day.

column3: As a word on its own it is mostly "close, intimate" or "in person": 亲手 "with one's own hands", 亲眼 "with one's own eyes". It is the 亲 of 父亲, 母亲 and 亲人, where it means a blood relation.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ qīnshǒu zuò de dàngāo.
column7: This is a cake I made with my own hands.

column3: Close relatives, family, the people you are bound to by blood or marriage: 亲 ("close, related") plus 人. It is a warm word, used when speaking of missing family or sending greetings: 想念亲人.
column4: 过年的时候，亲人都回家了。
column5: 過年的時候，親人都回家了。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, qīnrén dōu huí jiā le.
column7: At New Year, all the family come home.

column3: Children, meaning sons and daughters as a group, from the parents' point of view: 子 ("son") plus 女 ("daughter"). It is written and formal, used when talking about raising or supporting them: 教育子女. In everyday speech people say 孩子.
column6: Tā yǒu liǎng ge zǐnǚ.
column7: He has two children.

column3: Family members of a particular person, such as a patient's or a worker's, and often the ones to be notified or looked after. It is formal and goes with a specific person: 病人家属 "the patient's family". It is not the word for your own household in general; for that use 家人.
column6: Bìngrén de jiāshǔ zài wàimiàn děng.
column7: The patient's family is waiting outside.

column3: Man, male, a written word that is more formal than 男人. It often appears in news and in sports, as in 男子 versus 女子 in competitions: 男子一百米 "men's 100 meters". It is rarely used when chatting.
column4: 这个男子在公园里跑步。
column5: 這個男子在公園裡跑步。
column6: Zhège nánzǐ zài gōngyuán lǐ pǎobù.
column7: This man is running in the park.

column3: Woman, female, the written counterpart of 女人, and the pair of 男子. It is the usual word in sports and in news reports: 女子足球 "women's soccer". Used as a label rather than for talking about a woman you know.
column4: 她是一名女子足球运动员。
column5: 她是一名女子足球運動員。
column6: Tā shì yī míng nǚzǐ zúqiú yùndòngyuán.
column7: She is a women's soccer player.

column3: Girl, young woman, spoken and friendly, often for someone not yet married: 漂亮的姑娘. The 娘 is light, so say gūniang. In some regions 姑娘 can also mean a daughter, and its father's-sister meaning 姑 is a different thing.
column6: Nàge gūniang shì wǒ de tóngxué.
column7: That girl is my classmate.

column3: Old lady, an elderly woman, said politely: 老 ("old") plus 太太. The third 太 is light. Also a polite way for a younger person to refer to someone's mother or an elderly wife: 您家老太太. Use it for women, not men, whose counterpart is 老头儿.
column4: 老太太坐在门口晒太阳。
column5: 老太太坐在門口曬太陽。
column6: Lǎotàitai zuò zài ménkǒu shài tàiyáng.
column7: The old lady sits at the door sunning herself.

column3: Old man, spoken and a bit casual, with the northern 儿 ending: 老头儿 is read lǎotóur. It can be affectionate, but it is not very polite to call a stranger this. A wife may call her husband 我家老头儿 jokingly.
column4: 那个老头儿每天在这里下棋。
column5: 那個老頭兒每天在這裡下棋。
column6: Nàge lǎotóur měitiān zài zhèlǐ xià qí.
column7: That old man plays chess here every day.

column3: Someone you know, an acquaintance: 熟 ("familiar") plus 人. It is more than a stranger but not necessarily a close friend. The pair is 生人 "stranger". Often seen in 在这儿碰到熟人: you run into someone you know.
column4: 我在街上遇到了一个熟人。
column5: 我在街上遇到了一個熟人。
column6: Wǒ zài jiē shàng yùdào le yī ge shúrén.
column7: I ran into someone I know on the street.

column3: Age, about how old a person is, mostly an older person's: 年纪大 "old", 年纪小 "young". To ask politely about an old person's age, say 您多大年纪? For a child you would use 几岁 instead. Compare 年龄, which is more neutral.
column6: Tā niánjì dà le, zǒulù hěn màn.
column7: He is getting on in years and walks slowly.

column3: Humankind, humanity: 人 plus 类 ("kind, type"). It speaks of all people as a species, as in 人类的未来 "the future of humankind". It is a collective noun and takes no measure word. Typical of science, news and big topics.
column6: Dìqiú shì rénlèi de jiā.
column7: The Earth is humanity's home.

column3: Human life, life as a whole, a journey from birth to death: 人生 is the word in 人生很短 "life is short" and 人生的意义 "the meaning of life". It talks of life in general. For being alive day to day, use 生活.
column6: Rénshēng jiù xiàng yī cì lǚxíng.
column7: Life is like a trip.

column3: Crowd, a mass of people in one place: 人 plus 群 ("group"). It is used with words for moving and gathering: 人群里 "in the crowd", 挤进人群 "squeeze into the crowd", 人群散了 "the crowd dispersed". A specific group of people is 一群人.
column4: 广场上的人群越来越多。
column5: 廣場上的人群越來越多。
column6: Guǎngchǎng shàng de rénqún yuè lái yuè duō.
column7: The crowd in the square keeps growing.

column3: Ordinary people, the common folk, as opposed to officials or those in power. 百姓 means the "hundred surnames", all the people. It is a spoken word with warmth: 老百姓的生活 "the lives of ordinary folk". The third syllable is read xìng.
column4: 老百姓都希望过上好日子。
column5: 老百姓都希望過上好日子。
column6: Lǎobǎixìng dōu xīwàng guò shàng hǎo rìzi.
column7: Ordinary people all hope for a good life.

column3: The people, the citizens of a country, in the political sense. It names the state and the public: 中国人民, 人民币 "RMB, the people's money". It is more formal than 老百姓 and usually goes with national or official topics.
column6: Rénmín de shēnghuó yuè lái yuè hǎo.
column7: The people's lives are getting better and better.

column3: Citizen, a legal member of a country: 公 ("public") plus 民 ("people"). It sounds official: 中国公民 "a Chinese citizen", 公民权利 "civil rights". It is used in law, rules and news, not in chat.
column4: 每个公民都要遵守法律。
column5: 每個公民都要遵守法律。
column6: Měi ge gōngmín dōu yào zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
column7: Every citizen must obey the law.

column3: To get married: 结 ("tie") plus 婚 ("marriage"). It is a verb and its object, so extra things come between: 结了婚, 结过婚 "have been married", and 和…结婚 "marry someone": 我和他结婚了. You cannot say 结婚他.
column6: Tāmen dǎsuàn míngnián jiéhūn.
column7: They plan to get married next year.

column3: To divorce: 离 ("leave, separate") plus 婚. Like 结婚, a verb with its object inside, so 离了婚 "got divorced" and 和…离婚 "divorce someone": 她和他离婚了. The opposite of 结婚.
column6: Tāmen qùnián líhūn le.
column7: They got divorced last year.

column3: Chinese cabbage, the pale-leaved vegetable used in soups and stir-fries and in northern winter cooking. 白 ("white") plus 菜 ("vegetable"). Also called 大白菜. It is cheap and common, so the saying 白菜价 means "dirt cheap".
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī kē báicài.
column7: I want to buy a Chinese cabbage.

column3: Apple. 果 is "fruit", and the first syllable is píng. Say 一个苹果 for one, or 一斤苹果 by weight. It also names the company and the phone, 苹果手机.
column6: Wǒ měitiān chī yī ge píngguǒ.
column7: I eat an apple every day.

column3: Cola, a borrowed word with the sound ke-le and the characters for "can be happy", which suit a drink. Say 一瓶可乐 "a bottle of cola" or 一杯可乐 "a glass". As a plain word, 可乐 can also mean "funny", but cola is its main use.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng hē yī bēi kělè.
column7: I'd like a glass of cola.

column3: Milk tea, the sweet drink popular across Asia, in China usually with tapioca pearls: 珍珠奶茶 "bubble tea". 奶 ("milk") plus 茶 ("tea"). You order it by the cup: 一杯奶茶. It is not the same as a pot of tea with milk.
column6: Wǒmen qù mǎi bēi nǎichá ba.
column7: Let's go and buy a milk tea.

column3: Black tea, literally "red tea": the Chinese name goes by the color of the brewed liquid, not of the leaves. It is the tea the West calls black. Compare 绿茶 "green tea". 一杯红茶 is a cup of it.
column4: 我喜欢喝红茶，不喜欢绿茶。
column5: 我喜歡喝紅茶，不喜歡綠茶。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan hē hóngchá, bù xǐhuan lǜchá.
column7: I like black tea, not green tea.

column3: Green tea, the unfermented tea (龙井 is a famous kind). 绿 is read lǜ, which dictionaries and word lists sometimes type lv. A pair with 红茶 "black tea". In slang 绿茶 can also describe a woman seen as fake-innocent, but that is a different use.
column6: Zhè bēi lǜchá hěn xiāng.
column7: This cup of green tea smells good.

column3: Red wine: 红 ("red") plus 酒 ("alcohol"). The fuller word is 红葡萄酒; 红酒 is the everyday short form. Beware 白酒: that is Chinese grain spirit, not white wine, which is 白葡萄酒. Count it by the glass (一杯) or bottle (一瓶).
column4: 晚饭的时候，他喝了一杯红酒。
column5: 晚飯的時候，他喝了一杯紅酒。
column6: Wǎnfàn de shíhou, tā hē le yī bēi hóngjiǔ.
column7: At dinner he had a glass of red wine.

column3: Beer, a loanword: 啤 stands for the sound "pi" of "beer" and 酒 means "alcohol". Measure words are 瓶 for a bottle, 杯 for a glass and 罐 for a can: 一瓶啤酒. 喝啤酒 is "drink beer".
column6: Nǐ xiǎng hē píjiǔ háishi guǒzhī?
column7: Do you want beer or juice?

column3: Cold water, water that is not heated: 凉 ("cool") plus 水. Chinese people often prefer warm drinks, so 别喝凉水 "don't drink cold water" is common advice, and 喝凉水 can sound a little unhealthy to them. Also "unboiled water". Fine for cooling off: 用凉水洗脸 "wash your face in cold water".
column4: 天气热，他喝了一杯凉水。
column5: 天氣熱，他喝了一杯涼水。
column6: Tiānqì rè, tā hē le yī bēi liángshuǐ.
column7: It was hot, so he drank a glass of cold water.

column3: Sugar and "candy": 糖 covers both. 一块糖 is "a piece of candy", 白糖 is "white sugar", and 糖果 is "sweets". The left part 米 is a clue to food; the right part 唐 is a sound part and also the name of the Tang dynasty.
column6: Zhège kāfēi lǐ méiyǒu fàng táng.
column7: There is no sugar in this coffee.

column3: Fragrant, smelling good, and also "tasty, appetizing" for food: 很香 is said of cooking that smells good. It can describe flowers, soap and food alike. Used with a verb it also means "taste good": 吃得很香 "eat with relish".
column6: Zhè dào cài wén qǐlái hěn xiāng.
column7: This dish smells delicious.

column3: Delicious food, gourmet food: 美 ("beautiful, good") plus 食 ("food"). It is often used for the food of a place or in an invitation to try it: 品尝美食 "taste fine food", 美食街 "food street". A positive, slightly written word.
column6: Zhège chéngshì yǒu hěn duō měishí.
column7: This city has a lot of good food.

column3: Food products, the goods sold as food, such as packaged or processed things: 食品店 "food shop", 食品安全 "food safety". It is a label for the category and not for a meal, so you do not say 吃食品 for eating dinner.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn mài gè zhǒng shípǐn.
column7: This shop sells all kinds of food products.

column3: Nutrition, nourishment, a noun that is also a modifier: 有营养 "nutritious", 营养很丰富 "rich in nutrients", 营养不良 "malnourished". Typical of health and cooking advice: 要注意营养.
column6: Jīdàn hěn yǒu yíngyǎng.
column7: Eggs are very nutritious.

column3: Cigarette and "smoke": 抽烟 or 吸烟 is "to smoke (tobacco)", and 一包烟 is "a pack of cigarettes". It also means smoke from a fire or mist in compounds such as 烟花 "fireworks". The 火 on the left shows it is about fire and smoke.
column6: Qǐng bù yào zài zhèlǐ chōu yān.
column7: Please don't smoke here.

column3: A measure word for meals, scoldings and beatings: 一顿饭 "a meal", 吃了三顿 "ate three meals", 骂了他一顿 "gave him a scolding". It counts how many times something happens as a full event, not time.
column6: Wǒmen yīqǐ chī yī dùn fàn ba.
column7: Let's have a meal together.

column3: Room or "house", a spoken word, with the light second syllable: 这间屋子很大 "this room is big". 屋 alone is more written. As a room the measure word is 间: 一间屋子. It can also be the whole house in some usage.
column6: Zhè jiān wūzi yòu dà yòu liàng.
column7: This room is big and bright.

column3: Houses, buildings as a class of thing, a written word: 房 plus 屋. You find it in property and legal terms such as 房屋买卖 "house sale" and 房屋租赁. It is a group word and takes no 个: not 一个房屋 in everyday talk.
column6: Zhèxiē fángwū yǐjīng hěn jiù le.
column7: These houses are already very old.

column3: Landlord or "landlady", the person who owns the place you rent. 房 ("house") plus 东 ("owner, host"; the old sense of 东 is where the host stands). A tenant is 房客. You pay the 房租 to your 房东: 我的房东很好.
column6: Fángdōng míngtiān lái shōu fángzū.
column7: The landlord is coming tomorrow to collect the rent.

column3: Rent for a room or house: 房 ("house") plus 租 ("to rent"). Typical phrases are 交房租 or 付房租 "pay the rent" and 房租很贵 "the rent is high". The rent for other things, like a car, is 租金.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fángzū tài guì le.
column7: The rent here is too expensive.

column3: To move something, carry or shift it from one place to another, usually something heavy: 搬桌子 "move a table", 搬东西 "move things". For moving house, use 搬家. The 手 on the left shows it is done by hand.
column4: 请帮我把这张桌子搬到楼上。
column5: 請幫我把這張桌子搬到樓上。
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ zhè zhāng zhuōzi bān dào lóu shàng.
column7: Please help me move this table upstairs.

column3: To move house: 搬 ("move") plus 家 ("home"), a verb and its object. Extras come between them: 搬了家 "have moved", 搬过三次家 "moved three times". The new place follows with 到: 搬到北京. 他们搬家了 is the plain statement.
column6: Wǒmen xià ge yuè yào bānjiā.
column7: We are moving house next month.

column3: Furniture: 家 ("home") plus 具 ("tool, utensil"). A collective noun with no 个; the pieces are called 件, as in 一件家具, or counted by type (一张桌子). 买家具 and 家具店 are common phrases.
column4: 我们的新家还没有家具。
column5: 我們的新家還沒有家具。
column6: Wǒmen de xīn jiā hái méiyǒu jiājù.
column7: Our new home doesn't have any furniture yet.

column3: Sofa, a loanword from English "sofa". It is counted with 个 or 张: 一个沙发. 坐在沙发上 is the usual phrase.
column6: Tā zuò zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì.
column7: He sits on the sofa watching TV.

column3: Quilt, duvet: the bedding you cover yourself with. Counted with 条 or 床: 一条被子, 一床被子. 盖被子 is "cover oneself with the quilt", and 叠被子 is "fold the quilt". The 子 ending is light: bèizi.
column4: 天冷了，要盖厚一点的被子。
column5: 天冷了，要蓋厚一點的被子。
column6: Tiān lěng le, yào gài hòu yīdiǎn de bèizi.
column7: It has turned cold, so use a thicker quilt.

column3: Bookshelf: 书 ("book") plus 架 ("frame, rack"). The measure word is 个 or 排 for a row. 架 turns up in other words for things that hold items, such as 衣架 "clothes hanger". 放在书架上 "put on the bookshelf".
column6: Wǒ de shūjià shàng yǒu hěn duō shū.
column7: There are a lot of books on my bookshelf.

column3: Clothes hanger or "clothes rack": 衣 ("clothes") plus 架 ("frame"). Both the single hanger and a standing rack are 衣架. Count them with 个: 一个衣架. 挂在衣架上 "hang on a hanger" is the typical use.
column6: Qǐng bǎ wàitào guà zài yījià shàng.
column7: Please hang your coat on the hanger.

column3: Air conditioner, also "air conditioning": 开空调 "turn on the air conditioning", 关空调 "turn it off". It is short for 空气调节. The 调 here is read tiáo ("to adjust"), not diào. A very common word in a hot-summer country.
column6: Tài rè le, bǎ kōngtiáo dǎkāi ba.
column7: It's too hot, turn the air conditioning on.

column3: Bathroom, toilet, the room where you wash and use the toilet: 卫生 ("hygiene") plus 间 ("room"). The polite word for a toilet in a home or a hotel, along with 洗手间. Ask 卫生间在哪儿? to find it.
column6: Qǐngwèn, wèishēngjiān zài nǎr?
column7: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

column3: Room, used almost only in compounds, not alone: 教室 "classroom", 卧室 "bedroom", 办公室 "office", 浴室 "bathroom". It marks the room's purpose. The 宀 on top is the roof radical, shared by 家, 字 and other words about buildings.
column6: Wǒmen de jiàoshì zài sān lóu.
column7: Our classroom is on the third floor.

column3: Board, plank, flat piece: 黑板 "blackboard", 地板 "floor", 老板 "boss". The 木 on the left shows it was first made of wood. In 老板 "boss, shop owner" it is read bǎn and has nothing to do with wood in meaning.
column6: Lǎoshī zài hēibǎn shàng xiě zì.
column7: The teacher writes on the blackboard.

column3: To hang something up: 挂在墙上 "hang on the wall", 挂衣服 "hang clothes". With a phone it means "to hang up": 挂电话. The 扌 on the left shows an action of the hand.
column6: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yī zhāng dìtú.
column7: A map hangs on the wall.

column3: Knife, blade, a picture of a blade. Its measure word is 把: 一把刀. It is also a radical, written 刂 on the right side of characters about cutting, like 到 and 别, though in those it is not always the sense of cutting. 菜刀 is a kitchen knife.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè bǎ dāo ná gěi wǒ.
column7: Please pass me this knife.

column3: Shirt, blouse, the dress shirt or blouse with a collar: 件 is its measure word, so 一件衬衫. It is smart rather than casual, and is not the T-shirt, which is T恤. The 衤 on the left is the clothing radical, shared by 衬衣 and 裤子.
column6: Tā chuān zhe yī jiàn bái chènshān.
column7: He is wearing a white shirt.

column3: Shirt, a variant of 衬衫 with the same meaning and the same measure word 件. 衬衣 is a little more used in the north, 衬衫 elsewhere, but both are understood. 衣 means "clothes" and 衫 is a top; here they are interchangeable.
column6: Zhè jiàn chènyī shì xīn mǎi de.
column7: This shirt is newly bought.

column3: Upper garment, the clothing worn on the top half: 上 ("upper") plus 衣 ("clothes"). It is the generic word for jackets, shirts and tops, in contrast to 裤子 "trousers" for the bottom half. Often in lists such as 上衣和裤子.
column6: Tā jīntiān chuān hóngsè de shàngyī.
column7: She is wearing a red top today.

column3: Shorts: 短 ("short") plus 裤 ("trousers"). Its measure word is 条: 一条短裤. The opposite is 长裤 "long trousers". Both 裤 and 短 are common elsewhere: 短 is in 短信 "text message", and 裤 appears in 裤子.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan chuān duǎnkù.
column7: In summer I like to wear shorts.

column3: Trousers, pants: 一条裤子 is the usual count. 子 gives it a light second syllable: kùzi. The word is singular in Chinese, unlike English "pants". The 衤 on the left marks clothing, and 库 on the right gives the sound.
column6: Zhè tiáo kùzi yǒudiǎnr cháng.
column7: These trousers are a bit long.

column3: Skirt or "dress": 条 is the measure word for a skirt, 一条裙子, and 件 for a one-piece dress, which is also often called 裙子 or 连衣裙. The 衤 on the left marks clothing, like 裤子 and 衬衫. 穿裙子 is "wear a skirt".
column4: 她今天穿了一条红裙子。
column5: 她今天穿了一條紅裙子。
column6: Tā jīntiān chuān le yī tiáo hóng qúnzi.
column7: Today she is wearing a red skirt.

column3: Clothing, apparel as a category, more formal than 衣服: 服装店 "clothing store", 服装设计 "fashion design". It speaks of garments in general and has no measure word, so 一件衣服 but not 一件服装. Think of it as the trade word.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn mài nánnǚ fúzhuāng.
column7: This shop sells men's and women's clothing.

column3: Skin, leather, peel: it covers the skin of a person (皮肤), leather (皮鞋 "leather shoes") and the peel of fruit (苹果皮). Also "cover, outer layer". As an adjective it means "naughty" about a child: 这孩子很皮.
column6: Zhè shuāng píxié shì xīn mǎi de.
column7: This pair of leather shoes is newly bought.

column3: Leather bag, handbag: 皮 ("leather") plus 包 ("bag"). It also covers a wallet-size bag. Count it with 个: 一个皮包. A more general word for a bag is 包. It is a little old-fashioned compared with 手提包 for a handbag.
column4: 他的皮包里有很多文件。
column5: 他的皮包裡有很多文件。
column6: Tā de píbāo lǐ yǒu hěn duō wénjiàn.
column7: His leather bag holds many documents.

column3: Cloth, fabric: 一块布 "a piece of cloth", 布鞋 "cloth shoes", 布娃娃 "rag doll". It is also a verb in written words such as 发布 "to release" and 公布 "to announce", where it means "spread out, declare". The 巾 at the bottom shows cloth.
column4: 妈妈用这块布做了一件衣服。
column5: 媽媽用這塊布做了一件衣服。
column6: Māma yòng zhè kuài bù zuò le yī jiàn yīfu.
column7: Mom made a piece of clothing out of this cloth.

column3: Luggage, baggage: 一件行李 or 一个行李箱 "a suitcase". It is a collective noun, so you do not say 很多行李们. Used with 带 "bring", 拿 "carry" and 检查 "check": 行李很重. At an airport, you 托运行李 "check in luggage". The 李 is light: xíngli.
column6: Wǒ de xíngli hěn zhòng.
column7: My luggage is very heavy.

column3: Brand and also "sign, plate". As a brand: 什么牌子的手机? "What brand of phone?" As a board: 门口挂着一块牌子 "a sign hangs at the door". 牌 alone is "card, tile" (打牌 "play cards"), and 牌子 is the more spoken form.
column6: Zhè shì shénme páizi de yīfu?
column7: What brand of clothes is this?

column3: Toy: 玩 ("to play") plus 具 ("tool"), a thing for playing. The measure word is 个 or 件. 买玩具 "buy toys", 玩具店 "toy shop", 玩具车 "toy car". 具 is also the second part of 家具 "furniture".
column4: 孩子们都喜欢这个玩具。
column5: 孩子們都喜歡這個玩具。
column6: Háizimen dōu xǐhuan zhège wánjù.
column7: The children all like this toy.

column3: Blood, read xuè in compounds like 血液 and 流血 "to bleed", though in speech many people say xiě: 一滴血 "a drop of blood". It is the same character either way.
column6: Tā de shǒu liú xuè le.
column7: His hand is bleeding.

column3: Heart in the body, and also "mind, feelings": 我的心跳得很快 "my heart is beating fast"; 开心 "happy", 小心 "careful", 担心 "worry". Many words for feelings use it. As a radical it appears as 心 at the bottom or 忄 on the left.
column4: 看到这个消息，我很开心。
column5: 看到這個消息，我很開心。
column6: Kàndào zhège xiāoxi, wǒ hěn kāixīn.
column7: I was happy to see this news.

column3: Finger: 手 ("hand") plus 指 ("to point"). The fingers have names: 大拇指 "thumb", 食指 "index finger". Count them with 个 or 根: 十个手指. Do not mix with 指 as a verb "to point at".
column6: Tā de shǒuzhǐ bèi mén jiā dào le.
column7: His finger got caught in the door.

column3: Brains, head, mind, in the sense of the ability to think: 他很有头脑 "he has a good head on him", 头脑清楚 "clear-headed". It praises someone's practical sense, rather than being the anatomical brain, which is 大脑.
column6: Zhège háizi tóunǎo hěn cōngmíng.
column7: This child has a clever mind.

column3: To injure, to hurt, and as a noun "injury, wound": 他的腿受伤了, 伤口 "wound". It also hurts feelings: 伤心 "heartbroken". 受伤 is the more common way to say that someone was hurt.
column6: Tā de shǒu shàng yǒu yī dào shāng.
column7: There is a wound on his hand.

column3: To be injured, to get hurt: 受 ("to receive") plus 伤 ("injury"), a verb with its object. Use 受了伤 or 受过伤: 他在比赛中受伤了. The injured body part is named with 腿受伤了 "the leg is hurt". The severity can be added: 受了重伤 "badly injured".
column6: Tā tī zúqiú shí shòushāng le.
column7: He got hurt while playing soccer.

column3: Sleepy: 我很困 is the everyday way to say "I am sleepy". It is spoken. A second meaning, "stuck, trapped, in difficulty", appears in 困难 "difficulty" and 被困 "trapped".
column4: 我昨天没睡好，今天很困。
column5: 我昨天沒睡好，今天很困。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān méi shuì hǎo, jīntiān hěn kùn.
column7: I didn't sleep well last night and am sleepy today.

column3: To save, to rescue: 救人 "save a person", 救命 "save a life", and the cry 救命! "Help!". It also means help someone out of trouble: 救了我一次 "saved me once".
column6: Nàge rén jiù le wǒ de mìng.
column7: That person saved my life.

column3: To die and "dead": 他死了 "he has died". As an intensifier after an adjective it means "extremely", in a spoken way: 累死了 "dead tired", 热死了 "boiling hot". Used for a person it can be blunt; 去世 is the polite word.
column6: Zǒu le yī tiān, wǒ lèisǐ le.
column7: After walking all day, I am dead tired.

column3: To pass away, to die, the polite and respectful way to talk about a person's death: 他的爷爷去年去世了. 去 ("go") plus 世 ("world"), so he "left the world". Use it for people, not animals, and not for 死 in rude sense.
column6: Tā de nǎinai qùnián qùshì le.
column7: Her grandmother passed away last year.

column3: Life as a living thing, with a stress on how precious it is: 生命很宝贵 "life is precious", 保护生命 "protect life". It is the life of a being, where 人生 is the course of a person's life and 生活 is daily living.
column4: 每个人的生命都很宝贵。
column5: 每個人的生命都很寶貴。
column6: Měi ge rén de shēngmìng dōu hěn bǎoguì.
column7: Every person's life is precious.

column3: As a verb "to live, to be alive": 活了一百岁 "lived to be a hundred". As an adjective "alive, lively", the opposite of 死. Also "work" in 活儿. It is the 活 in 生活 "life" and 活动 "activity". The 氵 on the left is "water", a sign of the life-giving thing.
column6: Zhè tiáo yú hái huó zhe.
column7: This fish is still alive.

column3: To get a haircut: 理 ("tidy") plus 发 ("hair"), a verb with its object, so 理了发 "had a haircut" and 去理发 "go for a haircut". Here 发 is read fà, not fā. A shop is 理发店.
column6: Wǒ míngtiān qù lǐfà.
column7: I am going for a haircut tomorrow.

column3: To shake hands: 握 ("hold, grip") plus 手 ("hand"), a verb with its object, so you insert words between: 握了握手, 和他握手 "shake hands with him". The greeting is often done on meeting: 见面时握手.
column4: 见面时，他们热情地握手。
column5: 見面時，他們熱情地握手。
column6: Jiànmiàn shí, tāmen rèqíng de wòshǒu.
column7: When they met, they shook hands warmly.

column3: Hygiene, sanitation, and as an adjective "clean, hygienic": 讲卫生 "pay attention to hygiene", 个人卫生 "personal hygiene", 不卫生 "unhygienic". It also names public health work: 卫生局. Also the 卫生 of 卫生间 "bathroom".
column6: Fàn qián yào xǐ shǒu, jiǎngjiu wèishēng.
column7: Wash your hands before meals and take care of hygiene.

column3: To survive, to exist: 生 ("live") plus 存 ("remain, keep"). It is about staying alive in hard conditions: 生存条件 "conditions for survival", 生存下去 "survive". It is more written and serious than 活.
column6: Dòngwù xūyào shuǐ cái néng shēngcún.
column7: Animals need water to survive.

column3: To grow, of plants and living things growing in a place: 生长在南方 "grows in the south". The 长 here is read zhǎng. It is the biological growth word, where 成长 is a person's growing up.
column6: Zhè zhǒng huā shēngzhǎng zài shān shàng.
column7: This kind of flower grows in the mountains.

column3: To grow up, to mature: 成 ("become") plus 长 ("grow", read zhǎng). It follows a person or a thing through development: 孩子健康成长 "children grow up healthy". Differs from 生长, which is plain biological growth, while 成长 stresses maturing.
column4: 孩子们在爱里快乐地成长。
column5: 孩子們在愛裡快樂地成長。
column6: Háizimen zài ài lǐ kuàilè de chéngzhǎng.
column7: The children grow up happily in love.

column3: To receive, to suffer, to be subjected to: 受欢迎 "be welcomed, popular", 受伤 "get hurt", 受到帮助 "receive help". It makes the passive sense for things happening to you. In 受不了 it means "can't stand".
column4: 这本书很受孩子们的欢迎。
column5: 這本書很受孩子們的歡迎。
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn shòu háizimen de huānyíng.
column7: This book is very popular with children.

column3: Sheep or "goat": the same word covers both. 一只羊 is the count. Meat is 羊肉 "mutton, lamb". It is one of the twelve zodiac animals. As a part 羊 appears in 美, 洋 and 样.
column6: Shān shàng yǒu hěn duō yáng.
column7: There are lots of sheep on the mountain.

column3: Horse: 一匹马 is "a horse", with 匹 as the measure word. 骑马 is "ride a horse". In 马上 it means "at once" (literally "on horseback").
column6: Tā qí mǎ qù le shān lǐ.
column7: He went into the mountains on horseback.

column3: Dragon. The Chinese dragon is a lucky, powerful creature, unlike the fierce dragon of Western stories. It is one of the twelve zodiac animals. 龙年 is "year of the dragon". 恐龙 is "dinosaur" (literally "terrible dragon").
column4: 龙是中国文化里的重要动物。
column5: 龍是中國文化裡的重要動物。
column6: Lóng shì Zhōngguó wénhuà lǐ de zhòngyào dòngwù.
column7: The dragon is an important animal in Chinese culture.

column3: Fire: 着火了 "caught fire", 火车 "train" (literally "fire vehicle"), 火山 "volcano". As a part it is the radical at the bottom of characters as 灬 (热, 点), and 火 on the left in 灯 and 烧. Also means "angry" in 发火 "lose one's temper".
column6: Xiǎoxīn, bié ràng huǒ shāo dào shǒu.
column7: Careful, don't let the fire burn your hand.

column3: Earth, soil, ground: 一块土 "a lump of soil", 土地 "land". As an adjective it can also mean "rustic, unfashionable": 他穿得很土. 土 is also a radical in 地, 城 and 块.
column4: 花需要好的土才能长大。
column5: 花需要好的土才能長大。
column6: Huā xūyào hǎo de tǔ cái néng zhǎng dà.
column7: Flowers need good soil to grow.

column3: Stone, rock: 一块石头 "a stone". The 头 is a light suffix: shítou, as in 木头 and 石头. 石 alone is more written (石油 "oil" ,石桥 "stone bridge"). It is the ordinary word for a rock lying on the ground.
column6: Hé biān yǒu hěn duō dà shítou.
column7: There are many big stones by the river.

column3: Wood, timber: 一块木头 "a piece of wood", as the stuff things are made of. 木 alone is the written, general word. 木头 ends with a light 头: mùtou. It also means "blockhead" as a casual insult, in 木头人. 木头桌子 is a wooden table.
column6: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì mùtou zuò de.
column7: This table is made of wood.

column3: Sand, the loose grains: 一粒沙子 "a grain of sand", 沙子进眼睛了 "sand got in my eye". 沙 alone is used in names such as 沙漠 "desert" and 沙滩 "sandy beach". 沙 is 氵 (water) with 少, small grains: sand on a shore.
column6: Wǒ de xié lǐ jìn le shāzi.
column7: Sand got into my shoe.

column3: Iron: 铁门 "iron gate", 铁路 "railway" (iron road), 地铁 "subway". A metal. Used for hard things too: 铁了心 "firmly decided". The 钅 on the left is the metal radical, shared by 钱 and 银.
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo shì yòng tiě zuò de.
column7: This bridge is made of iron.

column3: Petroleum, oil: 石 ("stone") plus 油 ("oil"), as in "rock oil". It is crude oil, not cooking oil, which is 食用油. Common in news about energy: 石油价格 "oil prices", 石油公司 "oil company". Not used for gasoline, which is 汽油.
column6: Zhège guójiā yǒu hěn duō shíyóu.
column7: This country has a lot of oil.

column3: Sky: 天 ("sky") plus 空 ("empty, air"). It is the sky as seen, in descriptions: 蓝蓝的天空 "the blue sky", 天空中有云 "there are clouds in the sky". It is the word in prose, while 天 alone can mean sky in speech.
column6: Tiānkōng zhōng yǒu yī zhī niǎo zài fēi.
column7: A bird is flying in the sky.

column3: Sunlight, sunshine: 阳 ("sun") plus 光 ("light"). It is what shines in: 阳光很好 "the sunshine is lovely", 晒太阳 uses 太阳. 阳光 can also describe a person as "sunny, cheerful": 阳光男孩.
column6: Yángguāng cóng chuānghu zhào jìnlái.
column7: Sunlight shines in through the window.

column3: Climate: long-term weather conditions of a place, not the day's weather, which is 天气. 气候 is used for regions and seasons: 气候变化 "climate change", 这里的气候很好 "the climate here is good". 候 is the "season, time".
column6: Zhèlǐ de qìhòu hěn shūfu.
column7: The climate here is very comfortable.

column3: Warm, pleasantly warm: 暖和 describes the weather, a room or a thing like a coat. It can also be a verb, "warm up": 暖和一下. Light 和: nuǎnhuo. Where 温暖 is written and warm in feeling too, 暖和 is the everyday word.
column6: Wūzi lǐ hěn nuǎnhuo.
column7: It is nice and warm in the room.

column3: Warm in a gentler, more literary tone: 温暖的阳光 "warm sunshine", 温暖的家 "a warm home". It also describes warm feelings (温暖的话). It can be a verb "warm someone's heart": 温暖了我的心. 暖和 is the plainer word for temperature.
column4: 家人的关心让我感到温暖。
column5: 家人的關心讓我感到溫暖。
column6: Jiārén de guānxīn ràng wǒ gǎndào wēnnuǎn.
column7: My family's care makes me feel warm.

column3: Seed: 种 ("kind, seed") plus 子. Here 种 is read zhǒng, "seed", where as a verb "to plant" it is zhòng. 撒种子 or 种下种子 "plant seeds". Also used figuratively: 在心里种下一颗种子. Count with 颗 or 粒.
column4: 我在花盆里种了一颗种子。
column5: 我在花盆裡種了一顆種子。
column6: Wǒ zài huāpén lǐ zhòng le yī kē zhǒngzi.
column7: I planted a seed in the flowerpot.

column3: Light: 阳光 "sunlight", 月光 "moonlight", 灯光 "lamplight". As an adjective, "bare, smooth, used up" in 光了 "all gone", and as an adverb "only": 光说不做 "all talk, no action".
column6: Fángjiān lǐ yīdiǎn guāng yě méiyǒu.
column7: There is no light at all in the room.

column3: Bright, light, and figuratively "hopeful": 光 ("light") plus 明 ("bright"). Literally it is full of light: 光明的房间; as a hope it points to a good future: 光明的前途 "a bright future". Written and often political or poetic.
column4: 他对未来充满了光明的希望。
column5: 他對未來充滿了光明的希望。
column6: Tā duì wèilái chōngmǎn le guāngmíng de xīwàng.
column7: He is full of bright hopes for the future.

column3: City, town or the "wall" of one: the old Chinese city was inside a wall. It is the 城 of 城市, 长城 "Great Wall" and 城门 "city gate". As a suffix, 北京城 "Beijing city". The 土 on the left shows the walls were built of earth.
column6: Zhè zuò gǔchéng hěn yǒumíng.
column7: This old city is very famous.

column3: City: 城 ("town wall") plus 市 ("market"). The general word for any urban area, big or small: 大城市 "big city", 城市生活 "city life". It contrasts with 农村 "countryside". The measure word is 个 or 座.
column4: 上海是一个很大的城市。
column5: 上海是一個很大的城市。
column6: Shànghǎi shì yī ge hěn dà de chéngshì.
column7: Shanghai is a very big city.

column3: The Great Wall: 长 ("long") plus 城 ("wall"). It is a proper name, so it is capitalized in pinyin. The 长 is read cháng here. 万里长城 "the ten-thousand-li Great Wall" is a set phrase. 爬长城 "climb the Great Wall", 不到长城非好汉 is a famous saying.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù pá Chángchéng.
column7: We are going to climb the Great Wall this weekend.

column3: Capital city, the seat of government: 首 ("head, first") plus 都 ("capital"). Here 都 is read dū, not dōu. 中国的首都是北京 "the capital of China is Beijing". Often asked as 哪里是首都? Not an ordinary big city, so it differs from 大城市.
column6: Běijīng shì Zhōngguó de shǒudū.
column7: Beijing is the capital of China.

column3: Village: 村子 is the spoken form, and 村 appears in names and compounds such as 农村 "countryside" and 村民 "villager". The 木 on the left is "tree", and 寸 on the right gives the sound cūn. 小村 is "small village".
column4: 我的奶奶住在一个小村里。
column5: 我的奶奶住在一個小村裡。
column6: Wǒ de nǎinai zhù zài yī ge xiǎo cūn lǐ.
column7: My grandmother lives in a small village.

column3: Countryside, rural area: 农 ("farming") plus 村 ("village"). The opposite of 城市. 农村生活 "country life", 农村户口 "rural household registration". Used when talking about areas where agriculture is the main activity, not for nature or scenery.
column6: Tā zài nóngcūn zhǎng dà.
column7: He grew up in the countryside.

column3: Farmer, peasant: 农 ("farming") plus 民 ("people"). The word for someone who works the land: 农民伯伯 is a respectful way to say "farmer" to children. It is a neutral occupation word in modern Chinese.
column6: Nóngmínmen zhèngzài tián lǐ gōngzuò.
column7: The farmers are working in the fields.

column3: Agriculture, farming as a field or industry: 农 ("farming") plus 业 ("industry"). 农业国 "an agricultural country", 发展农业 "develop agriculture". A written, abstract word; for the person who farms use 农民.
column4: 农业对这个国家很重要。
column5: 農業對這個國家很重要。
column6: Nóngyè duì zhège guójiā hěn zhòngyào.
column7: Agriculture is very important to this country.

column3: Region, area: a larger part of a country or the world: 北方地区 "the northern region", 亚洲地区 "Asia". It is used in news and formal talk. Not a point on the map but an extended zone, unlike 地方 "place".
column6: Zhège dìqū de dōngtiān hěn lěng.
column7: The winters in this region are cold.

column3: District, area: a part of a city or a zone with a job: 市区 "downtown", 小区 "residential compound", 北京的朝阳区 "Chaoyang District". It is also "zone" in 开发区 and 停车区.
column4: 我住在城东的一个小区里。
column5: 我住在城東的一個小區裡。
column6: Wǒ zhù zài chéng dōng de yī ge xiǎoqū lǐ.
column7: I live in a residential compound in the east of the city.

column3: Local, in that place: 当 ("at") plus 地 ("place"). It comes before a noun, with or without 的: 当地人 "locals", 当地的美食 "local food", 当地时间 "local time". It points to the place being talked about, where 本地 is "this locality".
column4: 我们去尝尝当地的美食吧。
column5: 我們去嚐嚐當地的美食吧。
column6: Wǒmen qù chángchang dāngdì de měishí ba.
column7: Let's try the local food.

column3: Everywhere, all over, various places: 各 ("each, every") plus 地 ("place"). It names places within a larger area: 全国各地 "all over the country", 世界各地 "all over the world". Usually it stands before a noun or as an adverbial: 来自各地的游客.
column4: 来自世界各地的朋友都来了。
column5: 來自世界各地的朋友都來了。
column6: Láizì shìjiè gèdì de péngyou dōu lái le.
column7: Friends from all over the world have come.

column3: Domestic, inside the country: 国 ("country") plus 内 ("inside"). It contrasts with 国外 or 海外: 国内航班 "domestic flight", 国内新闻 "national news". Often used by people abroad to mean "back home" in China.
column4: 我下个月要坐国内航班去成都。
column5: 我下個月要坐國內航班去成都。
column6: Wǒ xià ge yuè yào zuò guónèi hángbān qù Chéngdū.
column7: Next month I'll take a domestic flight to Chengdu.

column3: Embassy: 大使 ("ambassador") plus 馆 ("building for an institution"). The 馆 is also in 图书馆 "library" and 饭馆 "restaurant". 中国大使馆 "the Chinese embassy". Lose your passport and you go to the 大使馆.
column4: 我的护照丢了，要去大使馆。
column5: 我的護照丟了，要去大使館。
column6: Wǒ de hùzhào diū le, yào qù dàshǐguǎn.
column7: I lost my passport, so I have to go to the embassy.

column3: Customs, the border inspection of goods and people: 海 ("sea") plus 关 ("pass, gate"). It was first at ports. 过海关 "go through customs", 海关检查 "customs inspection". 申报 is the declaring of goods at it.
column4: 过海关时，他们要检查行李。
column5: 過海關時，他們要檢查行李。
column6: Guò hǎiguān shí, tāmen yào jiǎnchá xíngli.
column7: At customs they have to check the luggage.

column3: Folk, among the people: 民 ("people") plus 间 ("among"). It describes things that belong to ordinary people rather than the state: 民间故事 "folk tales", 民间艺术 "folk art", 民间组织 "non-governmental organization". A noun before a noun.
column4: 这是一个有名的民间故事。
column5: 這是一個有名的民間故事。
column6: Zhè shì yī ge yǒumíng de mínjiān gùshi.
column7: This is a well-known folk tale.

column3: Ethnic Chinese, people of Chinese descent, wherever they live, and whatever their passport: 海外华人 "overseas Chinese", 华人社区 "Chinese community". Differs from 中国人, which usually means a citizen of China. 华 is a literary name for China. Proper noun in the list, so capitalized in pinyin.
column4: 这个城市里有很多华人。
column5: 這個城市裡有很多華人。
column6: Zhège chéngshì lǐ yǒu hěn duō Huárén.
column7: There are many ethnic Chinese in this city.

column3: Ethnic group, nation: 民 ("people") plus 族 ("clan, group"). China officially recognizes 56 民族: 汉族 and 55 minority groups, e.g. 少数民族 "ethnic minority". 民族 can also be a whole nation with its culture: 民族文化 "national culture".
column6: Zhōngguó yǒu wǔshíliù ge mínzú.
column7: China has fifty-six ethnic groups.

column3: The Chinese nation, the Chinese people as a whole, including all 56 民族. A grand, official term seen in speeches, news and history: 中华民族的历史 "the history of the Chinese nation". 中华 is a literary name for China. The whole term is a proper name.
column4: 中华民族有五千年的历史。
column5: 中華民族有五千年的歷史。
column6: Zhōnghuámínzú yǒu wǔqiān nián de lìshǐ.
column7: The Chinese nation has a history of five thousand years.

column3: National Day: the Chinese national day on 1 October (国庆节), when there is a week of holiday. 国 ("nation") plus 庆 ("celebrate"). Said as 国庆节 for the day itself, or just 国庆 as in 国庆假期 "National Day holiday". Taiwan's national day is 10 October, called 国庆日 or 双十节; there 国庆 also goes before other words, as in 国庆烟火 "National Day fireworks".
column6: Guóqìngjié wǒmen fàng qī tiān jià.
column7: We get seven days off for National Day.

column3: Occasion, situation, setting: the kind of social situation you are in, with the manners that go with it: 正式场合 "formal occasion", 公共场合 "public place", 在这种场合 "on an occasion like this". Often followed by advice about how to behave.
column4: 在正式场合，要穿得整齐一点。
column5: 在正式場合，要穿得整齊一點。
column6: Zài zhèngshì chǎnghé, yào chuān de zhěngqí yīdiǎn.
column7: On formal occasions, you should dress more neatly.

column3: Place, venue, a space used for some purpose: 公共场所 "public place", 娱乐场所 "entertainment venue", 工作场所 "workplace". It is a written, rule-like word: 公共场所禁止吸烟. 所 here is "a place".
column4: 公共场所不能大声说话。
column5: 公共場所不能大聲說話。
column6: Gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ bù néng dàshēng shuōhuà.
column7: You can't talk loudly in public places.

column3: Hometown, native place: 家 ("home") plus 乡 ("village, countryside"). The place you grew up or your family comes from: 我的家乡在四川. It is warm and often tied to feelings of missing: 想念家乡.
column4: 我的家乡在一个小城市。
column5: 我的家鄉在一個小城市。
column6: Wǒ de jiāxiāng zài yī ge xiǎo chéngshì.
column7: My hometown is in a small city.

column3: Native place, homeland, the literary cousin of 家乡, with the old 故 ("former, old"). It sounds poetic and a bit nostalgic, used in songs and prose: 思念故乡, 回到故乡. For ordinary speech 家乡 is the more natural pick.
column4: 离开故乡二十年了，他很想回去看看。
column5: 離開故鄉二十年了，他很想回去看看。
column6: Líkāi gùxiāng èrshí nián le, tā hěn xiǎng huíqù kànkan.
column7: He left his hometown twenty years ago and longs to go back.

column3: Bridge: 一座桥, with 座 as the measure word for a bridge. 过桥 is "cross the bridge", 大桥 is a large bridge and often a proper name, as in 长江大桥. The 木 on the left shows the first bridges were wooden.
column6: Hé shàng yǒu yī zuò xīn qiáo.
column7: There is a new bridge over the river.

column3: Railway: 铁 ("iron") plus 路 ("road"). It names the railway system or track: 铁路运输 "rail transport", 一条铁路 "a railway line". A train station is 火车站. 铁路 is the line itself, where 火车 is the vehicle.
column4: 这条铁路连接两个城市。
column5: 這條鐵路連接兩個城市。
column6: Zhè tiáo tiělù liánjiē liǎng ge chéngshì.
column7: This railway links two cities.

column3: High speed, fast: 高 ("high") plus 速 ("speed"). In 高速铁路 "high-speed rail" or 高速发展 "develop rapidly" it works as a modifier. In everyday speech 高速 also stands for 高速公路 "expressway": 上高速 "get on the expressway".
column4: 我们坐高速列车去北京。
column5: 我們坐高速列車去北京。
column6: Wǒmen zuò gāosù lièchē qù Běijīng.
column7: We are going to Beijing on a high-speed train.

column3: Expressway, freeway: 高速 ("high speed") plus 公路 ("highway"). In speech people say 高速 for short. Usually has tolls in China: 高速收费. 在高速公路上开车 is "drive on the expressway".
column6: Gāosùgōnglù shàng de chē hěn duō.
column7: There are many cars on the expressway.

column3: Route, itinerary: 路 ("road") plus 线 ("line"). The way you go from one place to another: 旅行路线 "travel route", 公交路线 "bus route", 路线图 "route map". Also "line" in a political sense: 政治路线. For a trip, plan the 路线.
column4: 我们看一下去那里的路线。
column5: 我們看一下去那裡的路線。
column6: Wǒmen kàn yīxià qù nàlǐ de lùxiàn.
column7: Let's look at the route to get there.

column3: Hotel, inn: 旅 ("travel") plus 馆 ("lodge"). A small, simple place to stay, cheaper than a 酒店 or 宾馆. 住旅馆 "stay at an inn". The 馆 is also in 图书馆 and 大使馆.
column4: 我们在车站旁边找了一家旅馆。
column5: 我們在車站旁邊找了一家旅館。
column6: Wǒmen zài chēzhàn pángbiān zhǎo le yī jiā lǚguǎn.
column7: We found a hotel next to the station.

column3: Travel agency: 旅行 ("travel") plus 社 ("agency, society"). 社 is also in 报社 "newspaper office" and 社会 "society". 通过旅行社订票 "book tickets through a travel agency", 跟旅行社出国 "go abroad with a travel agency". Counted with 家.
column6: Tā zài lǚxíngshè gōngzuò.
column7: He works at a travel agency.

column3: To fly, flight, a written word for something moving through the air: 飞行员 "pilot", 飞行时间 "flight time". It names the act of flying, like an airplane's flight. For catching a flight use 飞机, 航班. 鸟在飞行 "a bird is flying".
column6: Zhè cì fēixíng yào shí ge xiǎoshí.
column7: This flight takes ten hours.

column3: To go to, to head for, a formal word used for a destination: 前往北京 "go to Beijing". It is the written version of 去 and is found in notices and announcements: 请前往三号门. 前往 does not take 了 as easily as 去.
column6: Qǐng qiánwǎng sān hào dēngjīkǒu.
column7: Please proceed to boarding gate number three.

column3: To arrive, to reach: 到 ("arrive") plus 达 ("reach"). It is more formal than 到 and used about a trip's destination or a time: 到达北京 "arrive in Beijing", 到达时间 "arrival time". Airports and train stations use it. It follows the place straight.
column4: 飞机会在三点到达上海。
column5: 飛機會在三點到達上海。
column6: Fēijī huì zài sān diǎn dàodá Shànghǎi.
column7: The plane will arrive in Shanghai at three.

column3: To hurry to catch, "to rush": 赶火车 "catch a train", 赶时间 "be short of time". It also means "to drive away" (赶走 "chase away"). 赶上 is "catch up with, make it in time".
column6: Kuài diǎnr, wǒmen yào gǎn huǒchē.
column7: Hurry up, we have a train to catch.

column3: To hurry to (a place) and arrive: 赶 ("rush") plus 到 ("arrive"). The result is that you got there, often in time or just in time: 赶到车站 "rush to the station", 他赶到时, 会议已经开始了. A result compound, so 赶不到 means "can't make it".
column4: 他赶到机场的时候，飞机已经起飞了。
column5: 他趕到機場的時候，飛機已經起飛了。
column6: Tā gǎndào jīchǎng de shíhou, fēijī yǐjīng qǐfēi le.
column7: When he rushed to the airport, the plane had already taken off.

column3: To welcome, to greet, of a person arriving or an event coming: 迎接客人 "welcome guests", 迎接新年 "welcome the new year". 迎 means "go to meet" and 接 "receive". It is more formal than 接, which is "pick up".
column6: Wǒmen qù jīchǎng yíngjiē péngyou.
column7: We are going to the airport to meet our friend.

column3: To receive, to host guests officially: 接待客人 "receive guests", 接待处 "reception desk". It suits an organization looking after visitors. Where 迎接 is the moment of greeting, 接待 is the whole care of guests. 接待 is a verb and not "hospitality" as a noun.
column4: 公司派他接待外国客人。
column5: 公司派他接待外國客人。
column6: Gōngsī pài tā jiēdài wàiguó kèrén.
column7: The company sent him to receive foreign guests.

column3: To visit officially, or "to interview": 访问中国 "visit China" is for a head of state or delegation, and 访问了一位老师 "interviewed a teacher" in the news. In computing it is "access" (访问网站). Not used for a friend's visit, which is 拜访 or 看.
column6: Zǒnglǐ míngtiān jiāng fǎngwèn Fǎguó.
column7: The premier will visit France tomorrow.

column3: To be a guest, to visit someone's home: 做 ("be") plus 客 ("guest"), a verb and object. 去朋友家做客 "go visit a friend's house as a guest". 作客 is a variant. The host says 欢迎来我家做客. It can come between: 做过客.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ qù péngyou jiā zuòkè.
column7: At the weekend I am going to a friend's house as a guest.

column3: To advance, to go forward: 前 ("forward") plus 进 ("advance"). It is both physical (军队前进 "the army advances") and figurative (在学习上不断前进 "keep making progress"). The opposite is 后退.
column6: Dàjiā yīqǐ xiàng qiánjìn.
column7: Let's all move forward together.

column3: To get close to, to approach, and as an adjective "close to": 接近中午 "close to noon", 接近目标 "approach the goal". 接 ("connect") plus 近 ("near"). It can speak of time, quantity or people: 他很难接近 "he's hard to approach".
column6: Xiànzài yǐjīng jiējìn zhōngwǔ le.
column7: It is already close to noon.

column3: To transport; transportation: 运 ("move") plus 输 ("convey"). It is about moving goods in bulk: 运输公司 "transport company", 铁路运输 "rail transport", 运输货物 "transport goods". Not for people going about, which is 交通.
column4: 这家公司专门做货物运输。
column5: 這家公司專門做貨物運輸。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhuānmén zuò huòwù yùnshū.
column7: This company specializes in freight transport.

column3: Compassion, a caring heart: 爱 ("love") plus 心 ("heart"). It is the wish to help others: 有爱心 "be caring", 献爱心 "show one's love, donate". Also the heart symbol ♥. In charity talk: 爱心捐款 "charity donation".
column4: 他很有爱心，常常帮助别人。
column5: 他很有愛心，常常幫助別人。
column6: Tā hěn yǒu àixīn, chángcháng bāngzhù biérén.
column7: He is very kind and often helps others.

column3: To love deeply, to be passionate about: 热 ("hot") plus 爱 ("love"). It takes a big object: 热爱祖国 "love one's country", 热爱生活 "love life", 热爱工作. Stronger than 喜欢 and 爱, and written. Not for a romantic partner in ordinary speech.
column6: Tā rè'ài zìjǐ de gōngzuò.
column7: He loves his work deeply.

column3: To be afraid: 害 ("harm") plus 怕 ("fear"). It takes an object or a verb, or stands on its own: 害怕黑 "afraid of the dark", 我害怕, 别害怕. Spoken and common. 怕 alone has the same meaning and also means "I'm afraid that".
column6: Wǒ hàipà yī ge rén zài jiā.
column7: I am afraid of being home alone.

column3: Curious: 好 ("like to") plus 奇 ("strange"). Read hàoqí, with 好 in the fourth tone as "to be fond of". It is an adjective that shows interest: 好奇心 "curiosity", 对…很好奇 "be curious about…". Describes a child asking questions.
column6: Háizi duì shénme dōu hěn hàoqí.
column7: The child is curious about everything.

column3: Joy, joyful: 欢 ("happy") plus 乐 ("joy"). It is a written, festive word for shared happiness: 欢乐的气氛 "a joyful atmosphere", 欢乐时光 "happy times". For personal happiness in speech, 高兴 and 快乐 are more normal.
column4: 孩子们的笑声带来了欢乐。
column5: 孩子們的笑聲帶來了歡樂。
column6: Háizimen de xiàoshēng dàilái le huānlè.
column7: The children's laughter brought joy.

column3: Read lè it means "happy, glad": 乐于助人 "happy to help others", 乐了 "burst out laughing" in speech. Read yuè it is "music", as in 音乐. The two readings share one character, so watch the context.
column4: 听到这个好消息，大家都乐了。
column5: 聽到這個好消息，大家都樂了。
column6: Tīngdào zhège hǎo xiāoxi, dàjiā dōu lè le.
column7: Everyone was delighted to hear the good news.

column3: The sound of laughter, "ha ha": 哈哈大笑 "burst out laughing". It is also what you write or say when something is funny, even in text messages. Both syllables are read in the first tone, hā. It is spoken and informal, not for formal writing.
column6: Tā hāhā dà xiào qǐlái.
column7: He burst out laughing.

column3: Sad, heartbroken: 伤 ("hurt") plus 心 ("heart"), a verb and object that works as an adjective: 很伤心. It can take 了: 他伤了心. It is deeper than 难过 or 不高兴, for grief or a heavy disappointment: 别伤心了 "don't be sad".
column4: 听到这个消息，她很伤心。
column5: 聽到這個消息，她很傷心。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā hěn shāngxīn.
column7: She was heartbroken to hear the news.

column3: Pain, painful, suffering: 痛 ("ache") plus 苦 ("bitter"). It is both a noun and an adjective, speaking of deep feeling or hardship: 很痛苦 "in pain, miserable", 带来痛苦 "bring suffering". It fits emotional or serious hardship more than a small bodily ache.
column4: 失去朋友让他非常痛苦。
column5: 失去朋友讓他非常痛苦。
column6: Shīqù péngyou ràng tā fēicháng tòngkǔ.
column7: Losing his friend made him very miserable.

column3: Happy, happiness, with a deep, lasting happiness in life, a family, a marriage: 幸福的家庭 "a happy family", 祝你幸福 "I wish you happiness". Deeper than 高兴 or 快乐, which are for a mood. Read xìngfú, with 幸 in the fourth tone.
column6: Zhù nǐmen xìngfú!
column7: I wish you both happiness!

column3: Lucky, fortunate; good luck: 幸 ("luckily") plus 运 ("fortune"). 我很幸运 "I am lucky", 幸运数字 "lucky number". It speaks of a good chance that came to you. Often contrasted with 不幸 "unfortunate".
column6: Wǒ hěn xìngyùn néng rènshi nǐ.
column7: I am lucky to have met you.

column3: To satisfy, to be content: 满足需要 "meet the needs", 他很满足 "he is content". As a verb it takes a thing: 满足要求 "meet the requirement". As an adjective it describes a feeling: 感到满足. 知足 is a related word, "know contentment".
column4: 这个房子满足了我们的所有要求。
column5: 這個房子滿足了我們的所有要求。
column6: Zhège fángzi mǎnzú le wǒmen de suǒyǒu yāoqiú.
column7: This house meets all our requirements.

column3: Nervous, tense, tight: 我很紧张 "I am nervous" before an exam or interview. It also describes a strained situation (气氛紧张 "tense atmosphere") or shortage (时间紧张 "time is short"). 别紧张 is "don't be nervous".
column6: Kǎoshì qián, wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng.
column7: I am a bit nervous before the exam.

column3: Uneasy, restless: 不 ("not") plus 安 ("peaceful"). It describes a worried feeling, not an event: 心里不安 "feel uneasy", 感到不安. Also in apologies: 很不安 "I feel bad about it". The 不 is read bù, and the next syllable begins with a glottal stop, written 'an.
column4: 这么晚还没有回来，我很不安。
column5: 這麼晚還沒有回來，我很不安。
column6: Zhème wǎn hái méiyǒu huílái, wǒ hěn bù'ān.
column7: He is still not back this late, and I feel uneasy.

column3: Feelings, emotion, affection: the feeling between people, such as love, friendship and attachment: 感情很好 "get on well", 有感情 "have feelings for". 夫妻感情 is the bond of a married couple. 感情 is relational.
column6: Tāmen liǎ gǎnqíng hěn hǎo.
column7: The two of them are very close.

column3: Feeling, impression; to feel: 感 ("sense") plus 受 ("receive"). It is what you take in from an experience: 我的感受 "my feeling", 感受到 "feel, experience". Used for taking in a thing deeply, like the warmth of a place: 感受生活 "experience life".
column4: 你对这次旅行有什么感受？
column5: 你對這次旅行有什麼感受？
column6: Nǐ duì zhè cì lǚxíng yǒu shénme gǎnshòu?
column7: How did you feel about this trip?

column3: Emotion, feeling in general, a written word that speaks of human feelings as a subject: 情感生活 "emotional life", 表达情感 "express feelings". It is broader and more abstract than 感情, which is about a bond between people.
column4: 这首歌表达了很深的情感。
column5: 這首歌表達了很深的情感。
column6: Zhè shǒu gē biǎodá le hěn shēn de qínggǎn.
column7: This song expresses deep feeling.

column3: Wish, desire: 我的愿望 "my wish", 实现愿望 "make a wish come true". It is what you hope for, big or small: 生日愿望. 愿 means "be willing, wish" and 望 "look toward, hope". 许愿 is "make a wish".
column4: 我的愿望是去世界各地旅行。
column5: 我的願望是去世界各地旅行。
column6: Wǒ de yuànwàng shì qù shìjiè gèdì lǚxíng.
column7: My wish is to travel all over the world.

column3: As a verb "to hope": 我希望你快乐, 希望明天不下雨. As a noun "hope": 有希望 "there's hope", 没有希望 "no hope". The verb takes a clause after it, with a subject: 希望你来. 想 would mean "to want to", not to hope.
column6: Wǒ xīwàng míngtiān tiānqì hǎo.
column7: I hope the weather is good tomorrow.

column3: To wish: 祝你生日快乐 "happy birthday", 祝你成功 "wish you success", 祝大家新年快乐. It is how greetings begin. The person wished comes next, then the wish. It is for good wishes only. The 礻 on the left is the radical for ritual and blessings.
column6: Zhù nǐ yīlù píng'ān!
column7: I wish you a safe journey!

column3: To celebrate: 庆 ("congratulate") plus 祝 ("wish"). It takes an event as its object: 庆祝生日 "celebrate a birthday", 庆祝胜利 "celebrate a victory". A formal, public kind of celebration, where 过 is more casual (过生日).
column4: 我们开了一个晚会庆祝新年。
column5: 我們開了一個晚會慶祝新年。
column6: Wǒmen kāi le yī ge wǎnhuì qìngzhù xīnnián.
column7: We held a party to celebrate the new year.

column3: Inner heart, inside: 内 ("inside") plus 心 ("heart"), a person's deepest feelings, which others cannot see: 内心的想法 "inner thoughts", 在内心深处 "deep inside". It is a noun and often a modifier.
column6: Tā de nèixīn hěn bù píngjìng.
column7: His heart is far from calm.

column3: To be full of, to be filled with: 充 ("fill") plus 满 ("full"). It is followed by the thing that fills it, often abstract: 充满希望 "full of hope", 充满爱 "full of love", 充满快乐. Written and positive. A result compound, so 充满了 is common.
column6: Zhège jiā lǐ chōngmǎn le kuàilè.
column7: This home is full of happiness.

column3: With the second syllable in the second tone, jīngshén is "spirit, mind, energy" as an abstract noun: 精神生活 "spiritual life", 精神压力 "mental pressure", 民族精神 "the spirit of a nation". Pairs with 物质 "material". The other reading is for "lively".
column4: 读书是一种精神上的享受。
column5: 讀書是一種精神上的享受。
column6: Dúshū shì yī zhǒng jīngshén shàng de xiǎngshòu.
column7: Reading is a spiritual enjoyment.

column3: With a light second syllable, jīngshen is "lively, energetic" or "spirited": 很精神 "full of energy, looking sharp", 精神好 "in good spirits". Said of a person's look or state. A short nap makes you 有精神. Not the same word as the abstract one.
column6: Tā jīntiān kàn qǐlái hěn jīngshen.
column7: He looks full of energy today.

column3: Quiet, still, calm: 安静 "quiet", 平静 "calm", 静下来 "calm down". It is the quiet of a place or a mind. 夜深人静 "deep in the night and everyone quiet" is a set phrase.
column6: Yè shēn le, sìzhōu jìng jí le.
column7: The night is late and all around is very still.

column3: Good fortune, blessing: 幸福 "happiness", 福气 "good fortune", and the 福 posted upside down at New Year, because 倒 "upside down" sounds like 到 "arrive", so "fortune has arrived". Wish: 祝你福如东海. The 礻 on the left marks blessings.
column4: 新年到了，家家户户都贴福字。
column5: 新年到了，家家戶戶都貼福字。
column6: Xīnnián dào le, jiājiā hùhù dōu tiē fú zì.
column7: New Year has come and every household sticks up a 福 character.

column3: The beginning of the year: 年 ("year") plus 初 ("beginning"). It comes before the verb as a time word: 年初的时候, 今年年初 "early this year". The pair is 年底 "year's end". 初 here means the first part of a time.
column6: Tā niánchū qù le yī cì Rìběn.
column7: He went to Japan once at the beginning of the year.

column3: The end of the year: 年 ("year") plus 底 ("bottom"). 到年底 "by the end of the year", 年底的时候 "at year's end". A busy time for bonuses, deadlines and travel home. The opposite is 年初.
column6: Gōngsī niándǐ huì fā jiǎngjīn.
column7: The company gives out bonuses at the end of the year.

column3: Decade, era, mostly in the form of a decade: 八十年代 "the eighties", 九十年代的歌 "songs from the nineties". A bare 年代 also means "period" in general: 那个年代 "that era". Not the same as 年, which is a single year.
column4: 八十年代的音乐我很喜欢。
column5: 八十年代的音樂我很喜歡。
column6: Bāshí niándài de yīnyuè wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
column7: I like the music of the eighties.

column3: Century: 二十一世纪 "the twenty-first century", 上个世纪 "last century". Always with the number before 世纪 and no 个: not 一个世纪 in dates. The 纪 is also in 年纪 "age".
column4: 我们生活在二十一世纪。
column5: 我們生活在二十一世紀。
column6: Wǒmen shēnghuó zài èrshíyī shìjì.
column7: We live in the twenty-first century.

column3: Era, age, times: 时代 is a long period with a character: 新时代 "new era", 信息时代 "information age", 我们的时代. It can also be a stage of life: 学生时代 "school days", 童年时代. Longer than 时候, "a moment".
column4: 在学生时代，我们都很快乐。
column5: 在學生時代，我們都很快樂。
column6: Zài xuéshēng shídài, wǒmen dōu hěn kuàilè.
column7: In our school days, we were all happy.

column3: Time; when. In writing, 时 after a clause means "when": 下雨时 "when it rains", 上课时 "during class". It is the shorter, more written form of 的时候. It is also in 小时 "hour" and 当时 "at that time". The 日 on the left is "sun, day".
column6: Shàngkè shí bùyào shuōhuà.
column7: Don't talk during class.

column3: As a noun, "moment, time": 重要时刻 "an important moment", 关键时刻 "the critical moment". As an adverb, "always, constantly": 时刻准备着 "always be ready". 刻 is a quarter of an hour in 一刻钟. Written and a bit emphatic.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge nánwàng de shíkè.
column7: This is an unforgettable moment.

column3: Old, ancient: 古代 "ancient times", 古城 "ancient city", 古书 "old book". It is an adjective that lives in compounds and does not stand alone as 老 or 旧 do. The pair is 今: 古今 "ancient and modern".
column4: 这座古城有两千年的历史。
column5: 這座古城有兩千年的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò gǔchéng yǒu liǎng qiān nián de lìshǐ.
column7: This ancient city has two thousand years of history.

column3: Ancient times, ancient: the period before the modern era, long ago: 古代的人 "people of ancient times", 中国古代 "ancient China", 古代文学. Used as a noun or a modifier. The opposite is 现代 "modern times". Not "old things" but a period.
column4: 这个故事发生在中国古代。
column5: 這個故事發生在中國古代。
column6: Zhège gùshi fāshēng zài Zhōngguó gǔdài.
column7: This story takes place in ancient China.

column3: First, beginning: 年初 "start of the year", 初中 "junior high", 初次 "first time", and for the first ten days of a lunar month, 初一 "the first". It also means "beginner": 初学者. The 衤 on the left is the clothing radical; the meaning "first" is a long way from clothing.
column6: Wǒmen shì zài yuèchū rènshi de.
column7: We met at the beginning of the month.

column3: Period, a set time: 学期 "term", 星期 "week", 日期 "date", 假期 "holiday". It is the term for a block of time with start and end. As a measure word: 第三期 "issue number three". Also the 期 of 期待 "look forward to". It has 月 "moon, month" on the right.
column6: Zhège xuéqī wǒ yǒu liù mén kè.
column7: This term I have six courses.

column3: Long-term; for a long period: 长期计划 "long-term plan", 长期住在国外 "live abroad for a long time". 期 means a period of time and 长 here is cháng ("long"). It works as a modifier or adverb. The opposite is 短期.
column6: Tā chángqī zhù zài guówài.
column7: He has lived abroad for a long time.

column3: Short-term: 短 ("short") plus 期 ("period"). 短期课程 "short course", 短期计划 "short-term plan". It is the opposite of 长期 and comes before the thing it describes. Often used with courses, loans, plans and visits.
column4: 我想报一个短期的汉语班。
column5: 我想報一個短期的漢語班。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bào yī ge duǎnqī de Hànyǔ bān.
column7: I'd like to sign up for a short Chinese course.

column3: Recent, in the near future: 近 ("near") plus 期 ("period"). It can look back or ahead, depending on the verb: 近期的新闻 "recent news", 近期会有变化 "there will be changes soon". Written, as in notices and news.
column6: Jìnqī tiānqì biànhuà hěn dà.
column7: The weather has been changing a lot lately.

column3: Regularly, at fixed times: 定期检查 "regular check-up", 定期开会 "meet regularly". It means set in advance and repeated, an adverb or a modifier. A bank 定期存款 is a "fixed deposit". Differs from 经常, "often", which has no fixed schedule.
column4: 我每年定期去医院检查身体。
column5: 我每年定期去醫院檢查身體。
column6: Wǒ měinián dìqī qù yīyuàn jiǎnchá shēntǐ.
column7: I go to the hospital for a regular check-up every year.

column3: Daily, everyday, routine: it comes before a noun and describes ordinary parts of life: 日常生活 "daily life", 日常用品 "daily necessities", 日常工作 "routine work". It is a modifier and not used as an adverb. 日 means "day" and 常 "often, usual".
column6: Tā de rìcháng shēnghuó hěn jiǎndān.
column7: His daily life is very simple.

column3: The whole day, all day long: 整 ("whole") plus 天 ("day"). It goes before the verb as an adverbial of time, often showing a complaint or surprise: 整天玩手机 "play on the phone all day". Takes no 的 and no 一: not 一整天的 unless 一整天.
column6: Tā zhěngtiān zài jiā kàn diànshì.
column7: He watches TV at home all day.

column3: Free time, spare moment, written kòngr in speech. It is a northern spoken word, often in the pattern 有空儿 "have free time" or 没空儿 "have no time": 你什么时候有空儿? Here 空 is read kòng, the fourth tone, not kōng. 儿 is a soft ending.
column6: Míngtiān nǐ yǒu kòngr ma?
column7: Do you have time tomorrow?

column3: Clock: 一个钟, 钟声 "the sound of a bell". The word covers wall clocks, bells and 钟 as a time word in 点钟 "o'clock" and 分钟 "minute", so 五分钟 means "five minutes". 钅 on the left is the metal radical; the older 鐘 was a bronze bell.
column6: Qiáng shàng de zhōng yǐjīng bā diǎn le.
column7: The clock on the wall already says eight.

column3: At that time, originally: looking back at the past, usually with regret or a comment on what should have been done: 当初我不该那样做 "I shouldn't have done it that way then". It points to the beginning of a situation, not just "back then", and is often followed by a reflection.
column6: Dāngchū wǒ yīnggāi tīng nǐ de huà.
column7: At the time I should have listened to you.

column3: In the past, once upon a time: 从前有一座山 "once upon a time there was a mountain" opens a fairy tale. It can also mean "formerly": 他比从前瘦了 "he's thinner than before". It is a time word and comes at the start of a sentence or before the verb.
column6: Cóngqián, zhèlǐ shì yī piàn tiándì.
column7: In the past, this was a field.

column3: At present, for now: 目 ("eye") plus 前 ("front"), literally "before the eyes". A formal time word about the current situation: 目前情况 "the present situation", 目前还没有 "not yet at present". It goes before the verb or at the start. Not for the moment of speech exactly, but a period.
column6: Mùqián wǒmen hái méiyǒu juédìng.
column7: At present we haven't decided yet.

column3: Before one's eyes, right now: 眼 ("eye") plus 前 ("front"). It is literal (眼前的风景 "the scene before my eyes") and figurative (顾及眼前 "think of the present only", 眼前的困难 "the difficulty at hand"). It speaks of the immediate here and now.
column6: Yǎnqián de fēngjǐng tài měi le.
column7: The scenery in front of me is so beautiful.

column3: The future, in the future: 将 ("will") plus 来 ("come"). It points to the time ahead, further off than 明天: 将来我想当老师 "in the future I want to be a teacher". 未来 is the same idea but more written and grand. It can start a sentence.
column6: Jiānglái nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme gōngzuò?
column7: What job do you want to do in the future?

column3: Since, ever since: it follows a point in time or a period and says the state has lasted until now: 今年以来 "since the start of this year", 三年以来 "for three years now". Unlike 自从, which starts the phrase, 以来 comes at the end: 自从来中国以来.
column4: 毕业以来，我一直在这家公司工作。
column5: 畢業以來，我一直在這家公司工作。
column6: Bìyè yǐlái, wǒ yīzhí zài zhè jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
column7: Since graduating, I have worked at this company.

column3: Up to now, to this day: 至 ("to") plus 今 ("now"). It says that a situation has lasted from the past until now, often with 仍 or 还: 至今没有结果 "no result to this day", 至今记得 "still remember". Written, and put before the verb.
column4: 这个问题至今没有答案。
column5: 這個問題至今沒有答案。
column6: Zhège wèntí zhìjīn méiyǒu dá'àn.
column7: This question has no answer to this day.

column3: Since, a conjunction that starts a clause naming a past starting point: 自从他来了, 我们的生活变了 "since he came, our lives changed". It often pairs with 以后 or 以来, and what follows describes a lasting change. The point must be in the past.
column4: 自从搬家以后，我每天都很忙。
column5: 自從搬家以後，我每天都很忙。
column6: Zìcóng bānjiā yǐhòu, wǒ měitiān dōu hěn máng.
column7: Since moving house, I've been busy every day.

column3: To do something ahead of time, in advance: 提前到 "arrive early", 提前一天 "one day in advance", 提前通知 "notify in advance". Used as a verb or an adverb, moving a plan earlier than set: 会议提前了 "the meeting was brought forward".
column4: 明天的会议提前到八点。
column5: 明天的會議提前到八點。
column6: Míngtiān de huìyì tíqián dào bā diǎn.
column7: Tomorrow's meeting has been moved up to eight.

column3: Already, a written form of 已经: 已知 "already known", 已婚 "married", 已有 "already have". It sits before the verb and is mostly used in formal writing, notices and set words. 已 does not usually stand in speech. 早已 and 业已 build on it.
column6: Tā yǐ bù zài zhèlǐ gōngzuò le.
column7: He doesn't work here any more.

column3: Once, before: it says something happened at some point in the past, often with 过: 我曾经去过北京 "I have been to Beijing before". The 曾 is read céng, not zēng, which is only a surname. It goes before the verb; negative form is 没(有)…过.
column4: 我曾经在那儿住过两年。
column5: 我曾經在那兒住過兩年。
column6: Wǒ céngjīng zài nàr zhù guo liǎng nián.
column7: I once lived there for two years.

column3: Long since, already a long time ago: 早 ("early") plus 已 ("already"). It stresses that something happened well before now: 早已知道 "have known for a long time", 早已忘了 "had long forgotten". Written and a bit stronger than 已经. It sits before the verb.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì tā zǎoyǐ zhīdào le.
column7: He has known about this for a long time.

column3: Originally, at first and "of course": 本来我想去 "I originally wanted to go (but didn't)", 本来就是这样 "it was always like that". The first sense often introduces a plan that changed. As an adjective: 本来的样子 "its original look".
column4: 我本来想去，但是下雨了。
column5: 我本來想去，但是下雨了。
column6: Wǒ běnlái xiǎng qù, dànshì xià yǔ le.
column7: I originally wanted to go, but it rained.

column3: Immediately, right away: 立 ("stand") plus 刻 ("moment"), "stand at once". It is an adverb that goes before the verb, and means without delay: 立刻出发 "set off at once". Slightly more formal than 马上, which also means "at once".
column4: 听到电话声，他立刻跑了过去。
column5: 聽到電話聲，他立刻跑了過去。
column6: Tīngdào diànhuà shēng, tā lìkè pǎo le guòqù.
column7: Hearing the phone, he ran over at once.

column3: Hastily, promptly: 连 ("in succession") plus 忙 ("busy"). It describes a quick reaction to something that just happened, and is used in narration of past events, not in commands: 他连忙站起来 "he hurriedly stood up". It cannot be used with 请 or imperatives.
column4: 看到老师进来，学生们连忙站了起来。
column5: 看到老師進來，學生們連忙站了起來。
column6: Kàndào lǎoshī jìnlái, xuéshengmen liánmáng zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: Seeing the teacher come in, the students quickly stood up.

column3: Quickly, hurry up and: 赶 ("hurry") plus 紧 ("tight"). It can describe a past action (他赶紧跑过去) or push someone in a command (你赶紧走吧). It means do it without delay, stressing urgency more than 马上. Always before the verb.
column4: 雨下大了，我们赶紧回家吧。
column5: 雨下大了，我們趕緊回家吧。
column6: Yǔ xià dà le, wǒmen gǎnjǐn huí jiā ba.
column7: The rain is heavy now, let's hurry home.

column3: Quickly, at once: used to urge someone to act fast: 赶快走 "go quickly", 赶快回家. It is common in commands and requests. 赶快 is much like 赶紧; 赶快 leans to the urging side, so it fits imperatives well.
column4: 时间不早了，你赶快起床吧。
column5: 時間不早了，你趕快起床吧。
column6: Shíjiān bù zǎo le, nǐ gǎnkuài qǐchuáng ba.
column7: It's getting late, hurry up and get up.

column3: In time, timely: 及 ("reach") plus 时 ("time"). As an adverb: 及时赶到 "arrive in time", 及时回复 "reply promptly". As an adjective: 及时雨 "timely rain". It stresses that something happens just when needed, not just fast.
column6: Tā jíshí gǎndào le jīchǎng.
column7: He got to the airport in time.

column3: At last, finally, for something long awaited that finally happens: 他终于来了 "he's finally here". It carries relief. It goes before the verb and usually with 了. It is not used for negative expected events that you dreaded; for those one says 最后.
column4: 等了一个小时，车终于来了。
column5: 等了一個小時，車終於來了。
column6: Děng le yī ge xiǎoshí, chē zhōngyú lái le.
column7: After waiting an hour, the bus finally came.

column3: Suddenly; sudden: 突然下雨了 "it suddenly rained". As an adverb it goes before the verb, and as an adjective it takes 很 or 的: 很突然 "very sudden", 突然的消息 "sudden news". Do not use it for something expected.
column6: Tiānqì tūrán biàn lěng le.
column7: The weather suddenly turned cold.

column3: The north part, northern region: 北 ("north") plus 部 ("part"). It names the northern portion of a country or place: 中国北部 "northern China", 台湾北部 "northern Taiwan". It is the part, where 北方 is the north as a direction or region of China.
column6: Táiwān de běibù xià yǔ hěn duō.
column7: It rains a lot in the north of Taiwan.

column3: The south part, southern region: 南 ("south") plus 部 ("part"). It is a part of a country: 南部地区 "the southern area", 美国南部 "the southern United States". 南方 is the "south" as a broader region, where 南部 is a section.
column6: Zhège guójiā de nánbù hěn rè.
column7: The south of this country is very hot.

column3: The eastern part: 东 ("east") plus 部 ("part"). 中国东部 "eastern China", the coast, where most big cities are. 东部地区 "the eastern region". It names a section of a larger place. 东方 is "the East" as a direction or the Orient.
column4: 中国的大城市大多在东部。
column5: 中國的大城市大多在東部。
column6: Zhōngguó de dà chéngshì dàduō zài dōngbù.
column7: Most of China's big cities are in the east.

column3: The western part: 西 ("west") plus 部 ("part"). 中国西部 "western China", 西部大开发 "the Western Development" policy. Often used for the inland, less developed areas of a country, and in the US for the "Wild West": 西部片 "western film".
column6: Tā xiǎng qù xībù lǚxíng.
column7: He wants to travel in the west.

column3: The central part: 中 ("middle") plus 部 ("part"). 中国中部 "central China", 台湾中部 "central Taiwan". It follows the pattern of 北部, 南部, 东部 and 西部, naming a region as a part of a whole. 中部地区 "the central region".
column6: Húběi zài Zhōngguó de zhōngbù.
column7: Hubei is in the central part of China.

column3: As a preposition, "toward, facing": 朝前走 "walk forward", 门朝南 "the door faces south". Read cháo it also means "dynasty": 朝代 "dynasty", 唐朝 "the Tang dynasty". The two senses share one reading in this word. 朝 as "morning" is zhāo, in 朝气 "vitality".
column6: Zhège fángzi de chuānghu cháo nán.
column7: The windows of this house face south.

column3: Inside, within: 国内 "domestic", 室内 "indoors", 内部 "interior", 一年内 "within a year". It follows a noun of place or time to mark the inside or a limit. The pair is 外 "outside".
column6: Qǐng zài sān tiān nèi huífù wǒ.
column7: Please reply to me within three days.

column3: Surroundings, around: 周 ("around") plus 围 ("surround"). It can be a noun, 周围的环境 "the surroundings", or a place word, 学校周围 "around the school", 我周围的人 "the people around me".
column6: Wǒ jiā zhōuwéi yǒu hěn duō shù.
column7: There are many trees around my home.

column3: Behind, at the back: 背 ("back") plus 后 ("behind"). It is the place behind something: 门背后 "behind the door", or figuratively "behind someone's back": 在背后说人坏话 "speak ill of someone behind their back", and "behind the scenes": 成功的背后.
column4: 他的背后站着一个小孩。
column5: 他的背後站著一個小孩。
column6: Tā de bèihòu zhàn zhe yī ge xiǎohái.
column7: A small child is standing behind him.

column3: Surface, outside, appearance: 桌子的表面 "the surface of the table", and in the abstract, 表面上 "on the surface", 表面现象 "outward appearance". It often contrasts with what is underneath: 表面上很平静, 其实… "calm on the surface, but actually…".
column4: 他表面上很平静，其实很紧张。
column5: 他表面上很平靜，其實很緊張。
column6: Tā biǎomiàn shàng hěn píngjìng, qíshí hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: On the surface he is calm, but really he is nervous.

column3: Around, about for time and "front and back" for place. For time: 春节前后 "around Spring Festival", 三点前后 "around three o'clock", 前后一共三年 "three years in all, from start to finish". For place: 房子前后 "front and back of the house".
column4: 春节前后，火车票很难买。
column5: 春節前後，火車票很難買。
column6: Chūnjié qiánhòu, huǒchē piào hěn nán mǎi.
column7: Train tickets are hard to buy around Spring Festival.

column3: After a number, "about, around": 三十岁左右 "about thirty years old", 十点左右 "around ten o'clock". It marks an approximate figure, either side of it. Alone, it means "left and right" (左右两边) or "to influence" (左右局势). Don't use 大概 and 左右 together.
column4: 他三十岁左右，个子很高。
column5: 他三十歲左右，個子很高。
column6: Tā sānshí suì zuǒyòu, gèzi hěn gāo.
column7: He is around thirty and quite tall.

column3: To come up: 上来 means move upward toward the speaker: 请上来 "please come up". As a verb complement it follows another verb: 爬上来 "climb up", 说不上来 "can't say", 想起来 is a different form. 上来 keeps the movement toward the speaker.
column6: Nǐ shànglái ba, wǒ zài èr lóu.
column7: Come on up, I'm on the second floor.

column3: To go up: the movement is up and away from the speaker: 走上去 "walk up", 爬上去 "climb up". The pair of 上来, with the direction away from the speaker. 上去 and 上来 are also complements after a verb: 他跑上去了 "he ran up".
column6: Wǒmen cóng lóutī zǒu shàngqù ba.
column7: Let's walk up the stairs.

column3: To come down: toward the speaker. As a verb alone: 你下来吧. As a complement after a verb: 跑下来, 坐下来 "sit down", 安静下来 "calm down". After a verb it can also show that something carries on from past to now: 传下来 "has been handed down". In 下来 the second syllable is light.
column6: Nǐ kuài xiàlai, fàn zuò hǎo le.
column7: Come down quickly, the meal is ready.

column3: To go down away from the speaker: 走下去. After a verb it shows continuing an action: 说下去 "go on talking", 坚持下去 "keep going". 学下去 would mean "to go on studying". Compare 下来, which is toward the speaker or a result.
column6: Qǐng nǐ shuō xiàqu, wǒ zài tīng.
column7: Please go on, I'm listening.

column3: Underneath, below: 桌子底下 "under the table", 树底下 "under the tree". It is a spoken place word, equal to 下面. It can also mean "later" or "under someone's lead": 他手底下有十个人 "he has ten people under him". The 下 is light.
column6: Xiǎo māo duǒ zài zhuōzi dǐxia.
column7: The kitten is hiding under the table.

column3: In the middle, among: 当 ("at") plus 中 ("middle"). 我们当中 "among us", 人群当中 "in the crowd", 三个人当中 "of the three". It points to a member of a group: 他是我们当中最高的 "he is the tallest among us".
column6: Tā shì wǒmen dāngzhōng zuì gāo de.
column7: He is the tallest of us.

column3: Straight: 直线 "straight line", 一直走 "go straight on", 直接 "direct". As an adverb it means "directly" or "continuously": 直哭 "cry non-stop". 一直 is "all along". It also means "upright" and "frank": 他说话很直.
column6: Qiánmiàn de lù hěn zhí.
column7: The road ahead is very straight.

column3: Moves the object before the verb: 我把书放在桌子上 "I put the book on the table". The pattern is subject + 把 + object + verb + result: the verb is not bare, it needs a result such as 完, 在 or 了. It is used when the object is known and gets affected. Also a measure word for things with a handle: 一把椅子.
column6: Qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng.
column7: Please close the door.

column3: Marks the passive: 杯子被他打破了 "the cup was broken by him". Pattern: object + 被 + doer + verb + result. The doer may be left out: 杯子被打破了. Often used for unwelcome events, though not always. In speech 让 and 叫 do the same job.
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
column7: My phone was stolen.

column3: To make, to cause: 使人高兴 "make people happy", 使我很吃惊 "surprised me". It is the written version of 让 in this sense and needs a person or a thing as the object, followed by the result. 使 also means "to use" (使用). Subject is often an event: 这件事使他很难过.
column4: 这个消息使大家很高兴。
column5: 這個消息使大家很高興。
column6: Zhège xiāoxi shǐ dàjiā hěn gāoxìng.
column7: This news made everyone very happy.

column3: The 所 of 所有 "all" and 所以 "so". As a function word, it goes before a verb in the pattern 所+verb+的, making a noun: 我所知道的 "what I know". Also in 为…所…. As a measure word for buildings, schools or hospitals: 一所学校, 一所医院. It is "a place" in 场所.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ suǒ zhīdào de yīqiè.
column7: This is all that I know.

column3: Even, in the pattern 连…也/都…: 连老师也不知道 "even the teacher doesn't know". It also means "to link" (连接) and "in a row" (连续). In 连我都… the 连 picks out the surprising case.
column4: 这个问题连老师也不知道。
column5: 這個問題連老師也不知道。
column6: Zhège wèntí lián lǎoshī yě bù zhīdào.
column7: Even the teacher doesn't know this question.

column3: Read liǎo it has its own sense, "to finish" or "able to", as in 了解 "to understand", and in the potential forms 吃不了 "can't finish eating", 受不了 "can't stand", 去得了 "can go". Don't confuse with the ordinary particle le, which marks completion.
column4: 这么多菜，我一个人吃不了。
column5: 這麼多菜，我一個人吃不了。
column6: Zhème duō cài, wǒ yī ge rén chī bu liǎo.
column7: I can't finish this many dishes on my own.

column3: Only, merely: 不仅 "not only", 仅有 "only have". It is a written word. It goes before the verb or number to say it is limited: 仅有一个 "only one". 仅 is a short form of 仅仅.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn jǐn zài zhōumò kāimén.
column7: This shop is only open at weekends.

column3: Merely, only, the stronger and doubled form of 仅. It stresses how small the amount is: 仅仅三天 "just three days", 仅仅是开始 "it's only the beginning". It is often followed by 就 or 是. Written.
column4: 他仅仅用了三天就学会了。
column5: 他僅僅用了三天就學會了。
column6: Tā jǐnjǐn yòng le sān tiān jiù xuéhuì le.
column7: He learned it in just three days.

column3: As an adverb, "comparatively, fairly, rather": 比较好 "fairly good", 比较便宜 "relatively cheap". It softens an adjective, like "rather". As a verb, "to compare": 比较两个国家. It is not the same as 比: with 比 you name the thing being compared with. 比较 does not do that.
column4: 这家店的东西比较便宜。
column5: 這家店的東西比較便宜。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi bǐjiào piányi.
column7: The things in this shop are fairly cheap.

column3: Comparatively or "to compare", mostly in compounds: 比较, 较大 "rather big", 较好 "better, fairly good". It is the written form of 比较 as an adverb and goes before an adjective: 较早 "rather early". Alone, it rarely appears in speech. The 车 on the left is for carts.
column6: Jīnnián de jiàgé jiào qùnián gāo.
column7: This year's price is higher than last year's.

column3: Even more, still more: 更 ("more") plus 加 ("add"). Placed before an adjective or verb to raise a degree that is already high: 更加努力 "work even harder", 更加重要. It needs something to be compared with. 更 alone does the same in speech.
column6: Tā bǐ yǐqián gèngjiā nǔlì le.
column7: He works even harder than before.

column3: Any, whichever: it goes before a noun and means no exception: 任何人 "anyone", 任何时候 "any time", 任何问题 "any problem". It is often paired with 都 or 也: 任何人都可以来. In negatives, it means "not any": 没有任何问题.
column4: 你有任何问题都可以问我。
column5: 你有任何問題都可以問我。
column6: Nǐ yǒu rènhé wèntí dōu kěyǐ wèn wǒ.
column7: You can ask me any question.
