column3: A certain, some: 某人 "a certain person", 某天 "a certain day", 某个地方 "some place". It is used for something not named, or kept vague on purpose: 某公司 "a certain company". Also stands for names in notices: 王某 "a Mr. Wang". It is written, and the thing follows directly.
column6: Mǒu tiān wǎnshang, tā tūrán lái le.
column7: One evening he suddenly came.

column3: Each, every, various: it comes before a noun and treats the members separately: 各位 "everyone" (polite), 各国 "each country", 各种 "all kinds", 各地 "all places". 各 doesn't count: it points to each of a group. 各位 is how you address an audience.
column6: Gèwèi tóngxué, qǐng zuò.
column7: Everyone, please take a seat.

column3: Should, ought to: 应 ("should") plus 当 ("ought"). Written and a bit more formal than 应该, with the same sense of duty or right: 应当遵守规定 "should follow the rules". Read yīngdāng. The 应 here is yīng, not yìng.
column4: 每个人都应当遵守规定。
column5: 每個人都應當遵守規定。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yīngdāng zūnshǒu guīdìng.
column7: Everyone should follow the rules.

column3: Necessary: 必要的条件 "a necessary condition", 有必要 "it is necessary", 没有必要 "no need". It works as an adjective before a noun, or in the pattern 有必要+verb. It is stronger than 需要, more about what has to be done. 不必要 is "unnecessary".
column6: Nǐ méiyǒu bìyào zhème zháojí.
column7: There is no need for you to be so anxious.

column3: Need not, no need to: 不必客气 "no need to stand on ceremony", 不必担心 "no need to worry". It says something isn't necessary, and sits before a verb. Compared with 不用, it is slightly more formal. It cannot be used for "must not", which is 不要 or 不能.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ bùbì dānxīn.
column7: You needn't worry about this matter.

column3: Class in a school, as a group of students: 班 ("class") plus 级 ("grade"). Our class is 我们班, and the 班级 is the formal term: 班级活动 "class activity". It may also mean the grade-and-class combination, like 三年级二班.
column4: 我们班级有三十个学生。
column5: 我們班級有三十個學生。
column6: Wǒmen bānjí yǒu sānshí ge xuésheng.
column7: Our class has thirty students.

column3: Junior high school in China: three years after primary school, ages about 12 to 15. 初中生 is a junior high student, 初一 is the first year of it. 初 means "first, beginner" and 中 "middle". The next stage is 高中.
column6: Tā míngnián shàng chūzhōng.
column7: He starts junior high next year.

column3: Beginner level, elementary: 初级班 "a beginners' class", 初级汉语 "elementary Chinese". 初 ("first") plus 级 ("level"). The next is 中级 "intermediate" and 高级 "advanced". It comes before a noun and tells a level of a course or skill.
column4: 我现在在上初级汉语班。
column5: 我現在在上初級漢語班。
column6: Wǒ xiànzài zài shàng chūjí Hànyǔ bān.
column7: I am in a beginner Chinese class now.

column3: Course, curriculum: 课 ("class") plus 程 ("program, course of a process"). The whole program of study in a subject or school: 汉语课程 "Chinese course", 课程表 "class schedule". Where 课 is one class or lesson, 课程 is the entire program. Count with 门: 一门课程.
column4: 这门课程包括听说读写。
column5: 這門課程包括聽說讀寫。
column6: Zhè mén kèchéng bāokuò tīng shuō dú xiě.
column7: This course includes listening, speaking, reading and writing.

column3: Teaching materials, textbook: 教 ("teach") plus 材 ("material"). It covers textbooks and any other materials for a course: 汉语教材 "Chinese teaching materials", 选教材 "choose materials". 材 has 木 "wood" because it means "raw material". Differs from 课本, one specific book.
column4: 这套教材很适合初学者。
column5: 這套教材很適合初學者。
column6: Zhè tào jiàocái hěn shìhé chūxuézhě.
column7: This set of materials suits beginners well.

column3: Tuition fee: 学 ("study") plus 费 ("fee, cost"). The money paid for classes: 交学费 "pay tuition", 学费很贵 "tuition is expensive". 费 is a general suffix for costs, as in 房费 and 电话费. A classic school phrase: 免学费 "tuition-free".
column4: 大学的学费一年多少钱？
column5: 大學的學費一年多少錢？
column6: Dàxué de xuéfèi yī nián duōshao qián?
column7: How much is university tuition per year?

column3: To study abroad: 留 ("stay") plus 学 ("study"), a verb that takes 国家 as a location. 去美国留学 "go study in the US", 留学生 "international student", 留学回国 "return from studying abroad". It is for studying in another country, not just away from home.
column4: 她打算明年去英国留学。
column5: 她打算明年去英國留學。
column6: Tā dǎsuàn míngnián qù Yīngguó liúxué.
column7: She plans to study in Britain next year.

column3: To prepare a lesson in advance: 预 ("beforehand") plus 习 ("practice"). Students look over new material before the class: 预习课文 "preview the text", 课前预习. The opposite is 复习 "to review". It is a school word and fits a routine of 预习, 上课, 复习.
column4: 上课以前，我们要先预习课文。
column5: 上課以前，我們要先預習課文。
column6: Shàngkè yǐqián, wǒmen yào xiān yùxí kèwén.
column7: Before class, we need to preview the text first.

column3: Exam question: 试 ("test") plus 题 ("question"). It refers to questions on a test paper: 一道试题 "an exam question", 试题很难 "the questions are hard". 考试题 is related. 试卷 is the test paper. Count with 道.
column4: 这次考试的试题不太难。
column5: 這次考試的試題不太難。
column6: Zhè cì kǎoshì de shìtí bù tài nán.
column7: The questions in this exam are not too hard.

column3: Topic, title, exam question: the title of an essay (作文题目), or a question in a test or exercise (一道题目). Also "topic" in speeches. 题 ("topic") plus 目 ("item"). Counted with 道 for questions. 题目 can be either the question or the essay title.
column4: 这篇文章的题目是什么？
column5: 這篇文章的題目是什麼？
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng de tímù shì shénme?
column7: What is the title of this article?

column3: To ask a question, formal, usually in a classroom or an interview: 老师提问学生 "the teacher asks students questions", 提问题 "put a question". 提 ("raise") plus 问 ("ask"). In class, 回答提问 is "answer the questions". A verb and an object that can be split: 提了一个问.
column6: Lǎoshī xiàng tóngxuémen tíwèn.
column7: The teacher asks the students questions.

column3: To ask for advice, to consult: 请 ("request") plus 教 ("teach"). Said politely to someone with more experience: 向老师请教 "ask the teacher for advice", 我想请教您一个问题 "I'd like to ask you something". Only for the asker. 教 here is read jiào.
column4: 我想向您请教一个问题。
column5: 我想向您請教一個問題。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng xiàng nín qǐngjiào yī ge wèntí.
column7: I would like to ask you a question.

column3: Unit: a section of a textbook or course, 第三单元 "unit three". Also an entrance or stairwell of a block of flats, as in 三号楼二单元 "building 3, entrance 2", used in addresses. 单 ("single") plus 元 ("part, unit").
column4: 这本书一共有十个单元。
column5: 這本書一共有十個單元。
column6: Zhè běn shū yīgòng yǒu shí ge dānyuán.
column7: This book has ten units in all.

column3: Read bēi it is "to carry on the back": 背书包 "carry a school bag", 背孩子 "carry a child on your back". Read bèi it is "the back" (后背) and "to learn by heart" (背课文 is bèi). The list means the verb with bēi. Mind the difference, which shows up in 背包 "backpack" bēibāo.
column4: 他背着一个很大的书包。
column5: 他背著一個很大的書包。
column6: Tā bēi zhe yī ge hěn dà de shūbāo.
column7: He is carrying a very large school bag on his back.

column3: To train; training: 训 ("instruct") plus 练 ("practice"). It is organized, repeated practice, for sports, work or a skill: 体育训练 "sports training", 训练班 "training class", 训练新人 "train new staff". It is more formal than 练习, which is any practice.
column4: 运动员每天都要训练四个小时。
column5: 運動員每天都要訓練四個小時。
column6: Yùndòngyuán měitiān dōu yào xùnliàn sì ge xiǎoshí.
column7: The athletes train for four hours every day.

column3: Listening ability, hearing: 听 ("listen") plus 力 ("ability"). In language study it is the listening part of a course or a test: 听力考试 "listening exam", 听力练习 "listening practice", 提高听力. It can mean your sense of hearing in a medical sense: 听力不好.
column4: 我的听力不太好，请说慢一点。
column5: 我的聽力不太好，請說慢一點。
column6: Wǒ de tīnglì bù tài hǎo, qǐng shuō màn yīdiǎn.
column7: My listening is not so good, please speak more slowly.

column3: Experiment: 做实验 "do an experiment". 实 ("real") plus 验 ("test"). It is a planned test in science, to see what happens, and is also a verb: 实验新方法 "try out a new method". A science-class word: 化学实验.
column4: 我们今天在课上做了一个化学实验。
column5: 我們今天在課上做了一個化學實驗。
column6: Wǒmen jīntiān zài kè shàng zuò le yī ge huàxué shíyàn.
column7: We did a chemistry experiment in class today.

column3: Laboratory: 实验 ("experiment") plus 室 ("room"). Where experiments are carried out: 化学实验室 "chemistry lab", 进实验室 "go into the lab". For research there is also 研究室 and 研究所. Count with 个 or 间.
column4: 学生们正在实验室里做实验。
column5: 學生們正在實驗室裡做實驗。
column6: Xuéshengmen zhèngzài shíyànshì lǐ zuò shíyàn.
column7: The students are doing experiments in the lab.

column3: Experiment, trial, test: 试 ("try") plus 验 ("test"). Similar to 实验, but 试验 is closer to trying something out to see if it works, e.g. a new product or method: 试验新药 "test a new drug", 试验阶段 "trial stage". 实验 is more scientific investigation.
column4: 这种新药还在试验阶段。
column5: 這種新藥還在試驗階段。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xīn yào hái zài shìyàn jiēduàn.
column7: This new drug is still at the trial stage.

column3: As a noun, "major, specialty": 你学什么专业? "What do you major in?", 我的专业是历史. As an adjective, "professional": 专业的 "professional", 很专业 "very professional". Both senses are in common use, in a school and at work. 专 means "focused" and 业 "field".
column6: Wǒ de zhuānyè shì jìsuànjī.
column7: My major is computer science.

column3: Special topic, feature: a subject taken up on its own: 专题讲座 "special lecture on a topic", 专题报道 "feature report", 专题节目. 专 ("special") plus 题 ("topic"). A word of media, lectures and reports, not of casual talk.
column4: 电视台做了一个关于环境的专题节目。
column5: 電視臺做了一個關於環境的專題節目。
column6: Diànshìtái zuò le yī ge guānyú huánjìng de zhuāntí jiémù.
column7: The TV station made a special program about the environment.

column3: Read xì it is a university "department": 中文系 "Chinese department", 数学系 "math department", 在历史系学习. It also means "system" in compounds (关系 "relationship", 联系 "contact") and "to be" in formal writing (系…). Not to be mixed with 系 read jì, "to tie".
column6: Tā zài Zhōngwén xì xuéxí.
column7: She studies in the Chinese department.

column3: Qualification, eligibility: 有资格 "be qualified to", 没有资格 "not entitled to", 资格考试 "qualifying exam". 资 means "resources" and 格 "standard". It names the right or the credentials to do something: 你没有资格说我.
column4: 你还没有资格参加这次比赛。
column5: 你還沒有資格參加這次比賽。
column6: Nǐ hái méiyǒu zīgé cānjiā zhè cì bǐsài.
column7: You are not yet qualified to take part in this competition.

column3: Qualified, up to standard: 合 ("fit") plus 格 ("standard"). It is both pass and fit for use: 考试合格 "pass the exam", 产品合格 "the product meets the standard", 合格证 "certificate". The opposite is 不合格 "substandard". It is used for people and goods alike.
column6: Zhè pī chǎnpǐn quánbù hégé.
column7: All of this batch of products are up to standard.

column3: Aspiration, volunteer: 志愿者 "volunteer", 志愿服务 "voluntary service". It also means the choices of university and major a student lists: 填志愿 "fill in the application choices", 第一志愿 "first choice". 志 means "will, ambition" and 愿 "wish". Two sides: a wish and a volunteer.
column6: Tā bàomíng dāng le zhìyuànzhě.
column7: He signed up to be a volunteer.

column3: To report in, to check in, to register: 报 ("report") plus 到 ("arrive"). Arriving at a school or workplace to say you have come: 新生报到 "new students register", 去公司报到 "report to the company". A verb and object, so 报了到.
column4: 新同学今天来学校报到。
column5: 新同學今天來學校報到。
column6: Xīn tóngxué jīntiān lái xuéxiào bàodào.
column7: The new students are coming to school today to register.

column3: TV drama, TV series: 电视 ("television") plus 剧 ("drama"). Count with 部 for the whole series: 一部电视剧, and with 集 for episodes: 第三集. 看电视剧 "watch a TV drama". 剧 in 电影 context is "play".
column4: 我最喜欢看这部电视剧。
column5: 我最喜歡看這部電視劇。
column6: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan kàn zhè bù diànshìjù.
column7: I most like watching this TV series.

column3: Serial drama, TV series: 连续 ("continuous") plus 剧 ("drama"). Same thing as 电视剧, but it stresses the series going on from episode to episode: 一部连续剧, 电视连续剧. Older and slightly formal; 电视剧 is the everyday word.
column4: 这部连续剧一共有四十集。
column5: 這部連續劇一共有四十集。
column6: Zhè bù liánxùjù yīgòng yǒu sìshí jí.
column7: This series has forty episodes in all.

column3: Television station: 电视 ("television") plus 台 ("station, platform"). The broadcaster: 中央电视台 "China Central Television", 在电视台工作. 台 is also in 电台 "radio station" and 舞台 "stage". Count with 个 or 家.
column6: Tā zài diànshìtái dāng jìzhě.
column7: He is a reporter at a TV station.

column3: Radio station: 电 ("electric") plus 台 ("station"). It is the radio broadcaster, or the radio program: 听电台 "listen to the radio", 电台节目 "radio show", 电台主持人 "radio host". Count with 家 or 个.
column4: 我开车的时候喜欢听电台。
column5: 我開車的時候喜歡聽電臺。
column6: Wǒ kāichē de shíhou xǐhuan tīng diàntái.
column7: I like listening to the radio when I drive.

column3: Film and television: 影 ("film") plus 视 ("TV"). A collective word for the whole industry: 影视明星 "film and TV star", 影视作品 "film and TV works", 影视公司. Used in news, careers and studies.
column4: 他想以后做影视方面的工作。
column5: 他想以後做影視方面的工作。
column6: Tā xiǎng yǐhòu zuò yǐngshì fāngmiàn de gōngzuò.
column7: He wants to work in film and television later.

column3: To broadcast, to air: 播 ("broadcast") plus 出 ("out"). Used for programs that go on TV or the radio: 播出时间 "air time", 节目已经播出了 "the program has aired". The object comes before: 这部电视剧将在明晚播出.
column4: 这个节目每天晚上八点播出。
column5: 這個節目每天晚上八點播出。
column6: Zhège jiémù měitiān wǎnshang bā diǎn bōchū.
column7: This program is aired every evening at eight.

column3: To play, to broadcast: 播 ("sow, broadcast") plus 放 ("put, release"). The thing being played comes after it: 播放音乐 "play music", 播放视频 "play a video", 播放电影. It is used for media and apps: the "play" button. Differs from 播出, which means to air on air.
column4: 请播放一首我喜欢的歌。
column5: 請播放一首我喜歡的歌。
column6: Qǐng bōfàng yī shǒu wǒ xǐhuan de gē.
column7: Please play a song I like.

column3: Live broadcast; to broadcast live: 直 ("straight") plus 播 ("broadcast"). Used on TV and online: 直播比赛 "broadcast the game live", 看直播 "watch the live stream", 直播间 "live stream room". In recent years it also covers streaming sales.
column6: Zhè chǎng bǐsài yǒu diànshì zhíbō.
column7: This match is broadcast live on TV.

column3: Radio broadcast; to broadcast: 听广播 "listen to the radio", 广播电台 "radio station", 车站广播 "station announcement". It names the radio as a medium and also announcements on a loudspeaker: 广播通知. 广 means "wide", so "spread widely".
column4: 广播里正在播放天气预报。
column5: 廣播裡正在播放天氣預報。
column6: Guǎngbō lǐ zhèngzài bōfàng tiānqì yùbào.
column7: The weather forecast is on the radio.

column3: To watch a TV program, mostly in announcements: 收看节目 "watch a program", 感谢收看 "thank you for watching". 收 ("receive") plus 看 ("watch"). A formal word of broadcasting, not for watching a thing at home casually.
column4: 欢迎收看今晚的新闻节目。
column5: 歡迎收看今晚的新聞節目。
column6: Huānyíng shōukàn jīnwǎn de xīnwén jiémù.
column7: Welcome to tonight's news program.

column3: To listen to a radio broadcast: 收听广播 "listen to the radio", 感谢收听 "thanks for listening". It pairs with 收看 for TV. 收 ("receive") plus 听 ("listen"). A formal word of broadcasting.
column4: 欢迎收听我们的广播节目。
column5: 歡迎收聽我們的廣播節目。
column6: Huānyíng shōutīng wǒmen de guǎngbō jiémù.
column7: Welcome to our radio program.

column3: Radio as a device: 收 ("receive") plus 音 ("sound") plus 机 ("machine"). Counted with 台 or 个: 一台收音机. 开收音机 "turn on the radio". Differs from 电台, the station, and 广播, the broadcast.
column4: 爷爷喜欢用收音机听新闻。
column5: 爺爺喜歡用收音機聽新聞。
column6: Yéye xǐhuan yòng shōuyīnjī tīng xīnwén.
column7: Grandpa likes to listen to the news on the radio.

column3: To record something: 录音 "record sound", 录像 "record video", 录取 "admit, enroll", 记录 "record, note down". It is mostly a part of compounds. It means to write down or capture.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè duàn huà lù xiàlai.
column7: Please record this passage.

column3: To record sound; a recording: 录 ("record") plus 音 ("sound"). A verb and its object: 录了音 "recorded". As a noun: 一段录音 "a recording". 听录音 "listen to a recording" is common in language classes. 录音机 is a tape recorder.
column6: Tīnglì kǎoshì yào xiān tīng lùyīn.
column7: In the listening exam, you listen to a recording first.

column3: Media: 媒 ("go-between") plus 体 ("body"). It covers news media as a whole: 新闻媒体 "news media", 社交媒体 "social media", 接受媒体采访 "be interviewed by the media". It is a collective noun, used with 各 and 很多.
column4: 这件事在社交媒体上很受关注。
column5: 這件事在社交媒體上很受關注。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì zài shèjiāo méitǐ shàng hěn shòu guānzhù.
column7: This matter gets a lot of attention on social media.

column3: To watch, to view, for something to look at as a show or an event: 观看比赛 "watch a match", 观看表演 "watch a performance", 观看电影. More formal than 看, it suggests an audience. 观 means "look at, view".
column4: 很多人到现场观看比赛。
column5: 很多人到現場觀看比賽。
column6: Hěn duō rén dào xiànchǎng guānkàn bǐsài.
column7: Many people came to watch the match on the spot.

column3: Audience, spectators: 观 ("watch") plus 众 ("crowd"). People who watch a show, a match or a film: 电视观众 "TV viewers", 现场观众 "live audience", 亲爱的观众朋友们 "dear viewers". For those who listen, use 听众. A collective, countable by 位, 名.
column6: Guānzhòngmen gěi yǎnyuán gǔzhǎng.
column7: The audience applauded the actors.

column3: Listeners, audience of radio, a talk or a concert: 听 ("listen") plus 众 ("crowd"). Pair with 观众 (people who watch). 亲爱的听众朋友们 "dear listeners". 听众来信 "letters from listeners".
column4: 主持人和听众一起聊天。
column5: 主持人和聽眾一起聊天。
column6: Zhǔchírén hé tīngzhòng yīqǐ liáotiān.
column7: The host chats with the listeners.

column3: To report, announce and also "newspaper": 报纸 "newspaper", 报告 "report", 报名 "sign up", 报警 "call the police", 报仇 "take revenge". The general sense is to let someone know or to give back.
column4: 我想去报名参加汉语班。
column5: 我想去報名參加漢語班。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng qù bàomíng cānjiā Hànyǔ bān.
column7: I want to sign up for the Chinese class.

column3: To report (news); a news report: 报 ("report") plus 道 ("say"). A verb with an object: 报道了这件事 "reported on this matter". Also a noun: 一篇报道 "a report", 新闻报道 "news report". The 道 here is read dào. Don't mix with 报到, "check in".
column4: 报纸上有一篇关于这件事的报道。
column5: 報紙上有一篇關於這件事的報道。
column6: Bàozhǐ shàng yǒu yī piān guānyú zhè jiàn shì de bàodào.
column7: There is a report about this matter in the newspaper.

column3: News, information, a piece of news you hear: 好消息 "good news", 坏消息 "bad news", 有消息吗? "any news?". It means a tidbit of news about someone or something, where 新闻 is public news on media. The 息 is light: xiāoxi.
column4: 我有一个好消息要告诉你。
column5: 我有一個好消息要告訴你。
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī ge hǎo xiāoxi yào gàosu nǐ.
column7: I have good news to tell you.

column3: To publicize, to promote; publicity: 宣传活动 "a promotion event", 宣传画 "poster", 做宣传 "do promotion". It can be advertising, public education or political propaganda, depending on the setting. A neutral word in business: 宣传新产品. 宣 means "declare" and 传 "spread".
column6: Gōngsī zhèngzài xuānchuán xīn chǎnpǐn.
column7: The company is promoting its new product.

column3: To spread, to disseminate: 传播知识 "spread knowledge", 传播消息 "spread news", 传播疾病 "spread disease". It is for things moving through people or the air, in a wide way. 传 ("pass on") plus 播 ("sow"). 传播得很快 is "spreads fast".
column4: 网络让消息传播得很快。
column5: 網路讓消息傳播得很快。
column6: Wǎngluò ràng xiāoxi chuánbō de hěn kuài.
column7: The internet lets news spread very fast.

column3: Match, competition; to compete: 参加比赛 "take part in a competition", 一场比赛 "a match", 比赛开始 "the match starts". As a verb: 两个队比赛 "two teams compete". Count with 场 for a match and 次 for events. 赛 is also in 决赛 "final".
column4: 今天下午有一场足球比赛。
column5: 今天下午有一場足球比賽。
column6: Jīntiān xiàwǔ yǒu yī chǎng zúqiú bǐsài.
column7: There is a soccer match this afternoon.

column3: Final of a competition: 决 ("decide") plus 赛 ("match"). 进入决赛 "reach the final", 决赛 is the match that decides the winner. Before it come 预赛 "preliminaries" and 半决赛 "semi-final".
column6: Wǒmen de duì jìnrù le juésài.
column7: Our team has reached the final.

column3: The World Cup, football's, held every four years: 世界 ("world") plus 杯 ("cup"). 看世界杯 "watch the World Cup", 世界杯比赛. A proper name, so it's capitalized in pinyin. 杯 is also "cup, glass" for drinks, so the word shows a trophy as a cup.
column4: 四年一次的世界杯又要开始了。
column5: 四年一次的世界杯又要開始了。
column6: Sì nián yī cì de Shìjièbēi yòu yào kāishǐ le.
column7: The World Cup, held every four years, is about to start again.

column3: Football, soccer: 足 ("foot") plus 球 ("ball"), both the game and the ball. 踢足球 "play soccer" uses 踢 "to kick", not 打. 足球比赛 "a soccer match", 一个足球 "a soccer ball". The 王 radical of 球 is jade, shared with other round things.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù tī zúqiú.
column7: We are going to play soccer this weekend.

column3: Fan of ball games: 球 ("ball") plus 迷 ("fan, enthusiast"). 足球迷 "soccer fan", 他是球迷. 迷 is also used as a suffix in other words, such as 歌迷 "music fan" and 影迷 "film buff". It means devoted fan.
column4: 很多球迷来到现场看比赛。
column5: 很多球迷來到現場看比賽。
column6: Hěn duō qiúmí láidào xiànchǎng kàn bǐsài.
column7: Many fans came to the scene to watch the match.

column3: To run, to jog: 跑 ("run") plus 步 ("step"). A verb and its object, so extra words come between: 跑了一会儿步, 跑过步. 去公园跑步 "go jogging in the park". For running as a sport, 赛跑 "race". 早上跑步 is a typical routine.
column4: 我每天早上去公园跑步。
column5: 我每天早上去公園跑步。
column6: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
column7: I go jogging in the park every morning.

column3: To take a walk, to stroll: 散 ("scatter, loosen") plus 步 ("step"). A verb and its object: 散散步, 散了一会儿步. After a meal, 饭后散步 is a common habit. Here 散 is read sàn, not sǎn. A relaxed walk, not a hike.
column4: 晚饭后，我们在河边散步。
column5: 晚飯後，我們在河邊散步。
column6: Wǎnfàn hòu, wǒmen zài hé biān sànbù.
column7: After dinner, we take a walk by the river.

column3: To swim and "to travel, to tour": 游泳 "swim", 游客 "tourist", 游戏 "game", 旅游 "travel". Mostly appears in compounds. The 氵 shows water, for swimming.
column6: Háizimen zài hé lǐ yóu.
column7: The children swim in the river.

column3: To swim: 游 ("swim") plus 泳 ("swim"). A verb and its object: 游了泳, 游过泳, 去游泳 "go swimming". 游泳池 is a "swimming pool". The word for the stroke: 蛙泳 "breaststroke". Both characters have the 氵 water radical.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ chángcháng qù yóuyǒng.
column7: In summer I often go swimming.

column3: To row a boat: 划 ("row, paddle") plus 船 ("boat"). A verb and its object: 划了船, 去划船. Here 划 is read huá. As "to plan" 划 is huà (计划). A pleasure activity on a lake or river: 在湖上划船. 划 for "cut" is also huá.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù hú shàng huáchuán.
column7: At the weekend we go rowing on the lake.

column3: High jump: 跳 ("jump") plus 高 ("high"). A track-and-field event; 跳远 is the long jump. It's a verb and object, as in 跳高比赛 "high jump competition", and 他跳高跳得很好. The 足 radical on the left of 跳 shows foot action.
column6: Tā shì xuéxiào de tiàogāo guànjūn.
column7: He is the school's high jump champion.

column3: Long jump: 跳 ("jump") plus 远 ("far"). A track-and-field event, the pair of 跳高. 跳远比赛 "long jump contest", 立定跳远 "standing long jump", which is a school fitness test in China.
column6: Wǒ tiàoyuǎn tiào le wǔ mǐ.
column7: I jumped five meters in the long jump.

column3: Gold, also "metal, money": 黄金 "gold", 金牌 "gold medal", 金色 "golden color", 现金 "cash". It is also the surname Jin. As a radical it appears as 钅 on the left in 钱, 银 and 铁, all metals and money.
column6: Zhè tiáo xiàngliàn shì jīn zuò de.
column7: This necklace is made of gold.

column3: Gold medal: 金 ("gold") plus 牌 ("medal, plate"). 拿金牌 / 得金牌 "win a gold medal", 一块金牌. Next come 银牌 and 铜牌. Used for sport results and, figuratively, for the best: 金牌教练 "top coach".
column4: 中国队在比赛中拿了十块金牌。
column5: 中國隊在比賽中拿了十塊金牌。
column6: Zhōngguó duì zài bǐsài zhōng ná le shí kuài jīnpái.
column7: The Chinese team won ten gold medals in the competition.

column3: Silver: 银子 "silver", 银行 "bank", 银色 "silver color", 银牌 "silver medal". Silver was once money, which is why 银 appears in the word for bank 银行. The 钅 on the left is the metal radical. The 艮 gives the sound.
column6: Zhège shǒuzhuó shì yín zuò de.
column7: This bracelet is made of silver.

column3: Silver medal: 银 ("silver") plus 牌 ("medal"). 拿到银牌 "win silver", 一块银牌. Second place in a sporting event. Together with 金牌 and 铜牌 (bronze), it makes the set of medals.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng dé le yínpái.
column7: He won a silver medal in the competition.

column3: To score; a score: 得 ("get") plus 分 ("point"). A verb and its object, so 得了分 and 得了十分 "scored ten points". In a game: 他得了三十分 "he scored thirty points". Here 得 is read dé, and 分 is fēn.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng défēn zuì duō.
column7: He scored the most points in the game.

column3: To lose a game or bet: 输了比赛 "lost the match", 我输了 "I lost". The opposite is 赢. It's not for losing a thing: that is 丢. In 输入 it means "to input", from the sense of "send": 输入密码 "enter a password".
column6: Wǒmen duì shū le zhè chǎng bǐsài.
column7: Our team lost this match.

column3: To win: 赢了比赛 "won the match", 我们赢了. It is about beating an opponent or winning a bet. Its pair is 输. 赢 is used for the winner, 胜 for the result.
column6: Wǒmen duì yíng le zhè chǎng bǐsài.
column7: Our team won this match.

column3: To win; to beat: 胜利 "victory", 胜负 "win or loss", 战胜 "defeat, overcome", 取胜 "win". It is more written than 赢, and it often appears in compounds. 胜 can also mean "better than" in written style.
column6: Wǒmen duì yǐ sān bǐ yī qǔshèng.
column7: Our team won by three to one.

column3: Victory; to win: 取得胜利 "achieve victory", 胜利了 "we won". It is a success in a fight, a competition or a hard task: 比赛胜利, 战争胜利, 工作的胜利. Where 赢 is the plain verb, 胜利 is the grand noun. Also used as "success" in speeches.
column4: 经过努力，我们终于取得了胜利。
column5: 經過努力，我們終於取得了勝利。
column6: Jīngguò nǔlì, wǒmen zhōngyú qǔdé le shènglì.
column7: After hard work, we finally won.

column3: Ranking; to rank: 排 ("arrange") plus 名 ("name, place"). As a noun, your place in a list: 排名第三 "ranked third", 世界排名 "world ranking", 成绩排名 "grade ranking". As a verb it takes the place first: 他排名第一. Used for school, sports and company lists.
column4: 他的成绩在班里排名第三。
column5: 他的成績在班裡排名第三。
column6: Tā de chéngjì zài bān lǐ páimíng dì sān.
column7: His grades rank third in the class.

column3: Coach, trainer: 足球教练 "soccer coach", 驾驶教练 "driving instructor". 教 ("teach") plus 练 ("practice"). Here 教 is read jiào, as in 教练, and the person is called with 位 or 名. It also works as a verb, "to coach", but the noun is the common use.
column4: 教练要求我们每天跑五公里。
column5: 教練要求我們每天跑五公里。
column6: Jiàoliàn yāoqiú wǒmen měitiān pǎo wǔ gōnglǐ.
column7: The coach asks us to run five kilometers every day.

column3: Contestant, athlete: 选 ("choose") plus 手 ("person skilled at"). A person who has been picked to compete: 参赛选手 "competitor", 运动选手 "athlete", 种子选手 "seeded player". 手 as a suffix names a person with a skill, as in 歌手 and 水手.
column6: Měi yī wèi xuǎnshǒu dōu hěn nǔlì.
column7: Every contestant is working hard.

column3: Team member: 队 ("team") plus 员 ("member"). Someone on a team: 足球队员 "soccer team member", 队员们 "the team". Also the 队长 is the captain. 员 as a suffix names a person in a role, as in 演员 and 学员.
column6: Duìyuánmen zhèngzài liànxí chuánqiú.
column7: The team members are practicing passing.

column3: Opponent, rival: 对 ("opposite") plus 手 ("person"). 比赛的对手 "opponent in a game", 强大的对手 "a strong rival". It can also be a worthy match: 他不是你的对手 "he is no match for you". Neutral, without hatred.
column4: 这次比赛，我们的对手很强。
column5: 這次比賽，我們的對手很強。
column6: Zhè cì bǐsài, wǒmen de duìshǒu hěn qiáng.
column7: In this match, our opponent is strong.

column3: To lead, to be ahead: 领 ("lead") plus 先 ("first"). In a race or a game: 领先一分 "lead by a point", 暂时领先 "temporarily in front". Also for companies and technology: 技术领先 "technologically leading". The opposite is 落后.
column6: Wǒmen duì zànshí lǐngxiān sān fēn.
column7: Our team temporarily leads by three points.

column3: To fall behind; backward: 落 ("fall") plus 后 ("behind"). In a race or in progress: 落后一步 "one step behind", 不要落后 "don't fall behind". As an adjective, "backward, undeveloped": 落后的地区. The opposite is 领先.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng luòhòu le.
column7: He fell behind in the race.

column3: Martial arts: 武 ("martial") plus 术 ("art, skill"). Traditional Chinese fighting arts, such as 太极拳 and 少林功夫: 学武术 "learn martial arts", 武术比赛. 术 is the "skill", as in 艺术 "art" and 美术 "fine art".
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo xué wǔshù.
column7: He has studied martial arts since childhood.

column3: Weapon: 武 ("martial") plus 器 ("tool, instrument"). 一件武器 "a weapon", 使用武器 "use weapons", 核武器 "nuclear weapons". Also figuratively: 语言是最好的武器. 器 is also in 机器 "machine" and 容器 "container".
column6: Jǐngchá méiyǒu dài wǔqì.
column7: The police did not carry weapons.

column3: Singing voice, sound of singing: 歌 ("song") plus 声 ("voice"). It is the sound of someone singing: 美妙的歌声 "lovely singing", 听到歌声 "hear singing". About the voice, where 歌 is the song.
column4: 我听到了从房间里传来的歌声。
column5: 我聽到了從房間裡傳來的歌聲。
column6: Wǒ tīngdào le cóng fángjiān lǐ chuánlái de gēshēng.
column7: I heard singing coming from the room.

column3: Singer: 歌 ("song") plus 手 ("one skilled at"). A professional or popular singer: 流行歌手 "pop singer", 著名歌手 "famous singer". For someone who simply sings, you can say 唱歌的人. The suffix 手 is also in 选手.
column4: 她是一位很有名的歌手。
column5: 她是一位很有名的歌手。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi hěn yǒumíng de gēshǒu.
column7: She is a very famous singer.

column3: Fan of a singer: 歌 ("song") plus 迷 ("fan"). Common in the news: 歌迷见面会 "fan meeting", 他是她的歌迷 "he is her fan". Like 球迷 and 影迷, the 迷 names someone who is hooked on a thing.
column4: 很多歌迷来听她的演唱会。
column5: 很多歌迷來聽她的演唱會。
column6: Hěn duō gēmí lái tīng tā de yǎnchànghuì.
column7: Many fans came to hear her concert.

column3: To perform a song: 演 ("perform") plus 唱 ("sing"). A formal word of stage singing: 演唱歌曲 "sing a song on stage", 演唱者 "the performer". Where 唱 is any singing, 演唱 is performing before an audience. Often in the program: 演唱：王小明.
column6: Tā jiāng yǎnchàng yī shǒu xīn gē.
column7: She will sing a new song.

column3: Concert of a singer or group: 演唱 ("perform a song") plus 会 ("meeting"). 开演唱会 "hold a concert", 去演唱会 "go to a concert", 演唱会门票 "concert tickets". For classical music, 音乐会 is the usual word.
column4: 我买了两张演唱会的票。
column5: 我買了兩張演唱會的票。
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng yǎnchànghuì de piào.
column7: I bought two tickets to the concert.

column3: Band, orchestra: 乐 ("music") plus 队 ("team"). A group of musicians: 摇滚乐队 "rock band", 学校乐队 "school band". Here 乐 is read yuè, "music", not lè. Count with 支 and 个.
column4: 他在一个乐队里弹吉他。
column5: 他在一個樂隊裡彈吉他。
column6: Tā zài yī ge yuèduì lǐ tán jítā.
column7: He plays guitar in a band.

column3: To perform, to act: 演戏 "act in a play", 演电影 "act in a film", 演出 "performance", 演员 "actor". It is also "to develop" in 演变. It is something shown to an audience.
column4: 她在这部电影里演一个老师。
column5: 她在這部電影裡演一個老師。
column6: Tā zài zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǎn yī ge lǎoshī.
column7: She plays a teacher in this film.

column3: Actor, actress, performer: 演 ("perform") plus 员 ("member"). It is gender-neutral: 电影演员 "film actor", 一位演员. To say it is a woman, 女演员. Also for any performer on a stage.
column6: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán yǎn de hěn hǎo.
column7: This actor performs very well.

column3: Director of a film or play, and "to direct": 电影导演 "film director", 他导演了这部电影 "he directed this film". 导 ("guide") plus 演 ("perform"). Count with 位 or 名.
column4: 这位导演拍了很多好电影。
column5: 這位導演拍了很多好電影。
column6: Zhè wèi dǎoyǎn pāi le hěn duō hǎo diànyǐng.
column7: This director has made many good films.

column3: Performance; to perform: 演 ("perform") plus 出 ("out"). A show for an audience: 一场演出 "a performance", 演出时间 "show time", 参加演出, 演出开始. As a verb, 他们在剧场演出. It covers plays, concerts and dances.
column6: Jīnwǎn de yǎnchū bā diǎn kāishǐ.
column7: Tonight's performance starts at eight.

column3: To perform; a performance: 表 ("show") plus 演 ("act"). A show of a skill: 表演节目 "put on an act", 精彩的表演 "a brilliant performance", 表演魔术 "do a magic trick". More general than 演出, with the stress on showing something.
column4: 孩子们给大家表演了一个节目。
column5: 孩子們給大家表演了一個節目。
column6: Háizimen gěi dàjiā biǎoyǎn le yī ge jiémù.
column7: The children put on an act for everyone.

column3: Stage: 舞 ("dance") plus 台 ("platform"). The platform in a theater: 站在舞台上 "stand on the stage", 舞台灯光 "stage lighting". Also figuratively, a place to show one's talent: 国际舞台 "the world stage".
column4: 她第一次站在大舞台上。
column5: 她第一次站在大舞臺上。
column6: Tā dì yī cì zhàn zài dà wǔtái shàng.
column7: She is standing on a big stage for the first time.

column3: Stage play in the spoken, modern sense: 话 ("speech") plus 剧 ("drama"). It is a play with dialogue and no singing, which differs from 京剧 or other sung opera. 看话剧 "see a play", 一部话剧.
column4: 周末我们去剧场看话剧。
column5: 週末我們去劇場看話劇。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù jùchǎng kàn huàjù.
column7: At the weekend we are going to the theater to see a play.

column3: Beijing opera, the famous musical theater with painted faces, singing and acrobatics. 京 stands for Beijing. 听京剧 "listen to Beijing opera", 京剧演员. Count with 出 for a play: 一出京剧. A proper name in the list, so capitalized in pinyin.
column6: Yéye hěn xǐhuan tīng Jīngjù.
column7: Grandpa loves listening to Beijing opera.

column3: Theater as a building: 剧 ("drama") plus 场 ("place"). A place for plays and shows: 在剧场看演出 "see a show in a theater". For films the place is 电影院. Count with 家 or 个.
column4: 这个剧场可以坐一千人。
column5: 這個劇場可以坐一千人。
column6: Zhège jùchǎng kěyǐ zuò yī qiān rén.
column7: This theater can seat a thousand people.

column3: Game; to play: 玩游戏 "play games", 电脑游戏 "computer game", 游戏机 "game console". As a noun it covers video games and children's games. 游 ("roam") plus 戏 ("play"). Not for sports games: those are 比赛.
column4: 孩子们在院子里玩游戏。
column5: 孩子們在院子裡玩遊戲。
column6: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ wán yóuxì.
column7: The children are playing games in the yard.

column3: Fan, enthusiast and "to be fascinated, to be lost": 球迷 "ball game fan", 迷路 "get lost", 迷上 "become hooked on", 着迷 "be captivated". As a suffix after a noun it names the fan. The 辶 radical on the left gives the sense of walking, which suits getting lost.
column6: Tā mí shàng le dǎ lánqiú.
column7: He has become hooked on playing basketball.

column3: A measure word for long, thin things such as pens (一支笔), and for teams and songs (一支队伍, 一支歌). It also means "to support" and "to prop up": 支持 "support", 支付 "pay". As a measure word, it is written and slightly more formal than 根 for sticks. Read zhī.
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī zhī xīn de gāngbǐ.
column7: I have a new fountain pen.

column3: Read zhī it is the measure word for most animals and for one of a pair: 一只猫 "a cat", 一只鸟 "a bird", 一只手 "one hand". Also for boats and some containers. Read zhǐ it means "only". The two are the same character in simplified, so context decides. The traditional measure word is 隻.
column6: Shù shàng yǒu yī zhī niǎo.
column7: There is a bird in the tree.

column3: Read zhǒng it is a measure word for kinds: 一种水果 "a kind of fruit", 各种各样 "all kinds". It also means "seed" (种子). Read zhòng, the verb "to plant": 种花 "plant flowers". For this list the kind/measure-word use matters most.
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ hěn tián.
column7: This kind of fruit is very sweet.

column3: A measure word for pairs: 一双鞋 "a pair of shoes", 一双筷子 "a pair of chopsticks", 一双手 "a pair of hands". Also "two, double": 双人床 "double bed", 双方 "both sides".
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī shuāng xīn xié.
column7: I bought a new pair of shoes.

column3: A measure word for bundles and things tied together: 一束花 "a bunch of flowers", 一束光 "a beam of light". As a verb "to bind": 约束 "restrain", and 结束 "to end". Read shù.
column6: Tā sònggěi wǒ yī shù huā.
column7: He gave me a bouquet of flowers.

column3: A measure word for crowds and flocks: 一群人 "a group of people", 一群鸟 "a flock of birds", 一群孩子. Also a noun "group": 人群, and 微信群 "WeChat group". It is used for living things together, and not for a few of them: for two or three, use 几个.
column6: Yī qún háizi zài gōngyuán lǐ wán.
column7: A group of children are playing in the park.

column3: A measure word for things with a frame or wings: 一架飞机 "an airplane", 一架钢琴 "a piano", 一架相机. As a noun "frame, rack": 书架. As a verb, "to prop up". The 木 at the bottom means "wooden frame". Flying machines are counted with 架.
column6: Tiān shàng fēiguò yī jià fēijī.
column7: An airplane flew across the sky.

column3: A measure word for films, books and machines: 一部电影 "a film", 一部手机 "a phone", 一部小说 "a novel". As a noun, "part, department": 北部, 外交部 "foreign ministry", 部分 "part". It is used for works made as a whole, which come in a complete form.
column4: 我昨天看了一部好电影。
column5: 我昨天看了一部好電影。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān kàn le yī bù hǎo diànyǐng.
column7: Yesterday I watched a good film.

column3: Step: 一步 "one step", 走一步 "take a step", 进步 "progress", 步行 "go on foot". As a measure word, it counts steps in a plan: 第一步 "the first step".
column4: 我们一步一步往山上走。
column5: 我們一步一步往山上走。
column6: Wǒmen yī bù yī bù wǎng shān shàng zǒu.
column7: We walked up the mountain one step at a time.

column3: Generation, era: 年轻一代 "the younger generation", 现代 "modern times", 古代 "ancient times". As a measure word, "generation": 三代人 "three generations". Also "to replace": 代替 "replace", 代表 "represent". The 亻 on the left is "person".
column6: Sān dài rén zhù zài yīqǐ.
column7: Three generations live together.

column3: Group, team, organization: 旅行团 "tour group", 代表团 "delegation", 团队 "team", 团圆 "reunion". As a measure word for a round mass: 一团毛线 "a ball of wool". Also the Communist Youth League, 共青团.
column4: 我们参加了一个去北京的旅行团。
column5: 我們參加了一個去北京的旅行團。
column6: Wǒmen cānjiā le yī ge qù Běijīng de lǚxíngtuán.
column7: We joined a tour group to Beijing.

column3: Everyone, ladies and gentlemen: 各 ("each") plus 位 ("person, polite measure word"). A polite way to address a group: 各位同学 "dear students", 各位来宾 "dear guests". It opens speeches and announcements. Not used for a single person.
column6: Gèwèi péngyou, dàjiā hǎo!
column7: Hello, friends, everyone!

column3: Quantity, amount: 数 ("count") plus 量 ("measure"). It is how much or how many there are: 数量很多 "a large quantity", 控制数量 "limit the amount", 数量和质量 "quantity and quality". Here 数 is read shù.
column4: 这里的车数量越来越多。
column5: 這裡的車數量越來越多。
column6: Zhèlǐ de chē shùliàng yuè lái yuè duō.
column7: The number of cars here keeps growing.

column3: Renminbi, RMB, the currency of China; the unit is the 元 (also called 块 in speech). 人民 ("the people") plus 币 ("currency"). 一百元人民币 "one hundred yuan RMB". Short written form: ¥ or RMB. Proper name of a currency, counted by 元.
column4: 这个多少钱？一百块人民币。
column5: 這個多少錢？一百塊人民幣。
column6: Zhège duōshao qián? Yī bǎi kuài rénmínbì.
column7: How much is this? One hundred RMB.

column3: US dollar: 美 (short for 美国) plus 元 ("yuan, currency unit"). 一百美元 "a hundred dollars", 美元汇率 "the dollar exchange rate". Other currencies follow the same plan: 欧元 "euro", 日元 "yen". 换美元 "change dollars".
column4: 我想把美元换成人民币。
column5: 我想把美元換成人民幣。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ měiyuán huàn chéng rénmínbì.
column7: I'd like to change dollars into RMB.

column3: Cash: 现 ("present, ready") plus 金 ("money"). 付现金 "pay in cash", 带现金 "bring cash", 现金支付 "cash payment". The opposite is 刷卡 "pay by card" or 手机支付 "mobile payment". Here 金 means money, not gold.
column6: Qǐngwèn kěyǐ fù xiànjīn ma?
column7: Excuse me, can I pay in cash?

column3: Price: 价 ("price") plus 格 ("standard"). The formal word: 价格高 "high price", 价格便宜, 价格表 "price list", 降低价格 "lower the price". Where 价钱 is spoken, 价格 is used in shops, business and news.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de jiàgé hěn hélǐ.
column7: The prices in this shop are very reasonable.

column3: Price, the spoken word: 价钱贵 "pricey", 讲价钱 "haggle", 这个价钱怎么样? "what do you think of this price?". 价 ("price") plus 钱 ("money"). Slightly more casual than 价格. The 钱 has a light tone: jiàqian.
column4: 这个价钱太贵了，便宜一点吧。
column5: 這個價錢太貴了，便宜一點吧。
column6: Zhège jiàqian tài guì le, piányi yīdiǎn ba.
column7: This price is too high, make it cheaper.

column3: Two words share this character. As a measure word for machines: 一台电脑 "a computer", 一台洗衣机 "a washing machine". And "platform, stage": 舞台 "stage", 阳台 "balcony", 讲台 "podium", 电视台 "TV station". In traditional characters the platform is usually 臺 and the measure word 台; Taiwan, 臺灣, is also written 台灣.
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng tái diànnǎo.
column7: My home has two computers.

column3: Actually, in fact: 其实 introduces a fact that differs from what was thought or said: 其实我不饿 "actually I'm not hungry". It usually opens a clause and contrasts with the previous remark. It is softer than 事实上.
column4: 他看起来很凶，其实很温柔。
column5: 他看起來很兇，其實很溫柔。
column6: Tā kàn qǐlái hěn xiōng, qíshí hěn wēnróu.
column7: He looks fierce, but actually he is gentle.

column3: In fact, as a matter of fact: 事实 ("fact") plus 上 ("in terms of"). It brings up the real situation, often against an assumption: 事实上，他并没有去。 It is more formal and more emphatic than 其实, and also usually begins the clause.
column4: 大家都以为他会来，事实上他没有来。
column5: 大家都以為他會來，事實上他沒有來。
column6: Dàjiā dōu yǐwéi tā huì lái, shìshíshàng tā méiyǒu lái.
column7: Everyone thought he would come, but in fact he didn't.

column3: In fact, actually, in reality: 实际 ("reality") plus 上 ("in terms of"). It is a contrast with how things look or what was said: 实际上，工作比看起来难 "in reality, the job is harder than it looks". Close to 事实上, with a focus on practice.
column4: 这件事看起来很容易，实际上很难。
column5: 這件事看起來很容易，實際上很難。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì kàn qǐlái hěn róngyì, shíjìshàng hěn nán.
column7: This looks easy, but in reality it is hard.

column3: Fact: 一个事实 "a fact", 这是事实 "that is the fact", 事实证明 "facts prove". It is what is really the case, against opinion: 尊重事实, 与事实不符 "doesn't match the facts". 事实 is a noun that follows 是.
column4: 这是一个不能改变的事实。
column5: 這是一個不能改變的事實。
column6: Zhè shì yī ge bù néng gǎibiàn de shìshí.
column7: This is a fact that cannot be changed.

column3: Of course, naturally: 当然可以 "of course you can", 当然不 "of course not". It is a reply that shows something is obvious. It also works as an adverb inside a sentence: 他当然知道 "of course he knows". 当 here means "ought" and 然 "so".
column6: Nǐ míngtiān lái ma? Dāngrán lái!
column7: Are you coming tomorrow? Of course!

column3: As expected, sure enough: 果 ("fruit, result") plus 然 ("so"). It says that what was predicted turned out true: 天气预报说会下雨，果然下雨了 "the forecast said rain, and sure enough it rained". It does not suit a surprise; for that use 竟然.
column4: 他说会下雨，果然下雨了。
column5: 他說會下雨，果然下雨了。
column6: Tā shuō huì xià yǔ, guǒrán xià yǔ le.
column7: He said it would rain, and sure enough it rained.

column3: Obviously, clearly: 显 ("show") plus 然 ("so"). It is used when the evidence is plain: 显然他生气了 "he was obviously angry", 显然不对 "obviously wrong". Written and more formal than 明显, which is an adjective.
column4: 他显然没有听懂我的话。
column5: 他顯然沒有聽懂我的話。
column6: Tā xiǎnrán méiyǒu tīngdǒng wǒ de huà.
column7: He obviously did not understand what I said.

column3: Indeed, really, truly: 确 ("sure") plus 实 ("real"). It confirms that something is true, often agreeing with a remark: 确实很好 "really good", 他确实来过 "he really did come". As an adjective it means "reliable": 确实的消息.
column4: 这家饭馆的菜确实很好吃。
column5: 這家飯館的菜確實很好吃。
column6: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài quèshí hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is indeed tasty.

column3: At all, simply (in negatives) and "basic; root": 根本不知道 "doesn't know at all", 根本没有 "there's none at all". It strengthens a negative. As a noun: 根本问题 "the fundamental problem". The 根 is "root". The negative sense is usually the one heard.
column6: Wǒ gēnběn bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.
column7: I don't know about this matter at all.

column3: Simply, virtually: 简直太好了 "simply wonderful", 简直不敢相信 "I simply can't believe it". It exaggerates, to say that something is almost or just like another thing. It is a spoken, emphatic adverb that goes before the verb or adjective.
column4: 这里的风景简直像画一样。
column5: 這裡的風景簡直像畫一樣。
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng jiǎnzhí xiàng huà yīyàng.
column7: The scenery here is simply like a painting.

column3: Absolutely; absolute: as an adverb: 绝对不行 "absolutely not", 绝对正确 "absolutely right". As an adjective: 绝对的 "absolute". It stresses strongly that there is no doubt. In negatives it states a firm refusal.
column4: 这件事绝对不能告诉别人。
column5: 這件事絕對不能告訴別人。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì juéduì bù néng gàosu biérén.
column7: You absolutely must not tell anyone about this.

column3: Could it be that…?, used for a rhetorical question that shows surprise or doubt: 难道你不知道吗? "Don't tell me you don't know?" It goes before the verb and the question ends with 吗 or 不成. The sentence expects a "no, surely not".
column4: 难道你不知道今天放假吗？
column5: 難道你不知道今天放假嗎？
column6: Nándào nǐ bù zhīdào jīntiān fàngjià ma?
column7: Don't tell me you didn't know it's a holiday today?

column3: I'm afraid that, probably: 恐 ("fear") plus 怕 ("afraid"). A polite way to give bad news or a guess: 恐怕来不及了 "I'm afraid it's too late", 恐怕不行 "I'm afraid it won't do". It shows concern, not fear itself. It is placed before the verb.
column4: 已经八点了，恐怕来不及了。
column5: 已經八點了，恐怕來不及了。
column6: Yǐjīng bā diǎn le, kǒngpà lái bu jí le.
column7: It's already eight, I'm afraid we won't make it.

column3: Anyway, in any case: 反正都一样 "it's all the same anyway", 反正我不去 "anyway, I'm not going". It says that whatever happens, the result won't change, and often sounds a bit carefree or stubborn. It goes after the subject, before the verb, and is a spoken word.
column4: 你别问了，反正我不会去。
column5: 你別問了，反正我不會去。
column6: Nǐ bié wèn le, fǎnzhèng wǒ bù huì qù.
column7: Stop asking, I'm not going anyway.

column3: Basically, on the whole: 基本 ("basic") plus 上 ("in terms of"). It says something is mostly true, with small exceptions: 基本上同意 "basically agree", 基本上完成了 "mostly finished". The 上 is light, so say jīběnshang. It makes a statement less absolute.
column4: 这件事基本上已经解决了。
column5: 這件事基本上已經解決了。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì jīběnshang yǐjīng jiějué le.
column7: This matter has basically been resolved.

column3: Probably, approximately: as an adverb 他大概不来了 "he probably won't come"; with numbers 大概三十个人 "about thirty people". As a noun, "general idea": 大概的意思. It is a hedge: it admits you don't know exactly. 大约 is close, and 大概 is more spoken.
column6: Tā dàgài liù diǎn huílái.
column7: He will probably be back around six.

column3: About, approximately: 大约三点 "around three o'clock", 大约五十人 "about fifty people". It goes before the number or time word. It can also mean "probably" in writing: 他大约不会来. Where 大概 is spoken, 大约 is a little more written.
column4: 从这里到机场大约要一个小时。
column5: 從這裡到機場大約要一個小時。
column6: Cóng zhèlǐ dào jīchǎng dàyuē yào yī ge xiǎoshí.
column7: It takes about an hour from here to the airport.

column3: Inevitable; inevitably: 必 ("surely") plus 然 ("so"). As an adjective: 必然的结果 "an inevitable result". As an adverb: 必然会 "will necessarily". It says something follows by necessity: 努力必然会有回报. Written and a bit abstract. Pair with 偶然 "by chance".
column4: 只要努力，就必然会进步。
column5: 只要努力，就必然會進步。
column6: Zhǐyào nǔlì, jiù bìrán huì jìnbù.
column7: As long as you work hard, you will surely progress.

column3: Quite, fairly, considerably: 相当好 "quite good", 相当多 "a good many", 相当不错. It goes before an adjective and means more than 比较 but less than 非常. As a verb it means "to be equal to": 相当于 "equivalent to".
column4: 这家饭馆的菜相当不错。
column5: 這家飯館的菜相當不錯。
column6: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài xiāngdāng bùcuò.
column7: The food in this restaurant is quite good.

column3: Extremely, added after an adjective or a feeling verb: 好极了 "wonderful", 累极了 "exhausted", 高兴极了 "overjoyed". It is spoken and always comes after what it intensifies, with no 很 in front: not 很好极了. It stands for a strong reaction. The 了 is light: jíle.
column6: Jīntiān de tiānqì hǎo jíle.
column7: The weather today is wonderful.

column3: After all, on earth, in a question that pushes for the real answer: 你到底想做什么? "What on earth do you want to do?", 到底是谁? "who is it really?". Also "in the end, after all" in statements: 他到底来了 "he came after all". It stresses getting to the bottom of things.
column6: Nǐ dàodǐ xiǎng chī shénme?
column7: What on earth do you want to eat?

column3: Almost, nearly: 将近三个小时 "almost three hours", 将近一百人 "close to a hundred people". It goes before a number and says the figure is just short of it. 将 ("be about to") plus 近 ("near"). The 将 is read jiāng.
column6: Tā děng le jiāngjìn liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
column7: He waited for nearly two hours.

column3: Two uses: "ten million" (千万人), and in warnings "must by all means": 千万别忘了 "be sure not to forget", 千万不要 "whatever you do, don't". The second use is a strong plea and goes before 别, 不要 or 要. It cannot be used for ordinary numbers like 一千万 in this way.
column6: Míngtiān qiānwàn bié chídào.
column7: Whatever you do, don't be late tomorrow.

column3: About, approximately: 约三十人 "about thirty people", 约一个小时 "about an hour". Written, it goes before the number. It also means "to make an appointment": 约朋友 "invite a friend", 约好 "arrange", and "agreement" (条约 "treaty").
column4: 我约了朋友明天一起吃饭。
column5: 我約了朋友明天一起吃飯。
column6: Wǒ yuē le péngyou míngtiān yīqǐ chīfàn.
column7: I've arranged to have a meal with a friend tomorrow.

column3: At least: 至 ("reach") plus 少 ("few"). It goes before a number or amount, giving a minimum: 至少三个 "at least three", 至少要一个小时. The pair is 最多 "at most". It can also say "at the very least": 至少你应该道歉.
column4: 这件事至少要一个星期才能做完。
column5: 這件事至少要一個星期才能做完。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì zhìshǎo yào yī ge xīngqī cái néng zuò wán.
column7: This will take at least a week to finish.

column3: Always; in total: 总是 "always", 总共 "altogether", 总会 "will certainly (in the end)", 总算 "at long last". Alone it means "total, overall": 总经理 "general manager". As an adverb it says something happens in every case or finally: 他总说… "he's always saying…".
column6: Nǐ zǒng huì chénggōng de.
column7: You will succeed in the end.

column3: Always: 他总是迟到 "he's always late". It says something keeps happening, with a touch of complaint or habit: 总是这样 "it's always like that". It goes before the verb. Close to 一直 but about repeated events, where 一直 is non-stop.
column4: 他总是第一个到办公室。
column5: 他總是第一個到辦公室。
column6: Tā zǒngshì dì yī ge dào bàngōngshì.
column7: He is always the first one at the office.

column3: Usually, normally: 通常我七点起床 "I usually get up at seven". It describes what generally happens and goes before the verb or at the start. It is a little more formal than 一般, and speaks about patterns, not a promise. The opposite is 偶尔 "occasionally".
column6: Wǒ tōngcháng zài jiā chī zǎofàn.
column7: I usually eat breakfast at home.

column3: Often, more often than not: it describes a pattern seen over time, with a result that tends to follow: 人们往往忽视小事 "people often overlook small things". It is not for a single event or for future or commands. It stresses the regularity: when A, B tends to follow.
column4: 周末，公园里往往有很多人。
column5: 週末，公園裡往往有很多人。
column6: Zhōumò, gōngyuán lǐ wǎngwǎng yǒu hěn duō rén.
column7: At weekends there are usually many people in the park.

column3: Always; never (with negatives): almost always used in a negative: 我从来不喝酒 "I never drink", 他从来没去过 "he has never been". It means "at all times up to now". Without a negative it appears in 从来都 "all along". It goes before the verb.
column6: Wǒ cónglái méiyǒu qù guo Shànghǎi.
column7: I have never been to Shanghai.

column3: All along, from start to finish: 始 ("begin") plus 终 ("end"). It describes an unchanged attitude or state through a period: 始终没有变 "never changed", 始终相信 "always believed". Written and a little firm.
column4: 他始终相信自己能成功。
column5: 他始終相信自己能成功。
column6: Tā shǐzhōng xiāngxìn zìjǐ néng chénggōng.
column7: He has always believed he could succeed.

column3: Continuously, constantly: 不 ("not") plus 断 ("break"), "without a break". 不断学习 "keep learning", 不断进步 "keep improving". It is an adverb before the verb, or an adjective in 不断的努力. Meaning repeating and going on.
column4: 我们要不断学习新东西。
column5: 我們要不斷學習新東西。
column6: Wǒmen yào bùduàn xuéxí xīn dōngxi.
column7: We must keep learning new things.

column3: Repeatedly, over and over: 反复练习 "practice repeatedly", 反复说 "say again and again". It is about doing the same thing several times. As a noun or a verb, it can mean "to go back and forth" (病情反复 "the illness comes back").
column4: 这个字我反复写了很多遍。
column5: 這個字我反覆寫了很多遍。
column6: Zhège zì wǒ fǎnfù xiě le hěn duō biàn.
column7: I wrote this character many times over.

column3: Still, yet, a written adverb: 仍在工作 "still working", 仍然 "still", 仍未 "has not yet". It says that a state goes on in spite of change. 仍 is short and mostly used with another word, 仍然 or 仍旧.
column4: 虽然下雨了，他仍在跑步。
column5: 雖然下雨了，他仍在跑步。
column6: Suīrán xià yǔ le, tā réng zài pǎobù.
column7: Though it rained, he was still running.

column3: Still, yet: 他仍然在这里 "he is still here". It says that the situation hasn't changed, often against expectation: 虽然…，仍然… "although… still…". Close to 还 and 依然, more written than 还. It goes before the verb.
column4: 很多年过去了，他仍然记得那天。
column5: 很多年過去了，他仍然記得那天。
column6: Hěn duō nián guòqù le, tā réngrán jìdé nà tiān.
column7: Many years have passed, and he still remembers that day.

column3: Continuously; in a row: 连续三天 "three days in a row", 连续下雨 "rain without a break". 连 ("link") plus 续 ("continue"). It describes events that come one after another: 电视连续剧. It puts the stress on succession, not on non-stop.
column4: 这个星期连续下了三天雨。
column5: 這個星期連續下了三天雨。
column6: Zhège xīngqī liánxù xià le sān tiān yǔ.
column7: It rained for three days in a row this week.

column3: To continue, to last: 持 ("hold") plus 续 ("continue"). It describes something that goes on over time, often a state or process: 持续下雨 "keep raining", 持续发展 "continue developing", 持续了三天. Written, for events that last.
column4: 这场大雨持续了一整天。
column5: 這場大雨持續了一整天。
column6: Zhè chǎng dà yǔ chíxù le yī zhěng tiān.
column7: The heavy rain lasted all day.

column3: To continue, to go on: 继续工作 "keep on working", 请继续 "please go on". It can take a verb or be used alone, and also restart after a pause: 休息一下再继续. 继 means "follow on".
column4: 休息一下，然后我们继续学习。
column5: 休息一下，然後我們繼續學習。
column6: Xiūxi yīxià, ránhòu wǒmen jìxù xuéxí.
column7: Let's rest a bit and then continue studying.

column3: Properly, well, carefully: 好好学习 "study hard", 好好休息 "have a good rest", 好好想想 "think it over properly". It goes before a verb and urges doing it thoroughly. Also in commands: 好好儿. The second 好 may be said in the first tone: hǎohāo.
column4: 你要好好休息，别太累了。
column5: 你要好好休息，別太累了。
column6: Nǐ yào hǎohǎo xiūxi, bié tài lèi le.
column7: Take a good rest and don't tire yourself out.

column3: Slowly, gradually: 慢慢走 "walk slowly", 慢慢来 "take your time", 慢慢地 "gradually". When someone leaves, 您慢走 is used, and 慢慢 can also mean gradually changing: 天慢慢黑了 "it gradually got dark". Like most doubled words, it can take 地 before the verb.
column6: Bié zháojí, mànmān shuō.
column7: Don't be anxious, speak slowly.

column3: As much as possible, to the best of one's ability: 尽量早点来 "come as early as you can", 尽量不要 "try not to". It goes before the verb. Read jǐnliàng, with 尽 in the third tone. It sets a limit on effort: do it to the extent you can.
column6: Míngtiān qǐng nǐ jǐnliàng zǎodiǎn lái.
column7: Please come as early as you can tomorrow.

column3: Personality, individuality: 个 ("individual") plus 性 ("nature"). It stresses what makes a person different: 他很有个性 "he has a strong personality", 个性鲜明 "a distinct character". It is often positive, meaning unique. Differs from 性格, which describes the type of character.
column4: 她是一个很有个性的人。
column5: 她是一個很有個性的人。
column6: Tā shì yī ge hěn yǒu gèxìng de rén.
column7: She is a person with a lot of personality.

column3: Character, personality: what kind of temperament someone has, such as 性格开朗 "cheerful", 性格内向 "introverted". 性 ("nature") plus 格 ("style"). Used to describe a person: 我的性格… Where 个性 is what makes one stand out, 性格 is the kind of person.
column6: Tā de xìnggé hěn kāilǎng.
column7: He has a cheerful character.

column3: As a suffix, it turns words into abstract nouns: 重要性 "importance", 可能性 "possibility", 积极性 "initiative", 灵活性 "flexibility". Alone it means "sex" or "nature": 性别, 个性. The 忄 on the left is the heart radical, for feelings, and 生 on the right gives the sound.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì de zhòngyàoxìng hěn dà.
column7: This matter is of great importance.

column3: Gender, sex: 性 ("sex") plus 别 ("difference"). It appears on forms: 性别：男/女. 性别平等 "gender equality", 性别不同. A neutral word for male or female status.
column4: 请在表格上填写你的性别。
column5: 請在表格上填寫你的性別。
column6: Qǐng zài biǎogé shàng tiánxiě nǐ de xìngbié.
column7: Please fill in your gender on the form.

column3: Strong, firm of character or will, in hard times: 坚强的人 "a strong person", 要坚强 "be strong", 坚强的意志 "strong will". 坚 ("firm") plus 强 ("strong"). Here 强 is read qiáng. It is about mental strength, not muscles.
column6: Tā hěn jiānqiáng, cónglái bù kū.
column7: She is strong and never cries.

column3: Firm, resolute: 坚决反对 "firmly oppose", 态度坚决 "a determined attitude", 坚决不去. It describes a decision not to be changed. As an adverb it goes before a verb of intent: 坚决要. 坚 ("firm") plus 决 ("decide").
column4: 他坚决不同意这个计划。
column5: 他堅決不同意這個計劃。
column6: Tā jiānjué bù tóngyì zhège jìhuà.
column7: He firmly disagrees with this plan.

column3: To dare: 不敢 "don't dare", 敢说 "dare to say", 你敢吗? "do you dare?". It goes before a verb: 他不敢一个人去 "he doesn't dare to go alone". Also in polite speech: 不敢当 "I don't deserve it". The negative 不敢 is the most common use.
column6: Wǒ bù gǎn yī ge rén zǒu yè lù.
column7: I don't dare to walk alone at night.

column3: Active, positive, proactive: 积极参加 "take part actively", 积极的态度 "positive attitude", 他很积极. It praises someone who takes initiative and pitches in. The opposite is 消极 "passive, negative".
column6: Tā duì xuéxí hěn jījí.
column7: He is very keen on studying.

column3: Optimistic: 乐 ("happy") plus 观 ("view"). 很乐观 "very optimistic", 乐观的人 "an optimist", 对未来乐观. The pair is 悲观 "pessimistic". Here 乐 is read lè, not yuè.
column4: 他是个乐观的人，总是笑着面对问题。
column5: 他是個樂觀的人，總是笑著面對問題。
column6: Tā shì ge lèguān de rén, zǒngshì xiào zhe miànduì wèntí.
column7: He is an optimist who always faces problems with a smile.

column3: Proactive, on one's own initiative: 主动帮忙 "offer help without being asked", 主动联系 "get in touch first". It describes acting without being told: 他很主动. The opposite is 被动 "passive". 主 ("main") plus 动 ("move").
column4: 他看到我拿东西，主动过来帮忙。
column5: 他看到我拿東西，主動過來幫忙。
column6: Tā kàndào wǒ ná dōngxi, zhǔdòng guòlái bāngmáng.
column7: Seeing me carry things, he came over to help on his own.

column3: Conscious, self-motivated: 自觉遵守 "observe by one's own accord", 很自觉 "very self-disciplined". It means acting right without being supervised. As a verb, "to be aware": 自觉不错. Read zìjué. Not "to wake by oneself".
column4: 他很自觉，不用别人提醒。
column5: 他很自覺，不用別人提醒。
column6: Tā hěn zìjué, bùyòng biérén tíxǐng.
column7: He is self-disciplined and needs no reminder.

column3: Warm, kind, friendly: 亲切的笑容 "a warm smile", 很亲切 "very kind", 感到亲切 "feel at home". It describes a person's manner or a feeling of closeness, as with a hometown accent: 听到乡音，觉得很亲切.
column6: Lǎoshī duì xuéshengmen hěn qīnqiè.
column7: The teacher is very kind to the students.

column3: Enthusiastic, warm: 热烈欢迎 "warmly welcome", 热烈的掌声 "warm applause", 气氛热烈. It describes a welcome, applause or a discussion with energy. 热 ("hot") plus 烈 ("fierce"). Written.
column4: 大家热烈地欢迎新同学。
column5: 大家熱烈地歡迎新同學。
column6: Dàjiā rèliè de huānyíng xīn tóngxué.
column7: Everyone gives the new student a warm welcome.

column3: Skillful; coincidentally: 手巧 "good with the hands", 巧克力 "chocolate" (a sound loanword), and the exclamation 真巧! "What a coincidence!". Also 碰巧 or 恰巧 "by chance". It is mostly used in set phrases.
column6: Zài zhèr yùdào nǐ, zhēn qiǎo!
column7: What a coincidence to run into you here!

column3: Great, grand: 伟大的人 "a great person", 伟大的作品 "a great work", 伟大的成就. It praises a person or achievement beyond the ordinary, with solemn respect. Not for a big size, which is 大.
column4: 他是一位伟大的科学家。
column5: 他是一位偉大的科學家。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi wěidà de kēxuéjiā.
column7: He is a great scientist.

column3: Mature; ripe: for fruit, 苹果成熟了 "the apples are ripe", and for people 他很成熟 "he is mature". Also for ideas and plans: 时机成熟 "the time is ripe". 成 ("become") plus 熟 ("ripe"). Here 熟 is read shú. For cooked food in speech, 熟 is often shóu.
column4: 这个孩子比同龄人成熟。
column5: 這個孩子比同齡人成熟。
column6: Zhège háizi bǐ tónglíngrén chéngshú.
column7: This child is more mature than others his age.

column3: Reliable, dependable: 可 ("can") plus 靠 ("rely on"). For people and for things or news: 可靠的朋友 "a dependable friend", 消息可靠 "the news is reliable". The opposite is 不可靠. 靠 is "lean on" and appears alone in 靠近 "near".
column6: Tā shì yī ge hěn kěkào de rén.
column7: He is a very reliable person.

column3: True, real, genuine: 真实的故事 "a true story", 真实感受 "real feelings", 真实情况 "the actual situation". It is for what is not made up. 真 ("real") plus 实 ("solid"). Stronger than 真, and used for stories, feelings and facts.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge zhēnshí de gùshi.
column7: This is a true story.

column3: Sturdy, strong, durable: for things 这张桌子很结实 "this table is sturdy", and for bodies 他身体很结实 "he is sturdy". It says something will not break easily. The 实 has a light tone: jiēshi.
column4: 这个箱子很结实，不会坏。
column5: 這個箱子很結實，不會壞。
column6: Zhège xiāngzi hěn jiēshi, bù huì huài.
column7: This box is sturdy and won't break.

column3: To pat, to clap; to shoot: 拍手 "clap", 拍照 "take a photo", 拍电影 "shoot a film", 拍球 "bounce a ball". The 扌 radical shows an action of the hand. For taking photos or videos, 拍 is the common verb in daily speech. Read pāi.
column4: 我们在公园里拍了很多照片。
column5: 我們在公園裡拍了很多照片。
column6: Wǒmen zài gōngyuán lǐ pāi le hěn duō zhàopiàn.
column7: We took a lot of photos in the park.

column3: To grab, to catch, to scratch: 抓住 "grab hold of", 抓鱼 "catch fish", 抓小偷 "catch a thief", 抓痒 "scratch an itch". With the hand radical 扌. Also "to take charge of": 抓工作 "attend to work". Read zhuā.
column6: Jǐngchá zhuādào le nàge xiǎotōu.
column7: The police caught that thief.

column3: To grab hold of, to catch: 抓 ("grab") plus 住 (result: held firmly). 抓住机会 "seize the chance", 抓住他的手 "grab his hand", 抓住小偷. The 住 shows the grip is firm. Negative: 抓不住 "can't catch".
column6: Nǐ yào zhuāzhù zhè cì jīhuì.
column7: You should seize this chance.

column3: To push open, to push away: 推 ("push") plus 开 ("open", a result). 推开门 "push the door open", 把他推开 "push him away". The 开 shows the thing is opened or moved off. Opposite: 拉开 "pull open".
column6: Tā tuīkāi mén zǒu le jìnqù.
column7: He pushed the door open and walked in.

column3: To break, to cut off: 断了 "snapped", 腿断了 "broke a leg", 电话断了 "the call dropped", 断电 "power cut", 中断 "interrupt". It is for long things that snap or links that end. 断 appears in 不断.
column6: Fēng tài dà, shùzhī dōu duàn le.
column7: The wind was so strong that the branches snapped.

column3: Broken, worn out; to break: 杯子破了 "the cup is broken", 衣服破了 "the clothes are torn", 破洞 "hole". As an adjective before a noun it can be rude or fond: 破车 "a beat-up car". 破 as a complement: 打破 "smash". The 石 on the left.
column6: Wǒ de xié pò le yī ge dòng.
column7: My shoe has a hole in it.

column3: To break, to smash: 打破杯子 "break a cup", 打破纪录 "break a record", 打破沉默 "break the silence". 打 ("hit") plus 破 ("broken"). It takes an object, literal or figurative. For a vessel it describes an accident: 我打破了杯子. Compare 破, which can be a state.
column4: 我不小心打破了一个杯子。
column5: 我不小心打破了一個杯子。
column6: Wǒ bù xiǎoxīn dǎpò le yī ge bēizi.
column7: I accidentally broke a cup.

column3: To destroy, to damage: 破坏环境 "damage the environment", 破坏规则 "break the rules", 破坏关系 "ruin a relationship". 破 ("break") plus 坏 ("bad"). Used for harm to things, plans or relations, often with a serious tone.
column6: Wǒmen bù yīnggāi pòhuài huánjìng.
column7: We should not damage the environment.

column3: To untie, to undo, to solve: 解开绳子 "untie the rope", 解开扣子 "undo a button", 解开谜 "solve a riddle". 解 ("loosen") plus 开 (result: apart). Opposite: 系上 or 绑上.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ jiěkāi zhège jié.
column7: Please help me untie this knot.

column3: To put somewhere: 放 ("put") plus 到 (result: arrive at a place). 放到桌子上 "put it on the table", 放到包里 "put it in the bag". The place follows. Different from 放在, which focuses on where it rests. Often follows 把: 把书放到桌子上.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shū fàngdào zhuōzi shàng.
column7: Please put the book on the table.

column3: To repair, to fix: 修车 "repair a car", 修电脑 "fix a computer", 修理 "repair", 修路 "build a road". Also "to study" in 修课. And "to trim": 修头发. For repairing, it is the everyday verb; 修理 is the full form. The 亻 on the left, from an old sense of tidying.
column4: 这台电视坏了，我想找人修一下。
column5: 這台電視壞了，我想找人修一下。
column6: Zhè tái diànshì huài le, wǒ xiǎng zhǎo rén xiū yīxià.
column7: This TV is broken, I want to find someone to fix it.

column3: To mend, to make up for: 补衣服 "mend clothes", 补课 "make up a class", 补充 "add", 补钱 "pay the difference". It means to fill a gap or repair. The 衤 on the left tells us that it was first about mending clothes.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ yào qù bǔkè.
column7: At the weekend I have to go to a make-up class.

column3: To book, to order, to set: 订票 "book a ticket", 订房间 "reserve a room", 订报纸 "subscribe to a paper", 订计划 "make a plan". Money often changes hands, or a reservation is made. Say 订好了 for "booked".
column4: 我已经订好了去北京的机票。
column5: 我已經訂好了去北京的機票。
column6: Wǒ yǐjīng dìng hǎo le qù Běijīng de jīpiào.
column7: I have already booked the flight to Beijing.

column3: To store, to save, to deposit: 存钱 "save money", 存在银行 "deposit in a bank", 存东西 "store things", 存在 "exist". The money meaning is common: 存款 "deposit". For a file, 存盘 or 保存. Read cún. The 子 at the bottom.
column6: Wǒ měi ge yuè dōu cún yīdiǎn qián.
column7: I save a little money every month.

column3: To preserve, to keep: 保存食物 "preserve food", 保存文件 "save a file", 保存完好 "well preserved". 保 ("protect") plus 存 ("store"). It stresses keeping something in good state over time. On a computer, 保存 is the "Save" button.
column6: Zhèxiē gǔshū bǎocún de hěn hǎo.
column7: These old books are very well preserved.

column3: To keep, to retain: 保留意见 "reserve one's opinion", 保留座位 "hold a seat", 保留原样 "keep as it was". 保 ("protect") plus 留 ("remain"). It means not to throw away or change. Differs from 保存, which preserves the condition of something.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ bǎoliú yī ge zuòwèi.
column7: Please keep a seat for me.

column3: To match; to pair: 配得上 "be worthy of", 搭配 "go together", 配钥匙 "make a key", 配眼镜 "get glasses made". It also means "to be fit for": 他配不上她. As in 配菜 "side dish". Read pèi.
column4: 这条裙子和你的鞋很配。
column5: 這條裙子和你的鞋很配。
column6: Zhè tiáo qúnzi hé nǐ de xié hěn pèi.
column7: This skirt goes well with your shoes.

column3: Read chuán it means "to pass on, to spread": 传球 "pass a ball", 传话 "pass a message", 传来 "come across (sound)", 传说 "legend". Read zhuàn it is "a biography": 自传 "autobiography". For this list, chuán is meant.
column4: 请把这个消息传给大家。
column5: 請把這個消息傳給大家。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhège xiāoxi chuán gěi dàjiā.
column7: Please pass this news on to everyone.

column3: To come across, to be heard: 传 ("pass") plus 来 ("come"). It is for a sound or news that reaches you: 传来音乐声 "music drifted over", 传来好消息 "good news came". The thing comes toward the speaker.
column6: Fángjiān lǐ chuánlái yī zhèn xiàoshēng.
column7: A burst of laughter came from the room.

column3: To retreat, to return: 退后 "step back", 退票 "return a ticket", 退钱 "refund", 退休 "retire", 退出 "withdraw". It means moving backward or giving back. The 辶 on the left suggests movement. Pair of 进. Read tuì.
column4: 你可以去退票，但是要扣手续费。
column5: 你可以去退票，但是要扣手續費。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ qù tuìpiào, dànshì yào kòu shǒuxùfèi.
column7: You can return the ticket, but a fee will be deducted.

column3: To withdraw, to quit: 退出比赛 "withdraw from a competition", 退出群 "leave a group", 退出程序 "exit a program". 退 ("retreat") plus 出 ("out"). It means leaving an organization or event. The opposite is 加入 "join" or 进入 "enter".
column4: 他因为受伤，退出了比赛。
column5: 他因為受傷，退出了比賽。
column6: Tā yīnwèi shòushāng, tuìchū le bǐsài.
column7: He withdrew from the competition because of an injury.

column3: Read zhuǎn it means "to turn, to change": 转身 "turn around", 转弯 "turn a corner", 转学 "change schools", 转告 "pass on a message". Read zhuàn it means "to rotate, spin": 转圈 "go in circles". For this list zhuǎn is meant.
column6: Qiánmiàn qǐng xiàng yòu zhuǎn.
column7: Please turn right ahead.

column3: To add, to supplement: 补充水分 "drink more water", 补充说明 "additional explanation", 补充一句 "add a word". 补 ("fill in") plus 充 ("fill"). For adding to what's said or what's lacking. Often used after someone speaks: 我想补充一点.
column4: 我想补充一点：明天要带身份证。
column5: 我想補充一點：明天要帶身分證。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bǔchōng yīdiǎn: míngtiān yào dài shēnfènzhèng.
column7: I would like to add one point: bring your ID card tomorrow.

column3: To surround, to enclose: 围起来 "enclose", 围着桌子坐 "sit around the table", 围巾 "scarf", 周围 "surroundings". It is about forming a ring around something. Read wéi.
column6: Dàjiā wéi zhe zhuōzi zuòxià.
column7: Everyone sat down around the table.

column3: To point; finger: 指着 "point at", 指路 "show the way", 指出 "point out", 指导 "guide", 手指 "finger". It also means "to refer to": 这里指… "here it refers to…". The 扌 on the left and 旨 on the right (the sound). Read zhǐ.
column4: 他指着地图告诉我怎么走。
column5: 他指著地圖告訴我怎麼走。
column6: Tā zhǐ zhe dìtú gàosu wǒ zěnme zǒu.
column7: He pointed at the map and told me which way to go.

column3: To chase, to pursue: 追上 "catch up", 追赶 "chase after", 追求 "pursue", 追问 "keep asking". 追 + 上 means you caught up. The 辶 on the left shows motion. For chasing someone romantically, 追 is also used: 他在追她. Read zhuī.
column6: Jǐngchá zài hòumiàn zhuī xiǎotōu.
column7: The police are chasing the thief from behind.

column3: Email: 电子 ("electronic") plus 邮件 ("mail"). The full, formal name, found on forms and in writing: 发电子邮件 "send an email", 电子邮件地址 "email address". In speech people often say 邮件 or 电邮.
column4: 请把文件发到我的电子邮件里。
column5: 請把文件發到我的電子郵件裡。
column6: Qǐng bǎ wénjiàn fā dào wǒ de diànzǐyóujiàn lǐ.
column7: Please send the file to my email.

column3: Mail, email: originally post, now mostly email: 发邮件 "send an email", 收邮件 "receive email", 一封邮件 "an email", with 封 as the measure word. 邮 refers to post. A bare 邮件 is usually the email in daily talk.
column4: 我给老师发了一封邮件。
column5: 我給老師發了一封郵件。
column6: Wǒ gěi lǎoshī fā le yī fēng yóujiàn.
column7: I sent the teacher an email.

column3: Mailbox, inbox: 邮 ("post") plus 箱 ("box"). Mostly the email box or address: 电子邮箱 "email address", 我的邮箱 "my email", 邮箱满了 "inbox full". It can also be a physical mailbox. Ask 你的邮箱是多少? or 你的邮箱地址?
column4: 请告诉我你的邮箱地址。
column5: 請告訴我你的郵箱地址。
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de yóuxiāng dìzhǐ.
column7: Please tell me your email address.

column3: The Internet: 互 ("mutually") plus 联 ("connect") plus 网 ("net"). 上互联网 "get on the internet", 互联网公司 "internet company". More formal than 网络 and 网; the shortened form is 网. A proper noun in the list, so capitalized.
column4: 互联网让我们的生活更方便。
column5: 互聯網讓我們的生活更方便。
column6: Hùliánwǎng ràng wǒmen de shēnghuó gèng fāngbiàn.
column7: The internet makes our lives more convenient.

column3: To send, to transmit: 发送邮件 "send an email", 发送短信 "send a text", 发送文件 "send a file". 发 ("send out") plus 送 ("deliver"). On screens, it's the "Send" button. Here 发 is read fā. Formal and used for electronic messages.
column4: 我已经把邮件发送给你了。
column5: 我已經把郵件發送給你了。
column6: Wǒ yǐjīng bǎ yóujiàn fāsòng gěi nǐ le.
column7: I have already sent the email to you.

column3: To send out, to emit: 发出声音 "make a sound", 发出邀请 "send an invitation", 发出通知 "issue a notice". 发 ("emit") plus 出 ("out"). The thing follows: it can be a sound, light, a signal or a document.
column4: 房间里发出一种奇怪的声音。
column5: 房間裡發出一種奇怪的聲音。
column6: Fángjiān lǐ fāchū yī zhǒng qíguài de shēngyīn.
column7: The room made a strange sound.

column3: To input, to type in: 输入密码 "enter a password", 输入文字 "type text". 输 ("send in") plus 入 ("enter"). A computer word; the opposite is 输出 "output". 输入法 is an input method. Here 输 means "convey", not "lose".
column6: Qǐng shūrù nǐ de mìmǎ.
column7: Please enter your password.

column3: To install: 安装软件 "install software", 安装空调 "install an air conditioner", 安装完成 "installation finished". 安 ("settle") plus 装 ("fit"). For both apps and equipment.
column4: 我需要安装一个新软件。
column5: 我需要安裝一個新軟體。
column6: Wǒ xūyào ānzhuāng yī ge xīn ruǎnjiàn.
column7: I need to install a new piece of software.

column3: To press; to follow: 按键 "press a key", 按门铃 "ring the doorbell", 按照 "according to", 按时 "on time". Both the finger-pressing and the "according to" sense are common. The 扌 on the left shows it is a hand action. Read àn.
column6: Qǐng àn zhège ànniǔ.
column7: Please press this button.

column3: Communication by letter or signal: 通信 is about sending messages by post, phone or network: 通信设备 "communications equipment", 手机通信 "mobile communications", 通信地址 "mailing address". Written and technical.
column4: 这个地区的手机通信很方便。
column5: 這個地區的手機通信很方便。
column6: Zhège dìqū de shǒujī tōngxìn hěn fāngbiàn.
column7: Mobile communication is convenient in this area.

column3: To contact; connection: 联系你 "contact you", 保持联系 "keep in touch", 联系方式 "contact information", 有联系 "be connected". The verb takes a person as object: 我会联系你. It is the standard word for contacting someone.
column6: Yǒu shì qǐng liánxì wǒ.
column7: Please contact me if anything comes up.

column3: To photocopy: 复印文件 "copy a document", 复印机 "photocopier", 复印件 "a copy". 复 ("again") plus 印 ("print"). Say 请帮我复印两份 "please make two copies". Here 复 is read fù.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ fùyìn zhè fèn wénjiàn.
column7: Please photocopy this document for me.

column3: To calculate: 计算价格 "work out the price", 计算机 "computer", 计算错了 "miscalculated". 计 ("count") plus 算 ("reckon"). It is math or planning: 他在计算花费 "he is working out the cost". The 计算机 is a "computer" in mainland usage.
column6: Nǐ bāng wǒ jìsuàn yīxià zǒngjià.
column7: Help me work out the total price.

column3: Science and technology: 科 ("science") plus 技 ("skill"). 科技发展 "technological development", 科技公司 "tech company", 高科技 "high-tech". A wide, news-like word for both fields.
column4: 科技让我们的生活越来越方便。
column5: 科技讓我們的生活越來越方便。
column6: Kējì ràng wǒmen de shēnghuó yuè lái yuè fāngbiàn.
column7: Technology makes our lives more and more convenient.

column3: Technology; skill, technique: 技术员 "technician", 技术问题 "technical problem", 新技术 "new technology", 他的技术很好 "he's very skilled". 技 means "skill" and 术 "art". The word covers both the know-how of a person and a technology.
column4: 这家公司有很先进的技术。
column5: 這家公司有很先進的技術。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu hěn xiānjìn de jìshù.
column7: This company has very advanced technology.

column3: Artificial, man-made: 人工智能 "artificial intelligence", 人工湖 "artificial lake", 人工服务 "human service" (a live agent, not a machine). 人 ("person") plus 工 ("work"). In some uses it means labor: 人工费 "labor cost". Opposite: 自然 for nature.
column6: Zhège hú shì réngōng zuò de.
column7: This lake is man-made.

column3: Automatic, automatically: 自动门 "automatic door", 自动关机 "shuts off by itself", 自动取款机 "ATM". 自 ("self") plus 动 ("move"). It describes machines or systems doing something without a person. Also "of one's own accord": 自动参加.
column6: Mén huì zìdòng dǎkāi.
column7: The door opens automatically.

column3: Modern times; modern: 现代人 "modern people", 现代社会 "modern society", 现代化 "modernized", 现代文学 "modern literature". 现 ("present") plus 代 ("era"). In history, it refers to the period after the early 20th century, and in daily use to "contemporary". The opposite is 古代.
column4: 现代人的生活节奏很快。
column5: 現代人的生活節奏很快。
column6: Xiàndàirén de shēnghuó jiézòu hěn kuài.
column7: The pace of life of modern people is fast.

column3: Modernization; to modernize: 现代 ("modern") plus 化 ("-ize"). 实现现代化 "achieve modernization", 现代化城市 "a modern city". The suffix 化 makes verbs and nouns from words: 绿化 "make green", 美化 "beautify".
column4: 这座城市正在快速现代化。
column5: 這座城市正在快速現代化。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì zhèngzài kuàisù xiàndàihuà.
column7: This city is modernizing quickly.

column3: To develop, to open up: 开发新产品 "develop a new product", 开发资源 "exploit resources", 开发区 "development zone", 软件开发 "software development". 开 ("open") plus 发 ("emit"). It is used for natural resources, land, software and products.
column4: 这家公司正在开发一个新软件。
column5: 這家公司正在開發一個新軟體。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhèngzài kāifā yī ge xīn ruǎnjiàn.
column7: This company is developing a new piece of software.

column3: Art as a field or a skill: 艺术家 "artist", 艺术品 "work of art", 艺术节 "arts festival". 艺 is skill or craft and 术 is technique, so the word is literally "skilled technique". It covers all the arts, music and dance included, not just painting.
column6: Tā hěn xǐhuan yìshù.
column7: She likes art very much.

column3: Fine arts, mostly drawing and painting, and the usual name of the school subject: 美术课 "art class". 美 "beautiful" + 术 "art, technique". Music is 音乐, not 美术.
column6: Wǒmen xiàwǔ yǒu měishù kè.
column7: We have art class this afternoon.

column3: A "picture", "diagram" or "chart": 图片 "picture", 地图 "map", 图书馆 "library". Pictures take the measure word 张: 一张图. On its own it is a little bookish; in speech people often say 图片 or 画.
column6: Qǐng kàn zhè zhāng tú.
column7: Please look at this picture.

column3: A "drawing" or "picture", something drawn or painted, such as a child's picture or an illustration. Measure word 幅 or 张. 图 is "picture" and 画 "draw", so it stresses that the picture was drawn, not photographed.
column4: 孩子在墙上画了一幅图画。
column5: 孩子在牆上畫了一幅圖畫。
column6: Háizi zài qiáng shang huà le yī fú túhuà.
column7: The child drew a picture on the wall.

column3: A "work" by an artist, writer or musician: 文学作品 "literary work", 他的作品 "his works". 作 "make" + 品 "article". It is the thing produced, so it is used for creative output, not for homework (that is 作业).
column6: Zhè shì tā zuì xīn de zuòpǐn.
column7: This is his latest work.

column3: To create a work of art, literature or music, and also the act of creation: 创作歌曲 "write songs", 文学创作 "literary writing". It suits original creative work only; for making ordinary things use 做 or 制作.
column6: Tā zhèngzài chuàngzuò yī shǒu xīn gē.
column7: He is writing a new song.

column3: Literature as a subject or art: 中国文学, 文学作品, 文学家 "man of letters". 文 "writing" + 学 "study", so it started as the study of writing. It names the field, not a single book (that is 作品 or 书).
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan dú Zhōngguó wénxué.
column7: I like reading Chinese literature.

column3: Written language or "script" as a system: 汉字 is a kind of 文字. Not a single character (that is 字) and not a text (that is 文章). Also used for written words in contrast to pictures or speech: 文字说明 "written explanation".
column4: 汉字是一种古老的文字。
column5: 漢字是一種古老的文字。
column6: Hànzì shì yī zhǒng gǔlǎo de wénzì.
column7: Chinese characters are an old writing system.

column3: An "article" or "essay", a complete piece of writing; measure word 篇: 一篇文章. 写文章 is "to write an article" and 看文章 "to read one". Longer than a note, shorter than a book.
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: This article is very interesting.

column3: Writing as an activity or a skill, composition: 写作课 "writing class", 写作能力 "writing ability". It can also mean to write as a profession: 他以写作为生 "he lives by writing". 写 "write" + 作 "make".
column4: 他每天早上写作两个小时。
column5: 他每天早上寫作兩個小時。
column6: Tā měitiān zǎoshang xiězuò liǎng gè xiǎoshí.
column7: He writes for two hours every morning.

column3: The "author" of a book, article or other work. 者 marks a person who does something: 作 "make" + 者 gives "the one who made it". Ask 这本书的作者是谁？ to find out who wrote a book.
column6: Zhè běn shū de zuòzhě shì shéi?
column7: Who is the author of this book?
