column3: A "reader" of a book, newspaper or magazine, thinking of the audience as a whole: 读者来信 "letters from readers". 读 "read" + 者 "person who". For someone reading right now, you would say 看书的人 instead.
column6: Zhè běn shū yǒu hěn duō dúzhě.
column7: This book has many readers.

column3: A "foreign language", especially as a written language: 外文书 "foreign-language books", 外文系 "foreign languages department". Compare 外语, which stresses the spoken language and learning it. 外 "outside" + 文 "writing".
column6: Tā huì kàn wàiwén shū.
column7: He can read books in foreign languages.

column3: Magazine; measure word 本: 一本杂志. 看杂志 and 订杂志 "subscribe to a magazine" are the usual verbs. 杂 means "mixed, miscellaneous", fitting a publication with many kinds of content.
column6: Wǒ měi gè yuè mǎi yī běn zázhì.
column7: I buy a magazine every month.

column3: A "title" or "headline" of an article, news story or document. 新闻标题 is a news headline, and 标题党 describes sites that use exaggerated headlines. 标 "mark" + 题 "topic".
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng de biāotí hěn cháng.
column7: The title of this article is very long.

column3: A "form" or "table" with boxes to fill in: 填表格 "fill in a form", 一张表格. 表 is a chart and 格 a grid or box, which is why the same word covers a spreadsheet's table.
column6: Qǐng tián yīxià zhè zhāng biǎogé.
column7: Please fill in this form.

column3: A "document" or "file": official papers, and also computer files. 发文件 "send a document", 打开文件 "open a file". 文件夹 is the "folder" that holds them.
column6: Bǎ wénjiàn fā gěi wǒ.
column7: Send the document to me.

column3: A "postage stamp": 贴邮票 "stick on a stamp", 买邮票 "buy stamps". 邮 is "post, mail" (as in 邮局 "post office") and 票 "ticket", so it is a ticket for the post.
column6: Xìn shang yào tiē yóupiào.
column7: A letter needs a stamp.

column3: An "ID card", the identity card carried in China. 身份 "identity, status" + 证 "proof". Often asked for when buying train tickets or checking into a hotel: 请出示身份证 "please show your ID". The full form is 居民身份证.
column6: Qǐng chūshì nǐ de shēnfènzhèng.
column7: Please show your ID card.

column3: Identification papers in general, a catch-all for ID card, passport, driver's license or work pass. 证 "proof" + 件, a counter for items and documents. Used when you are not saying which document is meant.
column6: Nǐ dài zhèngjiàn le ma?
column7: Did you bring your ID?

column3: A "certificate" or "proof". It mostly appears inside words: 毕业证 "graduation certificate", 驾驶证 "driver's license", 身份证 "ID card". As a verb it means "to prove", more often seen in 证明.
column6: Tā ná dào le bìyèzhèng.
column7: He got his graduation certificate.

column3: An "envelope": 信 "letter" + 封 "to seal". 封 is also the measure word for letters (一封信), so the same character is both the thing that seals and the count. 写信封 is "to address an envelope".
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī gè xìnfēng.
column7: Please give me an envelope.

column3: Read wéi here, the "to be / to act as" reading. It lives in fixed words: 成为 "become", 认为 "think that", 称为 "be called", 以……为 "take as". The other reading, wèi, is "for" as in 为了. Learn the pair by the words it appears in.
column6: Tā xiǎng chéngwéi lǎoshī.
column7: He wants to become a teacher.

column3: In order to or "for the sake of". It introduces a goal and the main clause gives the action: 为了学好汉语，我每天练习. It can also take a noun: 为了孩子. The goal always comes first and the action second.
column6: Wèile jiànkāng, tā měitiān pǎobù.
column7: For his health, he runs every day.

column3: Therefore, for this reason, written and fairly formal. It starts the second clause and refers back to the first: 他很努力，因此成绩很好. In speech people say 所以. 因 "cause" + 此 "this".
column4: 他每天练习，因此进步很快。
column5: 他每天練習，因此進步很快。
column6: Tā měitiān liànxí, yīncǐ jìnbù hěn kuài.
column7: He practices every day, so he improves quickly.

column3: Because of, owing to, formal and written. It opens a sentence with the reason, often followed by 所以 or 因此 in the second clause: 由于天气不好，航班取消了. It sounds more official than 因为.
column6: Yóuyú xiàyǔ, bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
column7: Because of the rain, the match was cancelled.

column3: Two main uses. As "by" naming who does something: 这件事由他负责 "he is in charge of this". And "from" in 由……到……. Also in 由于 and 理由. Unlike 被, it does not mean something bad happens to the subject.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì yóu wǒ lái zuò.
column7: I will do this.

column3: If, the spoken word for a hypothetical. The result clause usually has 就: 要是明天下雨，我就不去. It sets up something that may not happen, a bit like "if it should". 如果 is the same but a little more formal.
column4: 要是明天下雨，我们就不去了。
column5: 要是明天下雨，我們就不去了。
column6: Yàoshi míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bù qù le.
column7: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

column3: No matter (who, what, how), used with a question word or with 还是: 不论多忙，他都来. The second part nearly always has 都 or 也. Written style; spoken usage prefers 不管, which works the same way.
column6: Bùlùn duō máng, tā dōu lái.
column7: No matter how busy he is, he comes.

column3: Not only. It usually pairs with 而且, 还 or 也 in the next part: 不仅便宜，而且好用. 不仅 can come before the verb or before the subject. Slightly more formal than 不但, which means the same.
column4: 她不仅聪明，而且很努力。
column5: 她不僅聰明，而且很努力。
column6: Tā bùjǐn cōngmíng, érqiě hěn nǔlì.
column7: She is not only smart, but also hard-working.

column3: Not only, the colloquial cousin of 不仅. Used before a noun or verb, usually with 也 or 还: 不光我，大家都累了. 光 elsewhere means "light" or "only", which is where "not just" comes from.
column6: Bùguāng wǒ, dàjiā dōu lèi le.
column7: Not just me, everyone is tired.

column3: Put before 不, 没, 未 to push back on an assumption: "actually not, not at all". 他并不聪明 means "he is not really clever", answering what someone thought. It is not "and" here; that is 并且.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì bìng bù nán.
column7: This is actually not hard.

column3: And also, moreover, joining two verbs or clauses, not two nouns (for nouns use 和). 他会说英语，并且说得很好 adds a second point. It is slightly more formal than 还, and often follows 不仅 or 不但.
column4: 他会说英语，并且说得很好。
column5: 他會說英語，並且說得很好。
column6: Tā huì shuō Yīngyǔ, bìngqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
column7: He can speak English, and he speaks it very well.

column3: In addition, besides when starting a new point: 另外，我还有一个问题. It can also mean "other": 另外一个人 "another person". It adds something new, unlike 其次, which gives the next item in a list.
column4: 另外，我还想问一个问题。
column5: 另外，我還想問一個問題。
column6: Lìngwài, wǒ hái xiǎng wèn yī gè wèntí.
column7: Also, I have one more question.

column3: On the other hand, introducing the second side of a comparison. It usually answers 一方面: 一方面……，另一方面……. 方面 means "aspect, side", so it reads "another aspect".
column4: 这里很安静，另一方面也有点远。
column5: 這裡很安靜，另一方面也有點遠。
column6: Zhèlǐ hěn ānjìng, lìngyīfāngmiàn yě yǒudiǎn yuǎn.
column7: It is quiet here, but on the other hand it is a bit far.

column3: On the one hand. It sets out the first of two sides and is paired with 另一方面 or a second 一方面: 我一方面要工作，一方面要照顾孩子. With the same subject, the pair also means "while doing both".
column4: 我一方面要工作，一方面要照顾孩子。
column5: 我一方面要工作，一方面要照顧孩子。
column6: Wǒ yīfāngmiàn yào gōngzuò, yīfāngmiàn yào zhàogù háizi.
column7: I have to work and look after the children at the same time.

column3: Secondly, next in order, listing the second point after 首先. As a plain adjective it means "second in importance": 健康最重要，钱是其次. The ordinal 次 is also in 第二次 "the second time".
column6: Qícì, wǒmen yào zhùyì ānquán.
column7: Second, we must pay attention to safety.

column3: First of all, the opening word of a list of points, followed by 其次 and 最后. 首 means "head, first" and 先 "earlier", so it is "head of the line". Use it to begin instructions or arguments.
column6: Shǒuxiān, qǐng dàjiā zuò hǎo.
column7: First of all, everyone please sit properly.

column3: Except or "besides", often framed as 除了……以外. With 都 it excludes: 除了我，大家都来了. With 还 or 也 it adds: 除了英语，他还会法语. Pick the meaning from the second half.
column6: Chúle wǒ, dàjiā dōu lái le.
column7: Everyone came except me.

column3: Here, "it's just that" before a drawback: 这个手机很好，就是太贵了. It admits one flaw after praise. It is also "exactly, precisely", as in 他就是我老师 "he is my teacher", and "even if" in 就是……也.
column4: 这个手机很好，就是太贵了。
column5: 這個手機很好，就是太貴了。
column6: Zhège shǒujī hěn hǎo, jiùshì tài guì le.
column7: This phone is good, it is just too expensive.

column3: Only, merely: 他只是个孩子 "he is only a child". It also introduces a drawback, "it's just that": 菜很好吃，只是有点贵. In that second use it is close to 就是, a little more careful in tone.
column6: Tā zhǐshì ge háizi.
column7: He is only a child.

column3: Only (if): 只有努力，才能成功 "only by working hard can you succeed". The result clause normally has 才. It also means plainly "there is only": 这里只有一个人. Do not mix it with 只要, which means "as long as".
column6: Zhǐyǒu nǔlì, cáinéng chénggōng.
column7: Only by working hard can you succeed.

column3: Have no choice but to, followed by a verb: 没有车，我们只好走路. Something blocked the first plan, so the speaker accepts a second one. The mood is resigned. Often follows a clause giving the reason.
column6: Méiyǒu chē, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zǒulù.
column7: There is no car, so we have to walk.

column3: Have to, cannot help but, doing something because there is no alternative: 我不得不走了. It is stronger than 必须 in feeling, because the speaker does not want to. It wraps a verb: 不得不 + verb.
column6: Tài wǎn le, wǒ bùdébù huí jiā.
column7: It is too late, I have to go home.

column3: Until, marking the point a situation lasts to. With a positive verb, 才 often marks the late time: 直到晚上，他才回来 "he did not come back until evening". 直 "straight" + 到 "arrive" gives "straight on until".
column6: Zhídào wǎnshang, tā cái huílái.
column7: He did not come back until evening.

column3: To follow, and in compounds "as you like" or "along with": 随便 "casual, as you please", 随时 "at any time", 随着 "along with", 随身 "on one's person". On its own it is rare in speech; 请随我来 "please follow me" is a typical use.
column6: Qǐng suí wǒ lái.
column7: Please follow me.

column3: According to, in accordance with, before a rule, plan or instruction: 按照规定, 按照计划. The phrase often opens the sentence and then a comma. 按 "press" + 照 "shine on, follow" suggests going by the guide. 按 alone also appears.
column6: Qǐng ànzhào shuōmíng shǐyòng.
column7: Please use it according to the instructions.

column3: All kinds of, before a noun: 各种水果 "all sorts of fruit", and 各种各样 "of every kind". 各 means "each, various" and 种 "kind", so it lists the different kinds in a group.
column6: Shāngdiàn lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng shuǐguǒ.
column7: The shop has all kinds of fruit.

column3: Each going their own way. It goes before the verb, never before a noun, and refers back to a group: 大家各自回家 "everyone went home on their own". 自 means "self". Compare 每个, which does not carry this sense.
column6: Chī wán fàn, dàjiā gèzì huí jiā.
column7: After the meal, everyone went home separately.

column3: Whole, entire, placed before a measure word or time word: 整天 "all day", 整晚 "all night", 整个. It often shows that something took the full length. As a verb it also means "to fix up" or, in speech, "to mess with".
column6: Wǒ zhěng wǎn méi shuì.
column7: I did not sleep all night.

column3: The whole, entire, before a noun: 整个城市 "the whole city", 整个下午 "the whole afternoon". It stresses that nothing is left out.
column6: Zhěnggè chéngshì dōu tíngdiàn le.
column7: The whole city lost power.

column3: The whole, seen as one unit against its parts, or "overall" as an adjective: 整体来说 "on the whole", 整体效果 "overall effect". 整 "whole" + 体 "body". Common at the start of a summing-up.
column4: 整体来说，这个计划不错。
column5: 整體來說，這個計劃不錯。
column6: Zhěngtǐ lái shuō, zhège jìhuà bùcuò.
column7: On the whole, this plan is good.

column3: Everything, all: 一切都好 "everything is fine". Before a noun it means "all": 一切困难 "all difficulties". It stands alone as a pronoun and usually takes 都 before the verb. Note the 切 here is read qiè, not qiē.
column6: Yīqiè dōu huì hǎo qǐlái de.
column7: Everything will get better.

column3: Comprehensive, all-round, covering every side: 全面检查 "a full check-up", 全面发展 "all-round development". 全 "whole" + 面 "side, face". It can also modify a verb: 全面了解.
column4: 医生给他做了全面检查。
column5: 醫生給他做了全面檢查。
column6: Yīshēng gěi tā zuò le quánmiàn jiǎnchá.
column7: The doctor gave him a full check-up.

column3: The whole venue, meaning everyone in the hall, stadium or theater, or "the whole match": 全场观众 "the whole audience". 场 is a place for an event, so this word is tied to events and performances.
column6: Quánchǎng guānzhòng dōu zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: The whole audience stood up.

column3: Worldwide, global: 全球化 "globalization", 全球最大 "the biggest in the world". 全 "whole" + 球 "globe, ball". Mostly in news and formal writing; in speech 世界 is more usual, as in 世界上.
column6: Zhè shì quánqiú zuì dà de gōngsī.
column7: This is the biggest company in the world.

column3: Common, shared before a noun, with 的: 共同的爱好 "shared interest". It is also an adverb, "jointly", before a verb: 共同努力 "work together". 共 "together" + 同 "same".
column6: Wǒmen yǒu gòngtóng de àihào.
column7: We have a shared hobby.

column3: Altogether there are / altogether have: 全班共有三十人 "the class has thirty people in all". It is followed by a number. It can also mean "to own jointly", though that is less usual at this level.
column4: 这个班共有三十个学生。
column5: 這個班共有三十個學生。
column6: Zhège bān gòngyǒu sānshí gè xuésheng.
column7: This class has thirty students in all.

column3: Each other, mutually. It goes before the verb: 互相帮助 "help each other", 互相学习 "learn from each other". Both 互 and 相 already mean "mutual", so the word is doubly reciprocal, and it needs no object.
column6: Tóngxuémen hùxiāng bāngzhù.
column7: The classmates help each other.

column3: Mutual, each other. The same two characters as 互相 in reverse. It is a bit more formal and, unlike 互相, can sit before a noun: 相互关系 "mutual relation". Before a verb the two are interchangeable.
column6: Tāmen xiānghù liǎojiě.
column7: They understand each other.

column3: Both sides, both parties in a contract, talk or match: 双方同意 "both sides agree". 双 "pair" + 方 "side". The other side alone is 对方, and each side is 各方.
column6: Shuāngfāng dōu tóngyì le.
column7: Both sides agreed.

column3: The other party, the person or side you deal with: 对方的电话 "the other party's phone", whether in a call, match or negotiation. It always points away from the speaker. 对 "facing" + 方 "side".
column6: Wǒ tīng bù qīng duìfāng de shēngyīn.
column7: I can't hear the other person's voice clearly.

column3: Oneself, itself, for emphasis and usually in formal writing: 自身的问题 "one's own problems". 自 "self" + 身 "body". It follows a noun or stands before 的.
column6: Yào xiān jiějué zìshēn de wèntí.
column7: You have to solve your own problems first.

column3: Individual, personal: 个人意见 "personal opinion", 个人信息 "personal information". It also means "oneself" as an individual in contrast to a group or the state: 就我个人来说 "as for me personally".
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de gèrén yìjiàn.
column7: This is my personal opinion.

column3: Personally, in person, doing something yourself instead of sending someone: 亲自去 "go in person". It goes before the verb. 亲 here is "oneself, directly" and 自 "self", so the word underlines that the person did it.
column6: Jīnglǐ qīnzì lái jiē wǒmen.
column7: The manager came to pick us up in person.

column3: A full, whole amount, putting weight on a long time or big quantity: 整整一年 "a whole year". It sits before the number and measure word. The doubling makes it stronger than 整 and implies surprise at how much.
column6: Wǒ děng le zhěngzhěng yī gè xiǎoshí.
column7: I waited a full hour.

column3: Doctor, a spoken word, especially in northern China. Read dàifu, with a neutral tone; the reading dàfū is a different word (an ancient official rank). You can also address a doctor as 大夫.
column6: Dàifu shuō wǒ yào duō xiūxi.
column7: The doctor says I should rest more.

column3: Police officer and "the police". The measure word is 个 or 名: 一名警察. 警察局 is the "police station". 警 "warn, alert" + 察 "examine", an officer who watches for trouble.
column6: Jǐngchá zài bāng tā zhǎo háizi.
column7: The police are helping him look for his child.

column3: Traffic police, short for 交通警察. 交 is taken from 交通 "traffic". You see them directing cars or checking drivers, and they stand apart from the ordinary 警察.
column6: Jiāojǐng zhèngzài zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
column7: The traffic police are directing traffic.

column3: Security guard, the guard at a gate or building, not a police officer. 保 "protect" + 安 "safe". The pinyin takes an apostrophe (bǎo'ān) because 安 begins with a vowel.
column6: Bǎo'ān zài ménkǒu.
column7: The security guard is at the door.

column3: Boss or "shop owner". People call a shop or restaurant owner 老板 directly: 老板，多少钱？
column6: Lǎobǎn, duōshao qián?
column7: Boss, how much is it?

column3: Engineer: 工程 "engineering project" + 师, the suffix for a skilled professional, as in 老师, 医师 and 律师. The measure word for a person is 名 or 位: 一名工程师. Add the field in front: 软件工程师.
column6: Tā shì yī míng gōngchéngshī.
column7: He is an engineer.

column3: Civil servant, a government employee. 公务 "public affairs" + 员, the suffix for members of a staff. Many young people in China prepare to take the civil-service exam, 考公务员.
column6: Tā kǎo shàng le gōngwùyuán.
column7: She passed the civil service exam.

column3: Expert: 专 "specialized" + 家, the suffix for a person skilled in a field (作家, 画家). 专家 is usually named with the field: 医学专家 "medical expert". The measure word is 位.
column4: 专家说多喝水对身体好。
column5: 專家說多喝水對身體好。
column6: Zhuānjiā shuō duō hē shuǐ duì shēntǐ hǎo.
column7: The expert says drinking more water is good for your health.

column3: Reporter, journalist: 记 "record" + 者 "person who". 记者会 or 记者招待会 is a "press conference". The measure word is 位 or 名.
column6: Jìzhě wèn le tā sān gè wèntí.
column7: The reporter asked him three questions.

column3: Volunteer: 志愿 "voluntary aspiration" + 者 "person". The verb phrase is 做志愿者 or 当志愿者. 志愿 alone can be "volunteer" as a verb or "wish".
column4: 他每个周末都做志愿者。
column5: 他每個週末都做志願者。
column6: Tā měi gè zhōumò dōu zuò zhìyuànzhě.
column7: He volunteers every weekend.

column3: Director, head of a department, office or committee, and used as a title after a surname: 张主任. 主 "main" + 任 "duty, post". A hospital's 主任 is a senior doctor; an office's 主任 manages the office.
column6: Zhāng zhǔrèn zài bàngōngshì.
column7: Director Zhang is in the office.

column3: Minister, the head of a government 部 (ministry), or a "department head" in a company. Note 长 is read zhǎng "head", not cháng "long". Used as a title: 王部长. 教育部长 is the education minister.
column6: Bùzhǎng jīntiān yào kāihuì.
column7: The minister has a meeting today.

column3: The "head" of a 所, an institute, research center or small office such as a police station (派出所). 长 is zhǎng "head" as in 部长. Used as a title: 李所长.
column6: Tā shì yánjiūsuǒ de suǒzhǎng.
column7: He is the head of the research institute.

column3: A "leader" or "the leadership", in China the people in charge at work: 我们的领导 "our boss, our leaders". It is also a verb, "to lead": 领导大家. People address a leader by title, not by 领导 alone.
column6: Lǐngdǎo ràng wǒ míngtiān qù.
column7: The boss told me to go tomorrow.

column3: Employee, staff member of a company: 公司员工, 新员工 "new employee". 员 "member" + 工 "worker". The word covers every level of a company's staff, from clerks to managers.
column6: Gōngsī de yuángōng dōu hěn niánqīng.
column7: The company's employees are all young.

column3: Staff and workers of a work unit, especially a state-owned factory, school or hospital: 全体职工 "all the staff". It sounds older and more official than 员工, and is often a group word.
column6: Gōngchǎng yǒu wǔbǎi míng zhígōng.
column7: The factory has five hundred workers.

column3: Personnel, staff, a collective word for people in a job or role: 工作人员 "staff, a person working at an event", 技术人员 "technician". It names people by function and is not used for a single close person.
column6: Gōngzuò rényuán qǐng dào zhèbiān lái.
column7: Staff members, please come over here.

column3: A suffix for a person in a job or a member of a group: 售货员 "shop assistant", 服务员 "waiter", 演员 "actor", 学员 "trainee". It rarely stands alone. The same character is in 员工 and 会员.
column6: Tā shì zhè jiā diàn de shòuhuòyuán.
column7: She is a shop assistant in this store.

column3: A suffix meaning "the one who": 作者 "author", 读者 "reader", 记者 "reporter", 学习者 "learner". It turns a verb or noun into a person, much like English "-er" or "-or". A literary use as a pronoun survives in a few phrases, but you meet it mostly in compounds.
column6: Zhè jiā bàozhǐ yǒu hěn duō dúzhě.
column7: This newspaper has many readers.

column3: A "member" of a family, team or group: 家庭成员 "family member", 小组成员 "team member". It stresses being one part of a whole. 成 "become" + 员 "member".
column4: 我们家有四位家庭成员。
column5: 我們家有四位家庭成員。
column6: Wǒmen jiā yǒu sì wèi jiātíng chéngyuán.
column7: There are four people in my family.

column3: A "member" with a card, such as a club, gym or shop: 会员卡 "membership card", 成为会员 "become a member". Unlike 成员, it suggests joining and often paying. 会 here is "society, association".
column4: 她是这家健身房的会员。
column5: 她是這家健身房的會員。
column6: Tā shì zhè jiā jiànshēnfáng de huìyuán.
column7: She is a member of this gym.

column3: Talent in the sense of capable people: 需要人才 "need talented people", 人才市场 "job fair, talent market". It is the person, not the skill. 才 is "ability", the same as in 才能.
column6: Gōngsī xūyào gèng duō réncái.
column7: The company needs more talented people.

column3: Occupation, profession: 你的职业是什么？ is the polite way to ask what someone does. As an adjective it means "professional": 职业运动员 "professional athlete". 职 "post, duty" + 业 "trade".
column6: Nǐ de zhíyè shì shénme?
column7: What is your occupation?

column3: To find a job, be employed, used for the job situation of a population: 就业难 "hard to find work", 就业率 "employment rate". 就 "go to" + 业 "work". For "my job" say 我的工作.
column6: Jīnnián dàxuéshēng jiùyè hěn nán.
column7: It is hard for college graduates to find work this year.

column3: To start a business, start an enterprise: 创业公司 "start-up". 创 "start, create" + 业 "enterprise". Often said of young people building a company from nothing.
column6: Tā bìyè hòu kāishǐ chuàngyè.
column7: After graduating he started his own business.

column3: A "career" or "cause" that one is devoted to, bigger than a 工作 or job: 事业成功 "a successful career", 教育事业 "the cause of education". It can also mean a public undertaking such as a nonprofit organization. 事 "affair" + 业 "enterprise".
column6: Tā de shìyè yuèláiyuè hǎo.
column7: His career is getting better and better.

column3: To retire: 退休工资 "pension", 退休年龄 "retirement age". 退 "withdraw" + 休 "rest". It is used for ending a working life, not for quitting a job (that is 辞职).
column6: Wǒ bàba qùnián tuìxiū le.
column7: My father retired last year.

column3: Wages, salary: 发工资 "pay wages", 拿工资 "receive wages", 工资高 "high pay". 资 means "resources, funds". It is the usual word for monthly pay; 薪水 is also used.
column6: Wǒmen měi yuè shí hào fā gōngzī.
column7: We are paid on the tenth of every month.

column3: A "department" of a company or government: 哪个部门 "which department", 销售部门 "sales department". 部 "section" + 门 "door". The thing you work in, not the building.
column6: Nǐ zài nǎge bùmén gōngzuò?
column7: Which department do you work in?

column3: Industry, meaning manufacturing and heavy production: 工业化 "industrialization", 工业区 "industrial zone". Contrast 农业 "agriculture" and 商业 "commerce". 工 "work" + 业 "trade".
column4: 这个城市的工业很发达。
column5: 這個城市的工業很發達。
column6: Zhège chéngshì de gōngyè hěn fādá.
column7: This city's industry is well developed.

column3: Factory, used mostly in names and compounds: 钢厂 "steel works", 工厂, 厂长 "factory director". It is the first character of 厂长 "factory director".
column6: Zhège chǎng yǒu yīqiān míng gōngrén.
column7: This factory has a thousand workers.

column3: Factory. 工 "work" + 厂 "plant". People work 在工厂 "in a factory" and 工厂 produces goods in quantity. For a workshop or a small plant, 作坊 or 车间 may be used.
column6: Tā zài yī jiā gōngchǎng gōngzuò.
column7: He works in a factory.

column3: To process raw materials into products: 加工食品 "processed food", 来料加工 "processing of supplied materials". 加 "add" + 工 "work". It can also mean to process data or to machine metal.
column4: 这些食品是在工厂加工的。
column5: 這些食品是在工廠加工的。
column6: Zhèxiē shípǐn shì zài gōngchǎng jiāgōng de.
column7: This food was processed in a factory.

column3: A "task" or "mission": 完成任务 "complete a task", 接受任务 "accept a mission". It is something assigned to you by someone else. 务 is neutral-toned in the word, though 务 on its own is fourth tone.
column6: Tā wánchéng le jīntiān de rènwu.
column7: He finished today's task.

column3: Read háng here, "row, line" and then "trade, profession": 银行 "bank", 同行 "colleague in the same trade", 行业 "industry, trade". The common reading xíng means "to go; OK". Check the reading when you meet it in a word.
column6: Tā gàn zhè yī háng shí nián le.
column7: He has been in this line of work for ten years.

column3: Commerce, business: 商业区 "shopping district", 商业中心 "commercial center". It means the whole field of buying and selling, not a particular company. 商 "trade" + 业 "trade, industry".
column4: 这里是城市的商业中心。
column5: 這裡是城市的商業中心。
column6: Zhèlǐ shì chéngshì de shāngyè zhōngxīn.
column7: This is the city's commercial center.

column3: Goods, merchandise that are sold: 商品价格 "the price of goods". 商 "trade" + 品 "article". It treats a thing as an item for sale, so it is not used for gifts or possessions.
column6: Shāngdiàn lǐ de shāngpǐn hěn piányi.
column7: The goods in the store are very cheap.

column3: A "market", either a place (菜市场 "food market") or the economy's market in general: 市场经济 "market economy". 市 "market, city" + 场 "place". It is the word for the abstract market too.
column4: 这个市场卖水果和蔬菜。
column5: 這個市場賣水果和蔬菜。
column6: Zhège shìchǎng mài shuǐguǒ hé shūcài.
column7: This market sells fruit and vegetables.

column3: Business, trade as spoken: 做生意 "do business", 生意好 "business is good". It is about buying and selling, not a company (that is 公司). The second syllable is neutral: shēngyi.
column6: Tā zài Běijīng zuò shēngyi.
column7: He does business in Beijing.

column3: To run, manage a business: 经营餐馆 "run a restaurant", 经营不好 "poorly run". 经 "manage" + 营 "operate". The object is a business or shop, not a team of people.
column6: Tā jīngyíng yī jiā xiǎo cānguǎn.
column7: She runs a small restaurant.

column3: To open for business: 新店开业 "a new store opens", 开业大吉 "a good start to business". 开 "open" + 业 "business". It applies to the grand opening of a shop or company.
column6: Xīn shāngdiàn xià gè yuè kāiyè.
column7: The new store opens next month.

column3: To consume, spend money on goods and services: 消费者 "consumer", 消费水平 "level of spending". 消 "use up" + 费 "cost". Used for people's spending as an economic activity.
column4: 年轻人的消费越来越高。
column5: 年輕人的消費越來越高。
column6: Niánqīngrén de xiāofèi yuèláiyuè gāo.
column7: Young people spend more and more.

column3: A "transaction, deal": 网上交易 "online trade", 完成交易 "complete a deal". 交 "hand over, exchange" + 易 "exchange". Also a verb, "to trade".
column6: Wǎngshàng jiāoyì hěn fāngbiàn.
column7: Online trading is very convenient.

column3: Economy: 经济发展 "economic development", 世界经济. As an adjective it means "economical, cheap": 这样更经济. 经 here is "manage" and 济 "help, relieve", the old sense of running a state's affairs.
column6: Zhè jǐ nián jīngjì fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
column7: The economy has grown quickly in recent years.

column3: Fee, cost, or "to spend": it shows up as a suffix in 学费 "tuition", 电费 "electricity bill", 车费 "fare", 免费 "free of charge". Alone it can mean "to use up": 费时间 "waste time", 很费力 "takes much effort".
column6: Zhège yuè de diànfèi hěn gāo.
column7: This month's electricity bill is high.

column3: Expenses, costs, the total sum for something: 旅行费用 "travel costs", 费用高 "expensive". It is broader than 价格, which is a price tag; 费用 can include several things added together.
column4: 这次旅行的费用是多少？
column5: 這次旅行的費用是多少？
column6: Zhè cì lǚxíng de fèiyòng shì duōshao?
column7: How much will this trip cost?

column3: To pay: 付钱 "pay money", 付款 "make a payment", 付费 "pay a fee". Put the thing paid after it: 付房租. For paying in a shop, 付钱 is the ordinary phrase. Also see 支付 for a more formal version.
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng shǒujī fù qián.
column7: You can pay with your phone.

column3: To pay, a more formal word: 支付工资 "pay wages", 支付宝 (Alipay). The mobile payment era made 支付 a daily word: 手机支付 "mobile payment". 支 "support, pay out" + 付 "pay".
column6: Kěyǐ yòng shǒujī zhīfù.
column7: You can pay by phone.

column3: To pay a fee, for a set charge such as tuition, a phone bill or a utility: 交学费 "pay tuition", 去交费 "go and pay". 交 "hand in" + 费 "fee". For shopping, use 付钱 instead.
column6: Qǐng dào qiántái jiāofèi.
column7: Please pay at the front desk.

column3: To charge a fee: 收费停车场 "pay car park", 不收费 "free of charge". It is the side of the one receiving, while 交费 is the side of the payer. 收 "receive" + 费 "fee".
column6: Zhège tíngchēchǎng yào shōufèi.
column7: This car park charges a fee.

column3: Ticket price, for a train, movie or flight: 票价上涨 "ticket prices go up". 票 "ticket" + 价 "price". Ask 票价是多少？ to find the fare.
column6: Dìtiě piàojià shì liǎng kuài qián.
column7: The subway fare is two yuan.

column3: Rich: 富人 "rich person", 富有 "wealthy", 致富 "get rich". It can describe a family or a country, and also being full of something (see 丰富). Opposite: 穷.
column6: Tā jiā hěn fù.
column7: His family is very rich.

column3: To waste: 浪费时间 "waste time", 浪费水 "waste water". Also a noun: 这是浪费. 浪 here means "reckless" and 费 is "spend". Often used in warnings with 别 or 不要.
column6: Bié làngfèi shuǐ.
column7: Don't waste water.

column3: To save, economize: 节约用水 "save water", 节约能源 "save energy". The thing saved is a resource, not money in a bank (that is 存钱). It is a slogan word, seen on public signs.
column6: Wǒmen yào jiéyuē yòng shuǐ.
column7: We should save water.

column3: Demand, need as a noun, mainly in business and economics: 市场需求 "market demand", 满足需求 "meet the need". The verb "to need" is 需要; 需求 names the need itself. 求 is "seek".
column6: Shìchǎng xūqiú yuèláiyuè dà.
column7: Market demand is growing.

column3: To need and "need" as a noun. It can take a noun (需要帮助) or a verb (需要休息). Negative: 不需要 or 不用. It is the all-purpose word for need, a little more formal than 要 or 得. 需 means "must have".
column6: Nǐ xūyào bāngmáng ma?
column7: Do you need help?

column3: Funds, capital for a project or business: 缺少资金 "short of funds", 投入资金 "invest funds". 资 "resources" + 金 "gold, money". Not used for your own pocket money, which is 零花钱.
column6: Zhège xiàngmù quēshǎo zījīn.
column7: This project lacks funds.

column3: Value, worth: 有价值 "valuable", 价值观 "values". It covers both money value and importance. 价 "price" + 值 "worth". Said of an object, an idea or an experience.
column6: Zhè fú huà hěn yǒu jiàzhí.
column7: This painting is very valuable.

column3: To be worth: 值钱 "worth money, valuable", 不值 "not worth it". Put the price after it: 值五十块. In 值班 "be on duty" it means "to take a turn".
column6: Zhè běn shū zhí wǔshí kuài.
column7: This book is worth fifty yuan.

column3: Worth (doing): 值得看 "worth watching", 值得去 "worth going to", 值得一试 "worth a try". The next verb follows directly. Its opposite is 不值得. The second syllable is neutral: zhíde.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhíde kàn.
column7: This film is worth watching.

column3: Simple and "easy": 简单的问题 "a simple question". It can also be "plain, casual": 简单吃点东西 "have a light bite". Its opposite is 复杂 for "complicated". It is not used for "easy to get along with".
column6: Zhège wèntí hěn jiǎndān.
column7: This question is very simple.

column3: Complicated: 复杂的问题 "a complex problem", 关系复杂 "a tangled relationship". The opposite of 简单.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn fùzá.
column7: This matter is very complicated.

column3: Difficulty as a noun: 遇到困难 "run into difficulties", 克服困难 "overcome difficulties". And "difficult" as an adjective, with the second syllable neutral. In speech, 难 alone is more common for "hard". Also "hard up": 家庭困难.
column6: Tā yùdào le hěn duō kùnnan.
column7: He ran into many difficulties.

column3: The "degree of difficulty": 难度大 "very hard", 难度高, 降低难度 "make it easier". 难 "hard" + 度 "degree". Remember it is a noun, so say 难度很大, not 很难度.
column6: Zhè dào tí de nándù hěn dà.
column7: This question is very hard.

column3: To lack, to be missing: 缺钱 "short of money", 缺人 "short of staff", 缺一个 "one short". It also means "to be absent" in 缺席 and 缺课. Mostly seen in compounds in writing, but used as a verb in speech.
column6: Wǒmen hái quē yī gè rén.
column7: We are still one person short.

column3: A "shortcoming, weakness, fault": 每个人都有缺点. It is for a person, plan or thing. 缺 "lack" + 点 "point". Its opposite is 优点. Use it when you list good and bad.
column6: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu quēdiǎn.
column7: Everyone has faults.

column3: To lack, be short of: 缺少经验 "lack experience", 缺少水 "be short of water". Followed by a noun. 缺 "lack" + 少 "few". It is more formal than 缺.
column6: Zhèlǐ quēshǎo yīshēng.
column7: There is a shortage of doctors here.

column3: A "strong point, merit": 他的优点 "his strong points". It is the opposite of 缺点. 优 "excellent" + 点 "point". Use it for people, plans and products alike.
column6: Tā de yōudiǎn shì hěn xìxīn.
column7: His strength is that he is very careful.

column3: An "advantage, edge" over others: 有优势 "have an advantage", 价格优势 "price advantage". It compares with competitors, so it is less personal than 优点. 优 "excellent" + 势 "position, force".
column6: Wǒmen de jiàgé yǒu yōushì.
column7: Our prices have an advantage.

column3: A person's "strong point, strength": 发挥长处 "make use of one's strengths". The opposite of 短处. Here 长 is cháng "long", and 处 is read chù, "place, point". Usually said of ability, not of things.
column4: 每个人都有自己的长处。
column5: 每個人都有自己的長處。
column6: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de chángchù.
column7: Everyone has their own strengths.

column3: A "weakness, shortcoming" of a person: 知道自己的短处. The opposite of 长处, and the pair is often used together. 短 "short" + 处 "point". Gentler than 缺点, and used for abilities.
column4: 要看到别人的长处，也要知道自己的短处。
column5: 要看到別人的長處，也要知道自己的短處。
column6: Yào kàn dào biérén de chángchù, yě yào zhīdào zìjǐ de duǎnchù.
column7: See other people's strengths, and know your own weaknesses.

column3: Enough, sufficient: 足够的钱 "enough money", 足够了 "that's enough". It often comes after the thing and 了, or before a noun with 的. 足 "enough, full" + 够 "reach enough".
column6: Wǒmen de qián zúgòu le.
column7: We have enough money.

column3: Tight: 这双鞋太紧了 "these shoes are too tight". It also means "tense", "pressed for time" (时间很紧) and "closely" (抓紧 "grasp firmly"). The opposite of 松 "loose". Also see 紧急 "urgent".
column6: Zhè shuāng xié tài jǐn le.
column7: These shoes are too tight.

column3: Urgent, emergency: 紧急情况 "emergency", 紧急通知 "urgent notice", 紧急出口 "emergency exit". 紧 "tense" + 急 "pressing". More serious than 急, and used on signs and in announcements.
column6: Jǐnjí qíngkuàng qǐng dǎ diànhuà.
column7: In an emergency, please call.

column3: Fast, rapid: 快速发展 "develop rapidly", 快速通道 "fast lane". 快 "fast" + 速 "speed". It modifies a verb or a noun and is more formal than 快. A common adverb form is 快速地.
column6: Tā kuàisù de pǎo guòqù.
column7: He ran over quickly.

column3: Speed: 速度快 "fast", 提高速度 "increase speed", 每小时八十公里的速度 "a speed of eighty kilometers an hour". 速 "quick" + 度 "degree". Measures how fast anything moves or grows.
column6: Zhè liàng chē de sùdù hěn kuài.
column7: This car is very fast.

column3: Effective or "valid": 有效的办法 "an effective method", 有效期 "period of validity", 三天有效 "valid for three days". 有 "have" + 效 "effect". The opposite is 无效.
column6: Zhège bànfǎ hěn yǒuxiào.
column7: This method is very effective.

column3: Favorable, advantageous, usually in 对……有利 "good for": 对身体有利 "good for health". 有 "have" + 利 "benefit". Contrast 不利 "unfavorable". More formal than 有好处.
column6: Duō yùndòng duì shēntǐ yǒulì.
column7: More exercise is good for your health.

column3: Wonderful, fine, said of life, memories, wishes, a future: 美好的回忆 "fond memories", 美好的未来 "a bright future". It is rather abstract and uplifting. Not for a nice-looking person or a tasty dish.
column6: Zhù nǐ yǒu měihǎo de yī tiān.
column7: Have a wonderful day.

column3: Beautiful, a more literary word than 漂亮 and often used for scenery, a woman or a country: 美丽的风景, 美丽的姑娘. 美 "beautiful" + 丽 "pretty". It sounds poetic or formal.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měilì.
column7: The scenery here is beautiful.

column3: Image of a person or organization: 公司形象 "company image", 注意形象 "mind your appearance". It can also be an adjective, "vivid": 形象的比喻 "a vivid comparison". 形 "shape" + 象 "image".
column6: Tā zài gōngsī de xíngxiàng hěn hǎo.
column7: He has a good image in the company.

column3: Shape of an object: 圆形 "round", 形状特别 "unusual shape". 形 "form" + 状 "appearance". It describes what a thing looks like, while 形式 is about the type or manner.
column4: 这块石头的形状很特别。
column5: 這塊石頭的形狀很特別。
column6: Zhè kuài shítou de xíngzhuàng hěn tèbié.
column7: This stone has an unusual shape.

column3: Form in the sense of kind or manner: 活动的形式 "the form of an event", 以……形式 "in the form of". It contrasts with 内容 "content". Not the physical shape, which is 形状.
column6: Zuòyè de xíngshì yǒu hěn duō zhǒng.
column7: There are many forms of homework.

column3: Line, thread, wire: 一条线 "a line", 电线 "electric wire", 毛线 "yarn", 路线 "route". Also "the line" in online services: 在线 "online". The measure word is 条. 线 has the 纟 "silk" on its left because it began as thread.
column6: Zài zhè tiáo xiàn hòumiàn děng.
column7: Wait behind this line.

column3: Perfect, flawless: 完美的计划 "a perfect plan", 追求完美 "chase perfection". 完 "complete" + 美 "beautiful". It is stronger than 很好 and is often used negatively: 没有人是完美的.
column6: Méiyǒu rén shì wánměi de.
column7: Nobody is perfect.

column3: Colored, in color, as opposed to black and white: 彩色照片 "color photo", 彩色电视 "color television". 彩 is "colorful" and 色 "color". It is not the word for "colorful" in a lively sense (that is 多彩 or 五颜六色).
column6: Wǒ xiǎng dǎyìn cǎisè de zhàopiàn.
column7: I want to print the photos in color.

column3: Scenery, view: 美丽的景色 "beautiful scenery", 山上的景色 "the view from the mountain". 景 "scene" + 色 "appearance". It is a general word for what a place looks like, most often natural.
column6: Shān shang de jǐngsè hěn měi.
column7: The view from the mountain is beautiful.

column3: Brilliant, wonderful, for a performance, a match, a story or a speech: 精彩的比赛 "a great match", 精彩的表演 "a wonderful show". It means exciting to watch, not merely pretty. 精 "refined" + 彩 "brilliance".
column6: Zhè chǎng bǐsài hěn jīngcǎi.
column7: This match is brilliant.

column3: Strange, odd: 奇怪的声音 "a strange noise", 真奇怪 "how strange". It is also a verb in speech: 我很奇怪 "I'm puzzled". 奇 "unusual" + 怪 "odd, to blame". It is the everyday word for something that does not make sense.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn qíguài.
column7: This is very strange.

column3: Moving, touching or "charming": 动人的故事 "a touching story", 美丽动人 "beautifully charming". 动 "move" + 人 "people", so it moves people. A literary word used for stories, music and voices.
column4: 这是一个很动人的故事。
column5: 這是一個很動人的故事。
column6: Zhè shì yī gè hěn dòngrén de gùshi.
column7: This is a very touching story.

column3: Clear, definite: 明确的目标 "a clear goal", 态度明确 "a clear stance". It can also be a verb, "to make clear": 明确规定. It describes statements and aims that leave no doubt. 明 "bright" + 确 "sure".
column4: 他给了我一个明确的答复。
column5: 他給了我一個明確的答覆。
column6: Tā gěi le wǒ yī gè míngquè de dáfù.
column7: He gave me a clear answer.

column3: Obvious, clear to see: 明显的变化 "a noticeable change", 很明显 "it's obvious". 明 "bright" + 显 "show". It is something you can see or feel without being told, as in 明显进步了.
column6: Tā de jìnbù hěn míngxiǎn.
column7: His progress is obvious.

column3: Concrete, specific, opposite of abstract: 具体情况 "the specific situation", 请说得具体一点 "please be more specific". 具 "have" + 体 "body", something with a body you can point to. Often asked for in discussions and plans.
column6: Qǐng shuō de jùtǐ yīdiǎn.
column7: Please be a bit more specific.

column3: Objective, based on facts and not feelings: 客观的看法 "an objective view", 客观事实 "objective facts". Its opposite is 主观. 客 is "guest, outside", and 观 "view", so it means seeing from outside.
column6: Tā de kànfǎ hěn kèguān.
column7: His view is very objective.

column3: Formal, official: 正式比赛 "official match", 正式开始 "formally begin", 正式员工 "full employee". It is the opposite of 非正式 or 随便. 正 "proper" + 式 "form".
column6: Bǐsài míngtiān zhèngshì kāishǐ.
column7: The match officially begins tomorrow.

column3: Complete, whole, intact: 完整的故事 "a complete story", 保持完整 "stay intact". It means nothing is missing and nothing is broken. 完 "complete" + 整 "whole". Compare 完美, which means perfect.
column6: Zhè shì yī gè wánzhěng de gùshi.
column7: This is a complete story.

column3: Well developed, thorough as an adjective: 设施完善 "well-equipped". As a verb, "to perfect, improve": 完善制度 "improve the system". 善 "good" is the second half, so it ends up as "complete and good". Common in formal writing and reports.
column6: Zhèlǐ de shèshī hěn wánshàn.
column7: The facilities here are very complete.

column3: Neat, tidy, in order: 整整齐齐 (doubled) "neatly arranged", 排得整齐 "lined up neatly". It describes things lined up, such as books, rows of people or handwriting. 整 "whole" + 齐 "even".
column6: Shū fàng de hěn zhěngqí.
column7: The books are put neatly.

column3: Even, level and "all together, complete": 齐了 "all here", 到齐 "all arrived", 齐心 "of one mind". Often a result: 人到齐了 "everyone has arrived". It is the character in 整齐.
column6: Rén dōu dào qí le.
column7: Everyone has arrived.

column3: Prominent, outstanding as an adjective: 成绩突出 "outstanding results". As a verb, "to highlight": 突出重点 "emphasize the key points". 突 "sudden, sticking out" + 出 "out", so it sticks out.
column6: Tā de chéngjì hěn tūchū.
column7: His results are outstanding.

column3: Vivid, lively for descriptions, stories and speeches: 生动的故事 "a lively story", 讲得很生动 "told vividly". 生 "alive" + 动 "move". It praises how real something feels. Not for a person's energy.
column6: Tā jiǎng de hěn shēngdòng.
column7: She tells it very vividly.

column3: To possess, have, for qualities, in a formal register: 具有特点 "have characteristics", 具有重要意义 "be of great importance". Followed by an abstract noun, not by concrete objects such as a book or a car.
column4: 这座城市具有悠久的历史。
column5: 這座城市具有悠久的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì jùyǒu yōujiǔ de lìshǐ.
column7: This city has a long history.

column3: Have plenty of: 我们有的是时间 "we have all the time in the world". The noun follows 是. It means there is no shortage, and the tone is a little cocky. Do not confuse with 有的 "some", which is followed by a noun or 人.
column6: Wǒmen yǒudeshì shíjiān.
column7: We have plenty of time.

column3: Reasonable, sensible: 合理的价格 "a reasonable price", 合理安排 "arrange sensibly". 合 "fit" + 理 "reason", so it fits logic. It judges whether a price, a rule or an explanation makes sense.
column6: Zhège jiàgé hěn hélǐ.
column7: This price is very reasonable.

column3: Legal, lawful: 合法的工作 "legal work", 合法权利 "legal rights". 合 "fit" + 法 "law". The opposite is 非法 or 违法, "illegal".
column6: Zhèyàng zuò shì héfǎ de.
column7: It is legal to do this.

column3: Widespread, common, universal: 普遍现象 "a common phenomenon", 很普遍 "very widespread". It is about how often something happens across a group. It cannot describe a single person. 遍 here means "everywhere".
column6: Zhè zhǒng xiànxiàng hěn pǔbiàn.
column7: This phenomenon is very common.

column3: To spread widely, become universal: 手机已经普及了 "mobile phones are now everywhere", 普及教育 "make education universal". 普 "wide" + 及 "reach". Both the spreading of a thing and the effort to promote it.
column6: Shǒujī yǐjīng pǔjí le.
column7: Mobile phones are now everywhere.

column3: A "distinguishing feature, character" of a place or a dish: 地方特色 "local flavor", 有特色 "have its own character". 特 "special" + 色 "color, look". Also used as an adjective: 特色菜 "a signature dish".
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng hěn yǒu tèsè.
column7: This restaurant has a lot of character.

column3: Specially, for the purpose: 我是专门来看你的 "I came specially to see you". As an adjective, "specialized": 专门的知识 "specialist knowledge". 专 "single-minded" + 门 "branch". It tells the reason for an action.
column6: Wǒ shì zhuānmén lái kàn nǐ de.
column7: I came specially to see you.

column3: Deep: 河很深 "the river is deep". Beyond physical depth it covers "profound" (深刻), "dark" colors (深蓝 "dark blue") and "late" (深夜 "late at night"). The opposite is 浅. Also a verb-like use in 加深.
column6: Zhè tiáo hé hěn shēn.
column7: This river is very deep.

column3: Profound, deep, for impressions, understanding and lessons: 深刻的印象 "a deep impression", 深刻的教训 "a deep lesson". It is only used for abstract things, never for a river or a hole (that is 深).
column4: 这件事给我留下了深刻的印象。
column5: 這件事給我留下了深刻的印象。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì gěi wǒ liú xià le shēnkè de yìnxiàng.
column7: This left a deep impression on me.

column3: To go deep into something, or "in depth": 深入了解 "understand deeply", 深入人心 "win people's hearts". 深 "deep" + 入 "enter". Said of study, investigation and discussion.
column4: 我们要深入了解这个问题。
column5: 我們要深入了解這個問題。
column6: Wǒmen yào shēnrù liǎojiě zhège wèntí.
column7: We need to look into this problem in depth.

column3: Vast for a place, and in formal use "broad, wide" for a group of people: 广大观众 "the broad audience", 广大农村 "the vast countryside". It is a respectful way to address the public. 广 "wide" + 大 "big".
column4: 广大观众很喜欢这部电影。
column5: 廣大觀眾很喜歡這部電影。
column6: Guǎngdà guānzhòng hěn xǐhuan zhè bù diànyǐng.
column7: The wider audience really likes this movie.

column3: Read chóng here, "again, to repeat": 重新 "anew, again", 重复 "repeat", 重来 "do over". The common reading zhòng means "heavy". The chóng reading is mostly in words that start with 重. 重新 is the one to learn first.
column6: Qǐng chóngxīn kāishǐ.
column7: Please start again.

column3: Major, significant: 重大决定 "a major decision", 重大事件 "a major event". 重 "heavy, important" + 大 "big". It is for events and decisions, never for physical weight, and appears often in news.
column6: Zhè shì yī gè zhòngdà de juédìng.
column7: This is a major decision.

column3: Rich, abundant: 经验丰富 "rich in experience", 内容丰富 "rich in content", 丰富多彩 "rich and colorful". It can also be a verb: 丰富生活 "enrich life". Used for abstract things like experience, knowledge and variety.
column6: Tā de jīngyàn hěn fēngfù.
column7: He has a lot of experience.

column3: Degree, level, extent: 教育程度 "level of education", 汉语程度 "Chinese level", 在一定程度上 "to a certain extent". Measures how far something goes, or how advanced a person is in a subject.
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ chéngdù hěn gāo.
column7: His Chinese level is high.

column3: Range, scope, limits: 在……范围内 "within the scope of", 活动范围 "range of movement". 范 and 围 both suggest a boundary, and the pair names how far something extends.
column6: Qǐng zài zhège fànwéi nèi xuǎnzé.
column7: Please choose within this range.

column3: Area of a surface: 面积大 "large in area", 房间面积 "room area". 面 "surface" + 积 "amount accumulated". For a body of land, a room or a lake, never for a short line or a person.
column6: Zhège fángjiān de miànjī hěn dà.
column7: This room has a large area.

column3: Ratio, proportion: 男女比例 "the ratio of men to women", 比例大 "a large share". The ratio is said with 比: 一比二 "one to two". 比 "compare" + 例 "example, rule".
column6: Nánnǚ bǐlì shì yī bǐ yī.
column7: The ratio of men to women is one to one.

column3: Read kōng here: "empty": 空的 "empty", 空房间 "an empty room", 天空 "sky". The reading kòng means "free time; vacant", as in 有空 "to be free". Learn the two readings together with the words that use them.
column6: Píngzi shì kōng de.
column7: The bottle is empty.

column3: Condition, state of affairs: 身体状况 "physical condition", 经济状况 "financial situation". More about how something is going than 情况 which is wider. 状 "form" + 况 "situation".
column6: Tā de shēntǐ zhuàngkuàng hěn hǎo.
column7: His physical condition is very good.

column3: State, condition of a person or system: 精神状态 "state of mind", 状态不好 "not in good shape". In speech it often means how well you are doing today: 今天状态很好 "I'm in good form today".
column6: Wǒ jīntiān zhuàngtài bù hǎo.
column7: I'm not in good form today.

column3: Situation, circumstances: 现在的情况 "the present situation", 这种情况 "this kind of case", 了解情况 "find out what's going on". It is the standard word to ask what is happening: 情况怎么样？ 情 "state" + 况 "condition".
column6: Xiànzài de qíngkuàng zěnmeyàng?
column7: What is the situation now?

column3: Basic: 基本知识 "basic knowledge". As an adverb, "basically, mostly": 基本完成 "nearly done". 基 "base" + 本 "root". Before a verb it softens a statement: it is not quite complete.
column6: Zhèxiē wèntí jīběn jiějué le.
column7: These problems are basically solved.

column3: Foundation, base: 打基础 "lay the groundwork", 基础好 "a solid grounding", 汉语基础 "a basis in Chinese". Of a building or a skill. 基 "base" + 础, the stone under a pillar.
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ jīchǔ hěn hǎo.
column7: He has a good foundation in Chinese.

column3: Content: 书的内容 "the content of a book", 内容丰富 "rich in content". It is what is inside, as distinct from form (形式) or title. 内 "inside" + 容 "contain". Also asked in questions: 内容是什么？
column4: 这本书的内容很有意思。
column5: 這本書的內容很有意思。
column6: Zhè běn shū de nèiróng hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: The content of this book is very interesting.

column3: Way, manner, method: 学习方式 "way of studying", 生活方式 "lifestyle", 付款方式 "payment method". It is the manner of doing something, a little more abstract than 方法, which is a concrete method.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan zhè zhǒng xuéxí fāngshì.
column7: I like this way of learning.

column3: Relationship, connection: 关系好 "on good terms", 有关系 "be related", 没关系 "it doesn't matter". The second syllable is neutral in speech: guānxi. In China it also covers personal connections: 找关系.
column6: Wǒmen de guānxi hěn hǎo.
column7: We have a good relationship.

column3: Super, a prefix for "very, extremely": 超级市场 "supermarket", 超级大 "super big", 超级好吃 "super tasty". In speech it works like an adverb meaning "really". 超 "surpass" + 级 "level".
column4: 这是一个超级大的蛋糕。
column5: 這是一個超級大的蛋糕。
column6: Zhè shì yī gè chāojí dà de dàngāo.
column7: This is a super big cake.

column3: To talk, discuss: 谈话 "converse", 谈工作 "talk about work", 谈恋爱 "date, be in a relationship". It is more serious than 聊 and takes a topic as the object. 谈谈 (doubled) is a soft request: 我们谈谈 "let's have a talk".
column6: Wǒmen tán le hěn jiǔ.
column7: We talked for a long time.

column3: A "talk, conversation", usually a purposeful one such as with a teacher, a boss or officials: 跟老师谈话 "have a talk with the teacher". Also a verb: 他们谈话了很久. It is not for casual chat, which is 聊天.
column6: Wǒ gēn lǎoshī yǒu yī cì tánhuà.
column7: I had a talk with my teacher.

column3: To negotiate, negotiations: 和平谈判 "peace talks", 价格谈判 "price negotiation". 谈 "talk" + 判 "decide". Used for business, politics and disputes.
column6: Liǎng guó zhèngzài tánpàn.
column7: The two countries are in negotiations.

column3: Noisy: 太吵了 "too noisy", and "to disturb with noise": 别吵 "stop making noise", 吵醒 "wake with noise". It also means "to quarrel", as in 吵架. The mouth radical 口 on the left hints at sound.
column6: Wàimiàn tài chǎo le.
column7: It is too noisy outside.

column3: To quarrel, have a row: 跟朋友吵架 "quarrel with a friend". It is a verb-object word, so the person comes before it, with 跟 or 和, and not after it: not 吵架他. 架 here means "fight".
column6: Tāmen zuótiān chǎojià le.
column7: They had a quarrel yesterday.

column3: To say goodbye, take leave: 向朋友告别 "say goodbye to friends", 告别仪式 "farewell ceremony". 告 "tell" + 别 "part". It is more formal and final than 再见, used when you are leaving for a long time or for good.
column6: Tā xiàng péngyoumen gàobié.
column7: He said goodbye to his friends.

column3: To speak, make a statement at a meeting or in public: 请你先发言 "please speak first", 发言人 "spokesperson". 发 "give out" + 言 "words". Also a noun, "a speech, remarks".
column6: Qǐng nǐ xiān fāyán.
column7: Please speak first.

column3: To publish, announce, state publicly: 发表文章 "publish an article", 发表意见 "voice an opinion", 发表讲话 "give a speech". 发 "send out" + 表 "express". It is made for something that others will see or hear.
column6: Tā fābiǎo le yī piān wénzhāng.
column7: He published an article.

column3: To express thoughts or feelings: 表达感谢 "express thanks", 表达意见. Also a noun. 表 "show" + 达 "reach". Usually about putting something into words, as in 不知道怎么表达.
column6: Wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme biǎodá.
column7: I don't know how to express it.

column3: To make clear, indicate: 表明态度 "make one's attitude clear", 事实表明 "facts show". 表 "show" + 明 "clear". The subject can be a person or a fact. A bit formal.
column6: Tā biǎomíng le zìjǐ de tàidu.
column7: He made his position clear.

column3: To stress, emphasize: 强调安全 "stress safety", 再次强调 "emphasize once more". 强 "strong" + 调 "tone". The subject is a person who stresses a point, in a speech or text.
column6: Lǎoshī qiángdiào le ānquán.
column7: The teacher stressed safety.

column3: To point out a mistake, fact or problem: 指出错误 "point out an error". 指 "point" + 出 "out". The person doing the pointing speaks plainly, with the aim of correcting or informing.
column6: Lǎoshī zhǐchū le wǒ de cuòwù.
column7: The teacher pointed out my mistake.

column3: To guide, supervise, coach: 指导学生 "guide students", 在……的指导下 "under the guidance of". Also a noun: 请多指导 "please give me your guidance", a polite phrase. 指 "point" + 导 "lead".
column4: 在老师的指导下，我完成了作业。
column5: 在老師的指導下，我完成了作業。
column6: Zài lǎoshī de zhǐdǎo xià, wǒ wánchéng le zuòyè.
column7: With the teacher's guidance, I finished the homework.

column3: A "statement" or "declaration" put out publicly: 发表声明 "issue a statement", 公司声明 "a company statement". Also a verb: 他声明自己不知情. 声 "voice" + 明 "make clear". It is for official or legal positions.
column6: Gōngsī fābiǎo le yī fèn shēngmíng.
column7: The company issued a statement.

column3: To announce, declare something official: 宣布结果 "announce the result", 宣布放假 "announce a holiday". 宣 "proclaim" + 布 "declare". The speaker is an authority and the news is important.
column6: Xuéxiào xuānbù míngtiān fàngjià.
column7: The school announced a holiday tomorrow.

column3: To make public, publish officially: 公布成绩 "announce the grades", 公布名单 "publish a list". 公 "public" + 布 "announce". Used for lists, results, rules and statistics, rather than one-time news.
column6: Chéngjì míngtiān gōngbù.
column7: The grades will be published tomorrow.

column3: A "report": 写报告 "write a report", 做报告 "give a talk, present". As a verb, "to report to a superior": 向领导报告.
column6: Jīnglǐ tīng le tā de bàogào.
column7: The manager listened to his report.

column3: It is said that, supposedly: 据说那家店很好吃 "I hear that shop is delicious". It opens a clause for hearsay, with the speaker not vouching for it. 据 "according to" + 说 "say".
column6: Jùshuō nà jiā diàn hěn hǎochī.
column7: They say that shop is delicious.

column3: A "legend" and "it is said": 古老的传说 "an ancient legend", 传说中 "in legend". As a verb it means that something is passed on by word of mouth. 传 "pass on" + 说 "say". Unlike 据说, it is a story handed down, not recent hearsay.
column6: Zhè shì yī gè gǔlǎo de chuánshuō.
column7: This is an old legend.

column3: To be called, to be known as: X 被称为 Y or 称 X 为 Y. 称为 + the name. 称 "call" + 为 "as", read wéi. The name often follows in quotation marks. It is the written way to give a name or title.
column6: Mǔdan bèi chēngwéi huāzhōngzhīwáng.
column7: The peony is called the king of flowers.

column3: To ask around, inquire about news, a person or a place: 打听消息 "ask for news", 向你打听一件事 "ask you about something". 听 "hear" is neutral here. It suggests asking discreetly, not a formal question.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng dǎting yī jiàn shì.
column7: I want to ask about something.

column3: A "topic" of conversation: 换个话题 "change the subject", 热门话题 "hot topic". 话 "talk" + 题 "subject". The measure word is 个.
column6: Wǒmen huàn ge huàtí ba.
column7: Let's change the subject.

column3: To exchange, communicate: 文化交流 "cultural exchange", 经验交流 "exchange experience", 和他交流 "talk with him". 交 "exchange" + 流 "flow". It suggests mutual give-and-take, not one-way speaking.
column6: Wǒmen xūyào duō jiāoliú.
column7: We need to communicate more.

column3: To associate with, have dealings with: 和朋友交往 "be in contact with friends", 交往多年 "friends for many years". Also used for dating in some uses. 交 "meet" + 往 "go". It is about ongoing contact between people.
column4: 他不喜欢和陌生人交往。
column5: 他不喜歡和陌生人交往。
column6: Tā bù xǐhuan hé mòshēngrén jiāowǎng.
column7: He doesn't like mixing with strangers.

column3: Thought, thinking, ideas: 思想开放 "open-minded", 思想家 "thinker". It means one's way of thinking or a body of ideas, not a single idea (that is 想法). 思 and 想 both mean "think".
column6: Tā de sīxiǎng hěn kāifàng.
column7: He is very open-minded.

column3: Idea, notion, attitude: 传统观念 "traditional ideas", 时间观念 "sense of time", 观念不同 "different outlook". It is a settled way of seeing things, often shaped by upbringing.
column6: Tāmen de guānniàn bù yīyàng.
column7: Their views are different.

column3: Concept: 基本概念 "basic concept", 没有概念 "have no idea (of)". 概 "general" + 念 "thought". Used in studies and discussions about ideas, and also in 我没有时间概念 "I have no sense of time".
column6: Zhège gàiniàn hěn nán dǒng.
column7: This concept is hard to understand.

column3: Theory: 理论知识 "theoretical knowledge", 理论和实践 "theory and practice". 理 "reason" + 论 "discuss". In speech it is set against 实践 or 实际, what is done in practice.
column6: Zhège lǐlùn hěn yǒumíng.
column7: This theory is well known.

column3: Reason, grounds for an action or argument: 有理由 "have good reason", 没有理由 "no reason", 充分的理由 "a sufficient reason". It is the justification, not the cause (that is 原因).
column6: Nǐ yǒu shénme lǐyóu bù qù?
column7: What reason do you have for not going?

column3: Idea, plan, mind: 好主意 "good idea", 出主意 "offer an idea", 拿主意 "make up one's mind". The second syllable is often neutral. It is a practical plan for what to do, while 想法 is any thought.
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī gè hǎo zhǔyi.
column7: I have a good idea.

column3: To advocate and "a stand, proposal": 主张和平 "advocate peace", 他的主张 "his position". 主 "main" + 张 "put forward". The person argues for a certain course. Stronger than 建议.
column6: Tā zhǔzhāng dàjiā yīqǐ qù.
column7: He thinks everyone should go together.

column3: To suggest and "a suggestion": 我建议你…… "I suggest that you…", 提建议 "make a suggestion". 建 "set up, propose" + 议 "discuss". It is polite and the suggestion is for the listener to consider.
column6: Wǒ jiànyì nǐ zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
column7: I suggest you rest early.

column3: Meaning, significance: 有意义 "meaningful", 没有意义 "pointless", 重要意义 "great significance". It is how important something is. For the meaning of a word, 意思 is the everyday term.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn yǒu yìyì.
column7: This is very meaningful.

column3: Impression: 留下印象 "leave an impression", 第一印象 "first impression", 印象深刻 "deeply impressed". 印 "imprint" + 象 "image". A thing leaves it in the mind, so the grammar is 给我留下印象.
column6: Tā gěi wǒ de yìnxiàng hěn hǎo.
column7: He made a good impression on me.

column3: To judge, decide what is true or likely: 判断对错 "judge right and wrong". Also a noun, "judgment". 判 "separate" + 断 "cut off". It is about reaching a conclusion from evidence.
column4: 我无法判断他说的是不是真的。
column5: 我無法判斷他說的是不是真的。
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ pànduàn tā shuō de shì bu shì zhēn de.
column7: I can't judge whether what he says is true.

column3: To evaluate and "evaluation": 评价很高 "highly rated", 对他的评价 "the verdict on him". Used for reviews of films, products and people. 评 "assess" + 价 "value".
column4: 大家对这部电影评价很高。
column5: 大家對這部電影評價很高。
column6: Dàjiā duì zhè bù diànyǐng píngjià hěn gāo.
column7: Everyone rates this film highly.

column3: To criticize, scold: 批评学生 "criticize a student", 受到批评 "be criticized". A teacher or parent criticizing a young person is the typical case. It can also mean a review of art in a neutral sense: 文学批评.
column6: Lǎoshī pīpíng le tā.
column7: The teacher criticized him.

column3: To agree: 我同意 "I agree", 同意你的看法 "agree with your view". 同 "same" + 意 "opinion". It also means to consent to a request: 老板同意了 "the boss agreed". The opposite is 反对.
column6: Wǒ tóngyì nǐ de kànfǎ.
column7: I agree with your view.

column3: To oppose, object to: 反对这个计划 "oppose this plan", 我反对 "I object". 反 "against" + 对 "face". The opposite is 同意 or 赞成. The object is a plan or opinion, not a person.
column6: Wǒ fǎnduì zhège jìhuà.
column7: I oppose this plan.

column3: To deny, negate a view or result: 否定这个说法 "reject this claim", 否定回答 "a negative answer". 否 "no" + 定 "settle". It rejects an idea as wrong, often as its conclusion.
column6: Tā fǒudìng le zhège shuōfǎ.
column7: He rejected this claim.

column3: To deny a fact or charge: 否认事实 "deny the facts", 他否认说过 "he denies having said it". 否 "no" + 认 "admit", so it is "not admit". The opposite is 承认.
column4: 他否认自己说过这句话。
column5: 他否認自己說過這句話。
column6: Tā fǒurèn zìjǐ shuō guo zhè jù huà.
column7: He denies having said this.

column3: To approve, recognize something as acceptable: 得到认可 "gain approval", 认可的标准 "an approved standard". 认 "recognize" + 可 "permit". Used for plans, results and qualifications.
column4: 这个方案得到了大家的认可。
column5: 這個方案得到了大家的認可。
column6: Zhège fāng'àn dédào le dàjiā de rènkě.
column7: This plan was approved by everyone.

column3: To trust and "trust": 信任朋友 "trust a friend", 得到信任 "earn trust". 信 "believe" + 任 "rely on". A deeper trust than 相信, which is mere belief that something is true.
column6: Wǒ hěn xìnrèn tā.
column7: I trust him a lot.

column3: To understand, in the sense of grasping reasons or feelings: 理解你的心情 "understand how you feel", 难以理解 "hard to understand". 理 "reason" + 解 "untie". It is deeper than 懂.
column6: Wǒ néng lǐjiě nǐ de xīnqíng.
column7: I can understand how you feel.

column3: To observe, watching carefully over time: 观察天气 "watch the weather", 观察病人 "observe a patient". 观 "look" + 察 "examine". It is deliberate, as in science or when checking on a situation, unlike 看.
column6: Tā zài guānchá nà zhī niǎo.
column7: He is observing that bird.

column3: To follow with interest, pay attention to: 关注这件事 "follow this matter", 受到关注 "receive attention". 关 "concern" + 注 "focus". The object is usually news, a cause or a trend. Social media follows are also 关注.
column6: Dàjiā dōu hěn guānzhù zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Everyone is following this matter closely.

column3: To come to understand through experience, with feelings: 体会到 "come to feel", 深刻的体会 "a deep insight". Also a noun, "what one has learned from it". 体 "body" + 会 "understand". You need to have lived it.
column4: 我体会到了学习的乐趣。
column5: 我體會到了學習的樂趣。
column6: Wǒ tǐhuì dào le xuéxí de lèqù.
column7: I came to feel the joy of learning.

column3: To experience first-hand and "experience": 体验生活 "experience life", 旅行体验 "travel experience", 用户体验 "user experience". 体 "body" + 验 "test". It is about trying something yourself, often something new.
column4: 我想体验一下当地的生活。
column5: 我想體驗一下當地的生活。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng tǐyàn yīxià dāngdì de shēnghuó.
column7: I'd like to experience local life.

column3: To embody, reflect, show: 体现了他的善良 "shows his kindness". The subject is an action or fact, and the object a quality. 体 "body" + 现 "appear", so a quality takes shape in something.
column4: 这件事体现了他的善良。
column5: 這件事體現了他的善良。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì tǐxiàn le tā de shànliáng.
column7: This shows his kindness.

column3: To appear, look, seem, followed by an adjective: 显得很累 "look tired", 显得年轻 "look young". The subject shows a quality in some situation. The second syllable is neutral.
column6: Tā jīntiān xiǎnde hěn gāoxìng.
column7: She looks very happy today.

column3: To show, display, of a screen, a result, or data: 屏幕显示 "the screen shows", 数据显示 "the data shows". 显 "show" + 示 "indicate". The subject is a machine or a fact, not a person.
column6: Píngmù shang xiǎnshì zhe shíjiān.
column7: The screen shows the time.

column3: It looks like, seemingly: 看起来很累 "looks tired", 看起来要下雨 "it looks like rain". It is a verb phrase fixed as a single unit of opinion, put before a clause or an adjective. 起来 gives "begins to appear".
column6: Nǐ kànqǐlái hěn lèi.
column7: You look tired.

column3: Looks, seems, close to 看起来: 看上去很年轻 "looks young". 看上去 describes an impression from the outside, from sight, while 看起来 can include a guess. Both go before an adjective.
column6: Tā kànshàngqù hěn niánqīng.
column7: He looks young.

column3: Performance, behavior: 表现好 "behave well, do well", 他的表现 "his performance". As a verb, "to show, display": 表现出来. 表 "show" + 现 "appear". For students and workers, it is how they conducted themselves.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng biǎoxiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: He performed very well in the match.

column3: To face, confront: 面对困难 "face difficulties", 面对面 "face to face". 面 "face" + 对 "toward". Used for people and problems: it means not turning away from them.
column6: Wǒmen yào yǒnggǎn miànduì kùnnan.
column7: We have to face difficulties bravely.

column3: To treat someone or something, an attitude toward: 对待朋友 "treat friends", 认真对待 "take seriously". 对 "toward" + 待 "treat". Put the manner first: 好好对待, 平等对待.
column6: Yào hǎohāo duìdài péngyou.
column7: You should treat your friends well.

column3: Phenomenon: 自然现象 "natural phenomenon", 社会现象 "social phenomenon", 这种现象 "this kind of thing". 现 "appear" + 象 "image". It is what you can see or notice, not the cause behind it.
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng chángjiàn de xiànxiàng.
column7: This is a common phenomenon.

column3: The scene, on the spot: 现场直播 "live broadcast", 现场观众 "live audience", 事故现场 "the scene of the accident". 现 "present" + 场 "place". It means the place where something is happening.
column6: Jìzhě zài xiànchǎng bàodào.
column7: The reporter is reporting from the scene.

column3: Reality, realistic: 面对现实 "face reality", 现实生活 "real life", 很现实 "very down to earth, practical". The contrast is usually with dreams: 梦想和现实.
column6: Mèngxiǎng hé xiànshí bù yīyàng.
column7: Dreams and reality are not the same.

column3: To shine on, to light: 阳光照在……上 "sunlight falls on". It also means "to reflect" (照镜子 "look in the mirror"), "to photograph" (照相 "take a photo", 照片 "photo") and "to look after" (照顾). The various senses come from light falling on something.
column6: Yángguāng zhào zài chuānghu shang.
column7: Sunlight falls on the window.

column3: Reaction, response: 反应很快 "quick to react", 化学反应 "chemical reaction", 没有反应 "no response". As a verb, "to react".
column6: Tā de fǎnyìng hěn kuài.
column7: He reacts quickly.

column3: To pay attention, take note, be careful: 注意安全 "be careful", 请注意 "attention please", 引起注意 "attract attention". 注 "pour, focus" + 意 "mind". It is also used to warn: 注意！
column6: Guò mǎlù yào zhùyì ānquán.
column7: Be careful when crossing the road.

column3: To recognize someone or something after seeing it, by identifying it: 认出他 "recognize him", 一眼认出 "recognize at a glance". 认 "know" + 出 "out", the result complement. Unlike 认识, it is a single moment of recognizing.
column6: Wǒ yī yǎn jiù rènchū le tā.
column7: I recognized him at once.

column3: To recognize, know a person or a character: 我认得他 "I know him (by sight)", 认得字 "recognize characters". Mostly used in negatives and questions: 认不认得？ It is close to 认识 but fits being able to identify.
column6: Wǒ bù rènde zhège zì.
column7: I don't recognize this character.

column3: To begin, start: 开始上课 "class begins", 开始学习 "start studying". Used as a verb with another verb as its object, and as a noun: 一开始 "at first". 开 "open" + 始 "start".
column6: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiùyào kāishǐ le.
column7: The film is about to start.

column3: To launch, carry out an activity or campaign: 开展活动 "hold activities", 开展工作 "carry out work". Used for organized, large activities, not a single thing. 开 "open" + 展 "unfold".
column6: Xuéxiào kāizhǎn le hěn duō huódòng.
column7: The school has held many activities.

column3: To unfold, spread out a physical thing: 展开地图 "open a map". It can also mean "to launch or develop": 展开讨论 "start a discussion". The reverse of 开展: there the activity is the point, here it is spreading out.
column6: Tā zhǎnkāi dìtú kàn le kàn.
column7: He unfolded the map and had a look.

column3: To hold an event, such as a match, exhibition or party: 举办比赛 "hold a competition", 举办婚礼 "hold a wedding". 举 "raise" + 办 "handle". The organizers are the subject.
column6: Xuéxiào jǔbàn le yī cì bǐsài.
column7: The school held a competition.

column3: To happen, occur: 发生了什么事？ "what happened?", 发生事故 "an accident happens". The subject is the event, not a person. 发 "emit" + 生 "arise". Used for things that were not planned.
column6: Zuótiān fāshēng le shénme shì?
column7: What happened yesterday?

column3: To start an engine, "to launch" a campaign: 发动汽车 "start a car", 发动战争 "start a war". Also "to mobilize": 发动群众. 发 "send out" + 动 "move". It sets something big in motion.
column6: Tā fādòng le qìchē.
column7: He started the car.

column3: To end, finish: 会议结束了 "the meeting is over", 结束工作 "finish work". It can be used with or without an object. 结 "tie up" + 束 "bind", so it ties off. The opposite of 开始.
column6: Huìyì yǐjīng jiéshù le.
column7: The meeting has already ended.

column3: To stop, cease: 停止工作 "stop working", 雨停止了 "the rain has stopped". 停 "halt" + 止 "stop". It is formal and used for a process or activity, not for a car stopping (that is 停).
column6: Yǔ yǐjīng tíngzhǐ le.
column7: The rain has stopped.

column3: To cancel: 取消比赛 "cancel the match", 取消预订 "cancel a booking". 取 "take" + 消 "remove". Often in the passive with 被: 被取消了. A cancelled flight or plan is 取消.
column4: 因为下雨，比赛被取消了。
column5: 因為下雨，比賽被取消了。
column6: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, bǐsài bèi qǔxiāo le.
column7: The match was canceled because of rain.

column3: To lose something precious or not recoverable: 失去工作 "lose a job", 失去机会 "lose a chance", 失去朋友 "lose a friend". Unlike 丢, it is not for dropping a lost object. 失 "lose" + 去 "go".
column6: Tā shīqù le gōngzuò.
column7: He lost his job.

column3: To disappear, vanish: 消失了 "has vanished", 慢慢消失 "gradually fade away". 消 "dissolve" + 失 "lose". Used for things that fade or vanish, such as smiles, sounds and symptoms. Not a person who walks off.
column6: Tā de xiàoróng xiāoshī le.
column7: His smile disappeared.

column3: To open to the public, or "open-minded": 对公众开放 "open to the public", 开放时间 "opening hours", 思想开放 "open-minded". It also describes a country opening up: 改革开放. 开 "open" + 放 "let go".
column6: Gōngyuán duì suǒyǒu rén kāifàng.
column7: The park is open to everyone.

column3: To wait for, a formal word: 等待结果 "wait for the result". 等待 is for an ongoing wait, often a long one or one with hope. 等 "wait" + 待 "wait". In speech, 等 is the usual word.
column6: Wǒmen zài děngdài hǎo xiāoxi.
column7: We are waiting for good news.

column3: How, in what way, the formal version of 怎么样 or 怎么: 如何处理 "how to handle", 不论如何 "no matter what". 如 "like" + 何 "what". Mostly in writing and speeches.
column4: 你觉得这件事该如何处理？
column5: 你覺得這件事該如何處理？
column6: Nǐ juéde zhè jiàn shì gāi rúhé chǔlǐ?
column7: How do you think this should be handled?

column3: What for? Why? in speech: 你干吗？ "what are you doing?", 干吗这么着急？ "why the rush?". It often sounds impatient or surprised, and it is a casual word. Some also write it 干嘛. Not for written Chinese.
column6: Nǐ gànmá zhème zháojí?
column7: Why are you in such a hurry?

column3: Preliminary, initial: 初步计划 "preliminary plan", 初步结果 "first results", 初步了解 "a first understanding". 初 "first" + 步 "step". It is a first stage that is not final yet.
column6: Wǒmen yǒu le chūbù de jìhuà.
column7: We have a preliminary plan.

column3: To exist: 存在问题 "there are problems", 不存在 "does not exist". 存 "keep, remain" + 在 "be present". Often used for abstract things like problems or differences: 存在差别. It is more formal than 有.
column6: Zhège wèntí réngrán cúnzài.
column7: This problem still exists.

column3: An "incident, event", especially one that matters in news or history: 历史事件 "historical event", 安全事件 "safety incident". 事 "affair" + 件 "item". It is bigger and less pleasant than 事 and more specific than 活动.
column4: 这个事件引起了很多人的注意。
column5: 這個事件引起了很多人的注意。
column6: Zhège shìjiàn yǐnqǐ le hěn duō rén de zhùyì.
column7: This incident drew many people's attention.

column3: Change, as a noun and a verb: 变化很大 "has changed a lot", 天气变化 "weather change". 变 "change" + 化 "transform". It names the change itself, and the process of becoming different.
column6: Zhège chéngshì de biànhuà hěn dà.
column7: This city has changed a lot.

column3: To change into, turn into: 变为现实 "become reality", 水变为冰 "water turns into ice". The result follows. 为 is read wéi here. A written equivalent of 变成.
column6: Bīng biànwéi shuǐ.
column7: Ice turns into water.

column3: To change, transform in attitude or direction: 转变观念 "change one's ideas", 转变态度 "change one's attitude". 转 "turn" + 变 "change". It means a real shift from one state to another.
column6: Tā de xiǎngfǎ zhuǎnbiàn le.
column7: His way of thinking has changed.

column3: To turn into, to change, mostly as a suffix that makes verbs from nouns, like "-ize": 现代化 "modernization", 绿化 "greening", 电子化 "digitalization". As a free verb it means "to melt, dissolve": 冰化了 "the ice melted".
column6: Bīng huà chéng le shuǐ.
column7: The ice melted into water.

column3: To develop, grow: 经济发展 "economic development", 发展得很快 "developing quickly". Also transitive: 发展经济 "develop the economy". 发 "emit" + 展 "unfold". It describes growth and progress over time.
column6: Zhège chéngshì fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
column7: This city is developing very fast.

column3: Developed, advanced: 发达国家 "developed country", 交通发达 "well-developed transport". 发 "emit" + 达 "reach". Said of countries, industries and systems. For a person it is rare.
column4: 这个国家的经济很发达。
column5: 這個國家的經濟很發達。
column6: Zhège guójiā de jīngjì hěn fādá.
column7: This country's economy is highly developed.

column3: Progress in a project or work: 进展顺利 "going smoothly", 有进展 "making progress", 进展缓慢 "slow progress". 进 "advance" + 展 "unfold". It measures how far along a process is.
column6: Gōngzuò jìnzhǎn de hěn shùnlì.
column7: The work is going smoothly.

column3: To improve, progress: 进步很快 "improve quickly", 有进步 "improving". Also an adjective, "progressive". 进 "advance" + 步 "step". It is how a student or a person gets better.
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ jìnbù hěn kuài.
column7: His Chinese is improving fast.

column3: Further, a step further: 进一步了解 "understand further", 进一步发展 "develop further". 进 "advance" + 一步 "a step". It goes before a verb, to show an extra degree.
column4: 我们要进一步了解情况。
column5: 我們要進一步了解情況。
column6: Wǒmen yào jìnyībù liǎojiě qíngkuàng.
column7: We need to look further into the situation.

column3: To increase, add: 增加收入 "increase income", 人数增加 "the number rises". Transitive or intransitive. 增 "increase" + 加 "add". It is about amounts and numbers, not a physical stack.
column6: Xuésheng de rénshù zēngjiā le.
column7: The number of students has increased.

column3: To grow, rise in numbers: 经济增长 "economic growth", 增长百分之十 "grow by ten percent". Read zhǎng "grow". Used for statistics, such as output, income and population.
column4: 今年收入增长了百分之十。
column5: 今年收入增長了百分之十。
column6: Jīnnián shōurù zēngzhǎng le bǎifēnzhīshí.
column7: This year's income grew by ten percent.

column3: To speed up: 加快速度 "speed up", 加快发展 "accelerate development". 加 "add" + 快 "fast". Used for pace, work and growth, with the object being something speedable.
column6: Qǐng jiākuài sùdù.
column7: Please speed up.

column3: To rise, go up: 气温上升 "temperature rises", 价格上升 "prices go up". 上 "up" + 升 "rise". Used for amounts, levels and positions, and the opposite is 下降. The subject is what rises.
column6: Qìwēn zài shàngshēng.
column7: The temperature is rising.

column3: To rise, go up, hoist: 太阳升起来了 "the sun has risen", 升国旗 "raise the flag", 升级 "upgrade, level up", 升职 "get promoted". It is not used on its own in many sentences, usually in 升起 or in compounds.
column6: Tàiyáng shēng qǐlái le.
column7: The sun has risen.

column3: To improve a method, product or work: 改进方法 "improve the method", 有待改进 "needs improvement". 改 "change" + 进 "advance". The thing improved is something that already exists.
column6: Wǒmen yào gǎijìn gōngzuò fāngfǎ.
column7: We need to improve our working methods.

column3: To rebuild, remodel, transform: 改造旧房子 "renovate an old house", 改造城市 "remake the city". 改 "change" + 造 "build". More thorough than 修改; it implies big changes.
column6: Zhè zuò lǎo fángzi zhèngzài gǎizào.
column7: This old house is being renovated.

column3: To revise, amend a text, plan or file: 修改文章 "revise an article", 修改计划 "change the plan". 修 "fix" + 改 "change". Used for adjusting something existing, typically in writing.
column6: Qǐng xiūgǎi yīxià zhè piān wénzhāng.
column7: Please revise this article.

column3: To adjust, rearrange: 调整时间 "adjust the schedule", 调整价格 "adjust prices". 调 "tune" + 整 "put in order". It fine-tunes something that exists, to fit changed circumstances.
column6: Wǒmen tiáozhěng le jìhuà.
column7: We adjusted the plan.

column3: Read tiáo here: "to adjust, tune, blend": 调整 "adjust", 空调 "air conditioner", 调味 "season", 调皮 "naughty". The other reading, diào, means "to transfer; tune (melody)" and appears in 调查 and 声调. Choose by the compound.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shēngyīn tiáo xiǎo yīdiǎn.
column7: Please turn the sound down a little.

column3: Advanced, state-of-the-art: 先进技术 "advanced technology", 先进经验 "advanced practice". 先 "ahead" + 进 "advance". Used for technology, methods and countries, in a praising way.
column6: Zhè shì xiānjìn de jìshù.
column7: This is advanced technology.

column3: Goal, target: 学习目标 "learning goal", 达到目标 "reach the goal", 目标明确 "clear goals". 目 "eye" + 标 "mark", something you aim at. It is also the actual target of a shot.
column6: Wǒ de mùbiāo shì xué hǎo Hànyǔ.
column7: My goal is to learn Chinese well.

column3: To decide and "a decision": 我决定去 "I decided to go", 做决定 "make a decision". 决 "decide" + 定 "fix". The decision made is followed by a verb. For the process of thinking it over, use 考虑.
column6: Wǒ juédìng míngtiān qù Běijīng.
column7: I've decided to go to Beijing tomorrow.

column3: Determination, resolve: 下决心 "make up one's mind", 有决心 "be determined". 决 "decide" + 心 "heart". The phrase 下定决心 "resolve firmly" is common.
column6: Tā xiàdìng juéxīn yào jièyān.
column7: He made up his mind to quit smoking.

column3: To fight or compete for: 争第一 "compete for first place", 争论 "argue", 争吵 "quarrel". The thing fought for follows it. The character is mostly seen in compounds like 争取 and 竞争.
column6: Liǎng gè háizi zài zhēng wánjù.
column7: Two children are fighting over a toy.

column3: To strive for, try to win: 争取机会 "strive for the chance", 争取时间 "gain time". 争 "compete" + 取 "take". The goal is possible but not certain, and the speaker will work for it. Often 争取 + a verb: 争取考好.
column6: Wǒmen yào zhēngqǔ dì yī míng.
column7: We must try to win first place.

column3: To reach, attain a level, goal or standard: 达到目的 "achieve the aim", 达到标准 "meet the standard". 达 "reach" + 到 "arrive". The object is an abstract level, not a place.
column4: 他的汉语达到了很高的水平。
column5: 他的漢語達到了很高的水平。
